The Committee is constrained to note that the Finance Ministry has drastically
reduced the allocation almost by half for Residential Building Plan in BE 2015-16 in
comparison to BE 2014-15, which could adversely affect housing needs of Central
Police Forces. The Committee, in view of the above, recommends that the Ministry
should take up the matter with Finance Ministry to enhance allocation as per
requirements of CAPFs, otherwise, it would not be impossible to achieve the target set
for 2015-16. The Committee also recommends that the Government should positively
look into the demand of `12243.25 crore for the last two years of Five Year Plan for
construction of 8900 residential quarters for CAPFs along with the office and security
infrastructure. (Para 4.2.10)
The Committee observes that present level of housing satisfaction for CAPFs is
about 11.63% which is far below than the recommended level of 25% which could
further decrease in view of the proposed additional Battalions to be raised by the
Central Government. The Committee, in view of this, recommends that a high level
committee may be constituted to look into the housing needs of the CAPFs personnel
and to suggest measures required to attain optimum satisfaction level. (Para 4.2.11)
The Committee expresses its displeasure that the Ministry has not been able to
complete its target in terms of construction of residential houses for CAPFs in the year
2014-15. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that concrete steps must be
taken to meet the target without further delay. (Para 4.2.12)
The Committee notes the submission made by the Home Secretary regarding the
need of having more executing agencies for construction/maintenance of houses for
CAPFs. The Committee also feels that more agencies can help expedite construction of
houses for CAPFs and recommends that the Government should come out with concrete
decision regarding this at the earliest. (Para 4.2.13)
Depression In Capfs
The Committee is shocked to note that the number of deaths  i.e.  978 due to
suicide caused by depression, heart attack and malaria is almost triple than the
number of deaths i.e.  323 caused by Left Wing Extremist violence. The Committee
apprehends that the figure of death due to above mentioned reasons may run into
thousands, if all CAPFs and Border Guarding Forces are taken into consideration. In
view of the Committee, this is an alarming bell for the Government and the
Government should immediately take measures for attending to the grave situation on
a war footing level. (Para 4.3.5)
The Committee is sympathetic to the desperate situation of paramilitary forces
personnel. The Committee feels that the Government should look into their agonies
through which they pass while working in difficult circumstances. The Committee
understands that when the personnel of paramilitary forces pass thorough stress and

67
feel de-motivated and demoralized it would have far reaching negative repercussions.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should look into the long
pending grievances of the paramilitary personnel and address them in a time bound
manner. (Para 4.3.6)
The Committee understands that years of working in hostile conditions by
CAPFs personnel and staying away from their family, long working hours, sleep
deprivation, denial of leave, etc. take a toll on their lives. The Committee
recommends that the paramilitary forces should introduce Yoga and other stress
management techniques in the CAPFs to de-stress these personnel. The Committee
also recommends that the personnel long posted in difficult areas should be
transferred to relatively normal area after a fixed duration. Special allowances aspect
should also be examined. (Para 4.3.7)
The Committee takes a serious note of the exhaustion of reserve battalions
among forces. Reserve Components are necessary to enable the personnel to have soft
posting for some time, may be nearer to their home town area. The Government should
consider this aspect seriously. (Para 4.3.8)
Delhi Police
The Committee is constrained to note that there is major shortfall in terms of
allocation to Delhi Police in almost all major schemes, projects, etc. The Committee
understands that Delhi is capital city of the country and the law and order of Delhi
comes under the jurisdiction of Delhi Police. In the recent period, number of crimes in
Delhi has risen and threat of terrorism is looming large over Delhi. In view of the
above, allocation less than required could hamper modernization process of Delhi Police.
The Committee is of the view that the Government should look into this and enhance
allocation at RE stage as per requirements of Delhi Police in terms of completing all
schemes, projects of Delhi in a time bound and effective manner. (Para 4.4.9)
The Committee notes the submission of the Ministry that the allocation of funds
for Delhi Police in BE 2015-16 is not sufficient to meet the requirement of growing
housing needs of Delhi Police personnel and for construction of residential buildings.
The Committee recommends that the Finance Ministry should reconsider the allocation
at RE stage. The Committee is constrained to note that housing projects of Delhi Police
are moving at snail’s pace and except one no project has been completed as yet. The
Committee therefore, recommends that all housing projects should be completed without
time and cost overrun. The Committee also recommends that all procedural bottlenecks
should be cleared at the earliest for residential projects and office building projects and
necessary funds should be provided for the purpose as per requirement. (Para 4.4.16)
The Committee is dismayed to note that only `0.50 crore has been allocated in
BE 2015-16 against the projected demand of `1.00 crore for Induction of Latest
Technology in Delhi Police. The Committee recommends that the Delhi Police may be
provided adequate fund as sought by it so that the work on induction of latest
technology is not hampered due to want of fund. (Para 4.4.19)

68
The Committee is not satisfied with the reply given in the context of action
taken against erring officials not registering FIRs. The Committee believes that the
number of instances when police officials refuse or discourage to register FIR may be
bigger than what has been claimed officially. The victims out of fear do not complain
against police officials. The Committee is displeased to note that during the last two
years (2013 & 2014) out of 30 and 20 complaints, only two complaints were found to be
genuine. The Committee smells a rat here and finds that this is a clear case of conflict
of interest where police officials themselves are investigating such cases. It would be
better if complaints of non- registration of FIRs are inquired by an independent body.
The Committee is of the considered view that there is an urgent need to have an
independent body consisting of civil society groups, judiciary, etc to look into such cases
and stringent action must be taken against the officials for not registering or
discouraging people who come for registering FIRs as just seeking of explanation is not
going to serve any purpose. The Committee in this connection is also of the view that
a police station is a vital organ of the society and its responsibility and duties to the
society are of very much significance for maintaining law & order. In the absence of
police system, the society may turn into anarchy. The Committee, therefore, feels that
social audit of police system is the need of the hour and the Government may think
consider social audit of policing in the country to improve its functioning in a
transparent manner. (Para 4.4.22)
Sensitisation Towards Ethical And Moral Values
The Committee empathizes with general perception about police in the country.
The Committee is of the opinion that a person in distress only comes to police station
or contacts police personnel for help. In such a situation if police personnel at the police
station do not behave like a protector of law & order, it causes further problem to the
person in distress. The Committee recommends that a training programme of long
duration on ethical and moral values and people friendly attitude should be imparted to
police personnel especially of lower ranks. The Committee is of the opinion that the
Government should not only emphasise on the security training of police personnel but
also train them for developing good communication skills, behavior, attitude and
responsibility with the general public. The Committee is of the considered view that
Government of India should issue guidelines to all the States and Union Territories in
this regard. (Para 4.4.24)
The Committee takes note of the fact that representation of women in the Delhi
Police has been increasing and the Committee hopes that the Delhi police will soon
bring the ratio to 33%. The Committee is aware that crime against women has risen in
the capital city in the recent period. In view of this, increasing visibility of women in
uniform in the Delhi Police will boost up the morale of women of Delhi. The Committee
while noting the fact that four police stations are being headed by Women SHOs,
recommends that the Delhi Police should post more and more women as head of police
stations as women victims will find police stations headed by women officers as friendly
to visit any time and report crimes against them. (Para 4.4.29)

69
The Committee notes the submissions made by the Home Secretary and Delhi
Police Commissioner for making Delhi Police a true reflection of cosmopolitan
composition of Delhi Police. The Committee recommends that the recruitment to the
posts of constabulary should also be done by Staff Selection Commission (SSC) as has
been done in the case of post of Sub-Inspectors. The recruitment on the basis of All
India test conducted by SSC in itself is a practical solution in this regard where people
from the whole country can apply. The Committee hopes that Delhi Police would soon
have all India character and be more representative and broad based. (Para 4.4.32)
The Committee raised the issue of duty hours of Delhi police personnel and
allowances paid for extra working hours. The Commissioner of Police, Delhi replied that
officially there is fixed duty hour, however, it is not possible to follow. He added that
there is no provision of compensatory leave and extra working hours allowances to Delhi
Police personnel. The Committee understands that in view of the nature of work, it is
not practically possible to follow fixed duty hours in Delhi Police. However, the
Committee feels that the police personnel working extra hours should be given
allowances/compensation, etc to keep them motivated. Subject to the exigency of work,
there should also be provision for compensatory leave for personnel deployed during
holidays. (Para 4.4.33)
Union Territories
The Committee understands that the budget provision under the Head ‘Plan’
under Demand No. 57 is decided by the Ministry of Finance. The Committee was
apprised that the Plan component under this demand has decreased during the last two-
three years. Keeping in view that NCT of Delhi being capital city of country its
requirement is very big in terms of infrastructure and basic facilities, allocation under
the Head Plan in this demand should be enhanced at RE stage. The Committee hopes
that with enhanced allocation the Delhi Government will be able to complete its ongoing
construction of hospitals, school buildings, college, signal free corridor, Signature Bridge
and flyovers. (Para 5.1.12)
The Committee also recommends that the Union Home Ministry should take
stock of financial needs for creation for social and physical infrastructure of the UT of
Puducherry. The Committee takes serious note of the fact that due to non utilization,
the Plan component of allocation to UT of Puducherry was reduced at RE stage in
2014-15. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs should
impress upon UT of Puducherry and other UT Administrations to util ize timely the
allocations made under various Heads to overcome drastic cut at RE stage.
(Para 5.1.13)
The Committee notes that the Budget Estimates allocation under Grant 57 has
taken a downward turn from the financial year 2013-14. The Committee also takes note
of the fact that during the last five years, there is 17% decrease in Budget Estimates

70
allocation. The Committee, in view of the inflationary pressures recommends that the
Government should enhance allocation under this demand at RE stage. (Para 5.1.14)
The Committee notes that during the financial year 2014-15, allocation on all
the Demands pertaining to UTs without legislature (99 to 103) was reduced at RE
stage. The Committee also noted that in the case of UT of Lakshadweep, drastic
reduction was made at RE stage and even then the UT could spend 84.08% of what
was allocated in RE. The Committee recommends that all the UT Governments
particularly UT of Lakhswadeep, should fast pace the project implementation to avoid
cut at RE stage. (Para 5.2.3)
The Committee notes the allocation details regarding Demand No. 99 to 103
pertaining to UTs without legislature. The Committee was briefed that the allocation is
not as per requirement of the UTs. The Committee in view of this, recommends that the
Ministry of Home Affairs should take up the matter with finance Ministry for enhancing
the allocation at RE stage so that ongoing projects /schemes may not be affected.
Keeping in view, lower connectivity facility from mainland, poor infrastructure facilities
in some of the Union Territories particularly Andaman & Nicobar Islands and
Lakshadweep, a separate long term planning should be made and the Government
should consider higher allocation for lagging Union Territories. (Para 5.2.6)
The Committee is of the view that the Plan expenditure pertaining to the Union
Territories without legislature should be more and there should not be any cut in the
Plan expenditure in the proposals as there is no institutional grievance redressal
mechanism as is available with UTs with legislature. Besides, the Committee
recommends that budget Grants for UTs without legislature should be made non-lapsable
as in the case of North Eastern States where unspent balances are carried forward for
the next year. The Committee desires that similar provisions should be applied to the
Union Territories in view of their pressing needs. (Para 5.2.7)
The Committee is also of the view that the Finance Ministry should relax its
norms/rules of 30th September cutoff date for one half of the expenditure to be
made from what was allocated in Budget Estimates for revising its estimates. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry in tandem with other Ministries should
take up the matter with the Finance Ministry for changing its unscientific cut off
dated i.e. 30th September for one half of the expenditure which is allocated in
Budget Estimate. (Para 5.2.8)
Monitoring Mechanism
The Committee while deliberating upon budgetary allocations of UTs without
legislature, came to the conclusion that even after 68 years of independence, these UTs
are still underdeveloped in terms of roads, education, basic infrastructure, etc. The
Committee feels that despite pouring of large sums of money during these years,
nothing concrete has been realized on ground. The Committee was also apprised of
under utilization of funds and projects or schemes lagging behind and not completed

71
years after projected time frame. The Committee recommends that a high level
committee in the Ministry of Home Affairs consisting of public representatives should
be constituted to monitor the projects/schemes under implementation in particular and
development in general of Union Territories. (Para 5.3.2)
Connectivity
The Committee recognizes that there is severe problem of connectivity in UTs of
Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands. The Committee recommends that in the
UT of Lakshadweep, frequency of ships should be increased. Besides, high capacity
three-four more ships should be procured on priority basis. The Committee also
recommends that the Government should take up the issue of extending the length of
the runway at Agatti Airport to make it operational for modern bigger aircrafts as it
would increase tourist flow and help develop Lakshadweep. (Para 5.4.8)
The Committee takes note of the submission made by the Ministry of Home Affairs that
the fares for the Airlines operating between the mainland and Islands in the UT of
Andaman & Nicobar Islands are on higher side which is a hindrance for tourism and
also causes hardships to the Islanders who often have to go to mainland on emergencies
including medical emergency. The Committee recommends that the Government should
look into this and come out with some concrete measures to lessen fares which will help
grow tourism sector in the UT of Andaman & Nicobar Islands and will also prove helpful
for residents of Andaman & Nicobar Islands. The Committee also notes that the A&N
Administration has recently introduced chartered flight services between Port Blair and
Chennai through Air India which operates two flights in a month on every 1st and 3rd
Saturdays and islanders are being offered subsidized airfare at
`5,000/- for one way between Port Blair and Chennai. The Committee hopes that the
Union Civil Aviation Ministry will consider positively the proposal of UT Administration
to increase the frequency of flights to Chennai and also to start chartered flight
services to Kolkata by Air India and also other proposals which will go a long way in
terms of development of UT of Andaman & Nicobar Islands. (Para 5.4.9)
The Committee takes note of the fact that due to ageing fleet in the inter-island
sector in UT of Andaman & Nicobar Islands and feels that there is a need to augment
the operational availability of vessels to improve the frequency. The Committee also
takes note of the fact that the proposed passenger ships to be included in the fleet are
still at planning stage. The Committee recommends that these ships should be ordered
for supply with a deadline. The Committee also recommends that interim arrangement
of chartering ships from the open market until own ships are supplied by the
manufacturer should be done at the earliest. There should not be any delay in
chartering the ships from open market. This may be done for both Andaman & Nicobar
Islands and Lakshadweep. (Para 5.4.10)

72
Compensatory Pay To Fire Service Personnel In UT Of A&N Islands
The Committee notes the reply and recommends that an early decision on
the re-instatement of compensatory pay to the fire service personnel should be
taken. (Para 5.5.2)
India Reserve Battalion, Lakshadweep, Daman & Diu And Dadra & Nagar Haveli
The Committee reiterates its recommendation that the local recruits should be
posted within their Territory which will help improve their operational efficiency. The
Committee is of the view that the recruits from Daman & Diu could be posted in Dadra
& Nagar Haveli and  vice-versa . The Committee understands that posting away from the
family can cause unnecessary stress among personnel and reduce their mental and
physical strength which will ultimately go against the interest of the battalion which
they are supposed to serve. The Committee recommends that the Government of India
should look into this and make necessary changes in the rules regarding posting of
personnel of this battalion. (Para 5.6.4)

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One-Hundred and Eighty Sixth Report on Demands for Grants (2015-16) relating
to the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER).
2. Under Rule 272 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Council of
States, the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs is mandated
to consider the Demands for Grants of the related Ministries, and make report thereon. In
pursuance thereof, the Committee heard the presentation of the Secretary, and other officials
of the Ministry of DoNER as well as officers of the Implementing Ministries/Departments/
Agencies in its sitting held on 27th March, 2015 and examined the Demands for Grants (2015-16)
of that Ministry.
3. The Committee considered and adopted the draft Report in its sitting held on 23 nd
April, 2015
4. The Committee, while making its observations/recommendations, has relied mainly upon
the following papers received from the Ministry of DoNER: -

CHAPTER -I
OVERVIEW
1.1 Introduction
1.1.1 The North Eastern Region comprising eight States of the North East  viz . Arunachal
Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura is a region of
myriad challenges and opportunities. The development challenges for these eight States require
special attention due to following special features:-
· The seven States of the North Eastern Region barring Sikkim are linked to the
rest of India through the 26 km long Siliguri Corridor commonly known as
Chicken’s neck. They therefore form an integrated geographical unit.
· 98% of NER’s border is bounded by India’s international neighbors.
· The region offers great diversity - of topography, climatic conditions, language,
religion, ethnicity and yet has common developmental challenges.
· Most of the region is hilly and of difficult terrain.
· While Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram are overwhelmingly
tribal, the other four States also have substantial tribal population.
· Infrastructure deficit in the region, particularly connectivity in all forms is
acute.
· The economy of the region is overwhelmingly agricultural.
For the above reasons, the Department of Development of North Eastern Region was
set up in September, 2001 under the Ministry of Home Affairs and subsequently upgraded to
a Ministry in May, 2004 underscoring its complete commitment to ensure development with
equity for the NER to unleash the potential of its human and natural resources.
1.2 Mandate of  the Ministry
1.2.1 Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region or DONER, as it is commonly
known, is a unique Ministry in the Union Government as its activities are regional and more
importantly advocating the special needs of the region to the other Ministries/Departments and
policy makers.
1.3 Goals of the Ministry
1.3.1 Goals of Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region inter-alia  include the
following:-
i) Accelerating the pace of socio-economic development in the North Eastern
Region.

2
ii) Synergizing the efforts of Central/State Governments/Other Stakeholders for
balanced development of the Region.
iii) Integrated & holistic planning for the Region, taking into account the heightened
consciousness of the people of the Region, their aspirations, needs and
sensitivities.
iv) Evolving a common approach for all the agencies working for the development
of the Region.
v) Formulating appropriate policies for the rapid development of the Region.
1.4 Functions of the Ministry
1.4.1 To fulfill its role the Ministry of DoNER undertakes the following functions and
activities:
i) Matters relating to planning, execution and monitoring development schemes/
projects of the North-East Region including projects in roads, power, irrigation
and communication sectors.
ii) Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR).
iii) Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR) Scheme (State and Central).
iv)  All matters relating to the North Eastern Council (NEC).
v) Providing support and guidance to:
(a) North Eastern Development Finance Corporation (NEDFi)
(b) North Eastern Regional Agricultural Marketing Corporation (NERAMAC)
and
(c) North Eastern Handlooms & Handicrafts Development Corporation
(NEHHDC).
vi) Building capacities and competencies in critical areas.
vii) Showcasing strength and potential of the region.
1.5 Policy Framework
1.5.1 The Ministry implements work mandated in para 1.1.1 through formulations of
appropriate policies, and implementation of specific Plan programmes. North Eastern Council,
Shillong also implements various Plan Schemes in the Region.
1.5.2 All non-exempted Ministries/Departments of Government of India are required to
earmark at least 10% of Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) towards development of North
Eastern States for creation of both economic and social infrastructure. Since 1998-99, annual
unspent amount out of outlays earmarked for NE Region by non-exempted Central Ministries/
Departments is being accounted as accrual to Central Resource Pool  for Development of North

3
Eastern Region which is maintained on proforma basis by Ministry of Finance and is known
as Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources  (NLCPR). Accruals from this Pool are utilized for
financing new infrastructure projects/schemes in the Region under NLCPR Plan Scheme
implemented by Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region.
1.5.3 The Ministry also supervises work of Public Sector Enterprises, North Eastern
Handicrafts and Handlooms Development Corporation Ltd.  (NEHHDC) and North Eastern
Regional Agricultural Marketing Corporation Ltd.  (NERAMAC). The Government provides
interest free loan to the North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Ltd. (NEDFi), a
financial institution which,  inter alia  provides credit and other facilities to industrial
enterprises, infrastructure projects, agro-horticulture units etc. in the Region for promotion,
expansion and modernisation.
1.5.4 While respective Ministries/Departments are responsible in respect of subjects allocated
to them, Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region coordinates with various Ministries/
Departments of Government of India and State Governments for various development and
welfare programmes/schemes/activities in North Eastern Region.

1.7 Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources For North Eastern Region (NLCPR)
1.7.1 All the States in the NER are Special Category States, whose development plans are
centrally financed on the basis of 90% Grant and 10% Loan. Further, the Special Category
States are allowed to use up to 20% of the central assistance for Non-plan expenditure. In
October 1996, the then Prime Minister announced “New Initiatives for North Eastern Region”
and stipulated that at least 10% of the Budget( s) of the Central Ministries/Departments will
be earmarked for the development of North Eastern States. A preliminary exercise undertaken
by the Planning Commission revealed that the expenditure on the North East by some Union
Ministries during 1997-98 fell short of the stipulated 10% of the Gross Budgetary Support
(GBS) for that year. Planning Commission thereafter set up a Central Pool of Resources for
the North East out of the unspent amount of stipulated 10% of GBS to support infrastructure
development projects in the North East. Since 1998-99, all non-exempted Ministries/
Departments of Government of India are required to earmark at least 10% of their GBS for
the development of North Eastern States for creation of both economic and social
infrastructure such as power, roads and bridges, education, health, water supply and sanitation,
etc. in the region.
1.7.2 The unutilized portion of the 10% Plan allocations of the concerned Ministries/
Departments is credited at the end of each financial year in a reserve fund known as the
Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR). The funds from this Pool are used for
financing new infrastructure projects/schemes in the region to ensure speedy development of
infrastructure in the North Eastern Region by increasing the flow of budgetary financing for
such projects/schemes. Both physical and social infrastructure sectors are considered for
providing support under the Central Pool and projects in physical infrastructure sector
receive priority. For this purpose, projects are sanctioned for State as well as Central
sectors. However, the funds available under the Central Pool are not meant to supplement the
normal Plan programmes either of the State Governments or Union Ministries/Departments/
Agencies.
1.8 Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources for North Eastern Region - Central
(NLCPR-Central)
1.8.1 The Union Cabinet, on 11
th August 2011, approved for introduction, of a new Central
Sector Plan Scheme titled “Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources-Central (NLCPR-
Central)”. This plan scheme has been formulated with the objective of enhancing effective and

5
optimal utilization of funds in the NLCPR Pool towards development of the North Eastern
States. The scheme is not meant to supplement the existing schemes, but to fill critical gaps
in the existing developmental programmes or schemes. As a Central sector plan scheme,
projects of Union Ministries/Departments pertaining to subjects listed in the Union and
Concurrent Lists of Constitution of India can be proposed for funding under the scheme.
Expenditure incurred under the NLCPR-Central scheme will be debited to the NLCPR Pool. The
guidelines for the scheme have been circulated to concerned Union Ministries/Departments,
inviting them to propose appropriate projects. The Governments of North Eastern States and
North Eastern Council have also been informed about the procedure by which they may
propose projects under the scheme.

2.3 North Eastern Council
2.3.1 North Eastern Council (NEC) was set up under NEC Act 1971, far securing
balanced development of North Eastern Area with seven constituent members viz . Arunachal
Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura. Through an
amendment of NEC Act in 2002, Sikkim was added as eighth member. By virtue of
Amendment, Council has been made regional planning body for North Eastern Area. It
functions as a regional planning body for its constituent States. It is also mandated to
maintain security and public order. The Council plays an advisory role in areas of interest
that are common to all its constituent States such as economic and social planning,
transport, communications, power and flood control. Besides ensuring effective
coordination, it is also mandated to put forward proposals for developmental schemes and
projects submitted by the States to the Centre.

15
2.3.2 NEC funds Inter-State and State-specific roads in the region. So far, it has funded
construction of more than 10,000 km of road in the region. Apart from roads in the region,
77 temporary bridges have been converted to permanent bridges in the region. Also 3
ISTTs and 9 ISBTs have been constructed. The NEC has undertaken development of
airports in the region and 12 airports are being upgraded regularly under its funding of
60:40 ratio with the Airports Authority of India (AAI). Apart from putting in its own funds
into the improvement of the infrastructure in the region, the NEC has also been
instrumental in providing necessary inputs to the line ministries i.e.  Ministry of Road
Transport & Highways, Railways, Inland Waterways and Ministry of Civil Aviation on
projects undertaken by them from time to time. Although, the resources with the NEC are
limited but it monitors the projects being executed by Central Ministries. The Rural
Development Ministry is doing the PMGSY programme for linking villages upto 250
population. The development of the Barak River as National Waterway No.6 will usher in
long term development in the Cachar Valley of Assam.

2.3.7 The Ministry also submitted that the strategy to eliminate/ overcome these barriers
may include increase in allocation of funds for enabling completion of projects, especially,
in view of the low annual plan allocations i.e. , R770 crore, R700 crore and R579 crore
at RE stages during 2012-13, 2013-14 and 2014-15 respectively which shows a decreasing
availability of plan funds. Also, the share of ongoing projects has been
61.71 %, 80.41 % and 88% during the 2012--13, 2013-14 and 2014-15 respectively which
shows an increasing trend.
2.3.8 The Committee notes with serious concern the trend of decreasing allocation of
funds to North Eastern Council. The substantial cut in allocation at RE stages in
consecutive years may be a result of non-submission/ late submission of Utilization
Certificate by State Governments who in turn are unable to do so due to severe weather
and heavy monsoon that lead to stoppage of work in various projects. The Committee
also note that the assessment period for determining budgetary allocation at RE stage,

17
coincides with the immediate aftermath of the longer monsoon season in North East
Region. In view of the Committee, this period of assessment is not realistic as not only
NE Region but also whole country except few pockets witness monsoon rains; thus
causing disruption in construction activities. The Committee recommends that the
Ministry of Finance should take a realistic and practical approach to the important issue
of deciding supplementary allocations and revised allocations and adopt a liberal
approach or may desist from making any substantial cut while allocating funds at RE
stage for schemes and projects particularly of North East Region. Alternatively, the
Ministry of DoNER may in consultation with North East States, NITI Aayog and Ministry
of Finance may explore a different mechanism like considering a different time period
for Northeast region having normal weather for assessment of utilization of funds and
consequent increase/decrease in allocation at RE stage.
2.3.9 The Committee is dismayed with the tentative division of allocated funds in
different sectors by NEC and is unhappy to see very low allocation being made to
critically and potentially important sectors like health, industries and tourism. The
Committee strongly feels that while it is important to give higher allocation to critical
sectors like transport and communication, HRD etc., socially and economically
important sectors cannot be afforded to be neglected. The Committee Therefore,
recommends that NEC and Ministry of DoNER should revisit the appropriation of
allocation to different sectors and evolve a more equitable and comprehensive method
of sectoral division of funds so that important sector gets neglected and a wholesome
development is achieved.
2.3.10 The Committee is disappointed with the issue of non-release of funds by State
Governments to implementing agencies becoming a major bottleneck in project
implementation and optimal fund utilization. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the State Governments must ensure timely release of funds to implementing
agencies for completion of projects without time and cost overruns. The Committee
further recommends that the monitoring mechanism must also be further strengthened
by including strict penal provisions for delay/non release of funds on one hand and also
giving incentives to those States who comply with timelines and guidelines in the
completion of projects.

2.6.1 NERAMAC was set up to support farmers/producers of North Eastern Region of the
country in getting remunerative prices for their produce and thereby bridge the gap between
the farmers and the market and also to enhance the infrastructure for procurement, processing
and marketing of agro-horticultural produce like ginger, orange, pineapple, kiwi, turmeric, large
cardamom, hill grass and bay leaves of the .North Eastern Region of India. The Corporation
is also engaged in setting up of Model Nursery, Model Floriculture Centre, Net House & Poly
House, and High Tech Green House etc. thereby helping in development of horticultural
activities in the North Eastern Region. To fulfill its prime objectives, NERAMAC is offering
helping hand to farmers by intervening in the market and provide them remunerative prices. It
also helps processing units by providing raw materials and arranging packaging materials.
NERAMAC has a few retail outlets within the North East region which directly sell various
processed and value added products produced locally in the region.
2.6.2 The Committee sought to know about the steps taken by NERAMAC in the recent years
for encouraging food processing units and creating world class marketing infrastructure in
NER. The Ministry informed that NERAMAC during the last two years organized six awareness
programs on food processing for the development of food processing in the State of Assam
with the financial support of NMFP. In order to create a world class infrastructure for
marketing agricultural and allied goods, NERAMAC organized a study through M/S. Omeo
Kumar Das Institute of Social Change & Development (OKDISCD) to set up Collection &
Procurement Centre with cold chain facilities for end marketing the produces & products of
North East to support the farmers. Further, to create infrastructure for processing, value
addition & marketing, NERAMAC is setting up a Cashew Processing Plant at Mankachar,
Assam under NLCPR funding through Ministry of DoNER. It also has three more food
processing projects in the pipeline for setting up of a Multi-fruit Processing Plant at Silchar
& a Quality Assurance & Central Packaging Centre at Chaygaon, Assam. Moreover, NERAMAC
has facilitated a manual Large Cardamom Auction Centre in the State of Sikkim from
FY 20 10 -11 to support the large cardamom producers there. This has given a great help to
the large cardamom growers in fetching better price. It also has a proposal for creation of
e-auction facility for large cardamom with the support of Ministry of Commerce & Industries,
Govt. of India.
2.6.3 On enquiring as to why there was a cut of nearly 50% to the tune of Rs.1 crore at
RE stage in 2014-15, the Ministry replied that it was done with a view to curtail total revenue
and total Expenditure of NERAMAC for controlling the trend of incremental financial losses.
There was an increasing burden of accumulated Working Capital loan (from Ministry of
DoNER) with release of each additional spell. Moreover, the working capital loan carries a high

21
interest rate (latest 13.5%) with a penal interest (16%) which is very high. Also, the financial
burden is going up on account of increasing burden of accrued interest on borrowings
including Working Capital loan. Thus, the Ministry deemed that it may not be financially
prudent to increase Budgetary allocation to NERAMAC in the form of Working Capital loan,
till the net worth of this PSE is methodically assessed, to avoid inefficient use of public funds
and also a vicious debt trap for NERAMAC to occur in future.
2.6.4 The Committee is not convinced with the contention of the Ministry that the cut
of nearly 50 percent at RE stage was done with a view to curtail the trend of
incremental financial losses especially in view of the increased demand and allocation in
BE 2015-16. In view of the Committee this trend was being followed since many years
and all of a sudden, this plea is being advanced. However, the Committee feels that the
working capital loan being given to NERAMAC carries unduly high interest and penal
interest rates. Therefore, the Committee recommends that either the Ministry should
facilitate NERAMAC and enable it to access cheaper funds from the market or the
Ministry must provide loans to it at relaxed rates of interest and favorable terms and
conditions. The Committee desires that the revival plan of the Corporation should be
expedited. It is very strange that entities in private sector in the same field are
flourishing while entity in Government sector is making continuous losses since many
years even to the such level that its working capital has wiped out.
2.6.5 The Committee desired to know as to why a desired level of intensification and
expansion of activities of NERAMAC has not taken place and also sought to know about the
Corporation’s future plans of expansion. The Ministry replied that NERAMAC has not ventured
into intensive marketing activities or expanded its activities in a desired manner due to lack of
adequate working capital from its inception. NERAMAC was set up to support farmers/
producers of North Eastern Region of the country in getting remunerative prices for their
produce and thereby bridge the gap between the farmers and the market and also to enhance
the infrastructure for procurement, processing and marketing of agro-horticultural produce of
the North Eastern Region of India. To fulfill its prime objectives, NERAMAC is offering helping
hand to farmers by intervening in the market and provide them remunerative prices. It also
helps processing units by providing raw materials and arranging packaging materials.
NERAMAC has a few retail outlets within the North East Region which directly sell various
processed and value added products produced locally in the region. The Ministry submitted a
perspective plan of the Corporation that primarily focused upon expanding activities in the
following sectors:
····· Processing: To harness the potentiality of cashew cultivation of the West Garo
Hills District of Meghalaya and adjoining districts of Assam, NERAMAC is
setting up a Cashew Processing Unit at Mankachar, Assam of 4 MT per day
capacity. The civil works have already been completed & erection of plant and
machinery is under process. The trial production is rescheduled in the next
cashew season and the commercial production is planned subsequently.
····· Marketing: NERAMAC has set up an Auction Centre for Large Cardamom at
Rongpoh in Sikkim. However, this auction centre needs to be upgraded as
e-auction centre with a view to make it attractive and large scale participation

22
for the convenience of auctioneers. It is proposed to set up this facility at
Singtam in Sikkim. Similarly, North Eastern region produces huge quantity of
ginger and at present there is no organized marketing yards and the farmers are
mainly depending on middlemen to market their produce. NERAMAC proposes
to set up an e-auction centre for the benefit of both farmers and buyers at
Byrnihat in Meghalaya or other ginger growing areas.
····· Develop FSSAI Registered Processing Units: NERAMAC is providing a
platform to market processed products produced by the FSSAI registered
processing units of North East. However, it is seen that a number of units are
defunct and the capacity of many units is under-utilized due to various factors
such as obsolete machinery, lack of skilled technical hands, lack of quality, poor
packaging, lack of financial assistance and many other factors. There are a
number of FSSAI Registered Food Processing Units in the North Eastern
Region. As value addition is essential to reduce post-harvest losses and increase
farm gate price, it is essential to strengthen these units.
····· Cluster Development:  It is noticed that the farmers of the region are not
organized and the production of farm produce is sporadic resulting that from a
single location one trader or entrepreneur may not be able to collect economic
quantity of any single produce either for trading or for processing. The
production being sporadic, the collection charges are also very high. This also
denies the farmers of the power of bargain, resulting in less realization of the
price for their produce. Therefore there is an urgent need to organize the
farmers by forming clusters. NERAMAC plans to form at least ten clusters each
of pineapple, orange, ginger, turmeric farmers in the identified locations in each
North Eastern State.
····· Development of Human Resources:  NERAMAC plans to impart training to its
employees to manage the e-auction centers, marketing of fresh fruits, vegetables
and processed food products, post-harvest Management and in incense stick
making.
····· Implementation of NMFP in North Eastern States:  Ministry of Food
Processing Industries has appointed NERAMAC as Project Monitoring
Agency (PMA) for implementing the Schemes in North Eastern States such
that it provides management, capacity building, coordination & monitoring
support. NERAMAC assists Ministry in implementation of the NMFP and
coordination with the North Eastern States/State Industry Associations. It
prepares & submits to Ministry state-wise monthly financial & physical
progress report of the project, inspects the assisted units & guides the State
Governments in implementing the Schemes. NERAMAC also organizes State
wise conferences once in a year. On the other hand NERAMAC assists the
entrepreneurs in getting the assistance from financial institutions and
coordinates with them in appraisal of their projects & getting approval of
term loan for the same.

23
2.6.6 The Committee feels that the Corporation’s efforts are focused in the right
direction but the pace needs to be hastened. The Committee recommends that the
proposed e-auction centers must be established at the earliest to ensure better and
timely returns for the producers. Also, the Ministry must ensure that such e-auction
centers must be spread throughout the region and a centralized e-auction system may
be devised to ensure a wider market for the growers.
2.6.7 Food processing units are necessary for value addition to agricultural produce;
prevent post-harvest losses and providing better remuneration to farmers. The
Committee is perturbed to note that various processing units are lying defunct and
suffering from various ailments. The Committee recommends that NERAMAC should
guide its efforts to revive these processing units by providing assistance for better
equipments, technical know-how and affordable finance.

2.8.8 North East India is a region which has been starved of development primarily due
to lack of critical infrastructure. The Committee has time and again stressed on
increasing pace of infrastructure creation in the Region. The latest status of
infrastructure projects submitted by the Ministry of DoNER has left the Committee
disappointed. A huge number of projects, more than one-third of the total numbers of
projects, worth R6177.54 crores are found to be delayed. Even among the delayed
projects more than a third have been delayed by more than four years. Such a lengthy
delay, whatever the reasons may be, is incomprehensible and unacceptable. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry must urgently fast track the delayed projects
on priority basis by resolving the pertinent issues and submit a status report of action
taken for expediting such projects to this Committee. The Committee also recommends
that the work for Greenfield airport at Holongi near Itanagar must also be started at
the earliest so that it could be completed in time.
2.8.9 The Committee also takes note of the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
of India (CAG) on the performance audit of roads and bridges projects funded by Non-
Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR) and the North-Eastern Council (NEC) in Audit
Report of Arunachal Pradesh for the year ended 31 March 2013. It reflects the financial
mismanagement as well as losses due to ill planning, lack of internal audit and inability of

30
the Departments to come up with utilization certificates. Some major audit findings are
highlighted below:
· There were delays ranging from 7 to 13 months in submission of Priority Lists.
· Records of 25 test-checked NLCPR projects revealed that Detailed Project
Reports were prepared without proper survey and investigation.
· There were delays ranging from 3 to 48 months in release of funds by the State
Government to executing agencies.
· The State Government did not contribute its share aggregating to Rs. 12.15
crore (48.41 percent) towards implementation of 25 test-checked NLCPR
projects.
· Against the total amount of Rs. 403.15 released up to 2012-13 for
implementation of NLCPR, utilization certificates (UCs) for Rs. 111.50 crare (30
per cent) were pending as of March 2013.
· In 22 test-checked projects, executing agencies incurred inadmissible
expenditure of Rs.10.16 crore against NLCPR funds.
· In three projects, executing agencies diverted Rs. 5.26 crore from NLCPR/NEC
funds to other projects.
· The completion rate of projects under NLCPR/NEC was far from satisfactory.
Out of 49 projects due for completion by March 2013 or earlier, only 11
projects (23 percent), involving an expenditure of Rs. 105.44 crore, were
completed. Even completed projects had huge time overruns ranging from 12 to
24 months.
· No Evaluation Study was conducted to assess the impact of projects created.
· Adequate transparency and publicity/dissemination of information relating to
NLCPR/NEC projects was not ensured through the Local media and Display
Boards.
2.8.10 The Committee has a similar feeling that such audit objections in the CAG
reports of performance audits of may also be there in respect of some other NE States.
The Committee notes the inconsistency between the Ministry’s submission and the
existing NLCPR Guidelines. Moreover, the States must not be allowed to withhold funds
beyond reasonable period of time. The Committee recommends that the Ministry must
effect suitable amendments to incorporate strict penal provisions in the NLCPR
Guidelines if the States withhold release of funds for a time greater than a maximum
acceptable limit. If the States fail to release funds for more than three months then the
funds may be reverted back to the Ministry of DONER and NEC and the payment may
be made directly to the executing agencies bypassing the States altogether in case of the
project where funds are not timely released by the States. The Committee feels that
such a strong measure is necessary to prevent huge delays in projects due to non-
release of funds by the States. Accordingly the ministry must apprise the Committee at
the earliest on the action taken on this recommendation.

the Central fund meant for BTC package used to be lying with the State Government
of Assam. The Committee took a serious view of this and felt that in federal set up like
India when the Central Government sanctions the fund, the State Government has no
business to retain the fund for a longer period The Committee at that time desired that
the Central Government may review the entire package and take up the matter with the
State Government to ensure that such thing does not recur in future. In case the State
Government does not release the fund for the purpose for which they are sanctioned,
future release of the fund to the State Government may be held up until the State
Government takes necessary action. Responding to the observations of the Committee,
the Ministry of DoNER informed that Government of Assam was apprised of the serious
concern of the Parliamentary Standing Committee regarding delay in transfer of funds

of BTC and requested to devise a mechanism so as to assure uninterrupted flow of funds

of Assam along with details of release made by the Government of Assam during the
last two years.
2.10.6 The Committee also notes that one project is yet to be completed from among
the 42 sanctioned projects under the package sanctioned in 2003. Non completion of all
the projects in a long time span of 12 yeas does not present a good picture. Likewise
under the Additional BTC Package of Rs. 250 crore, which was announced in August,
2008, only 2 projects out of 21 projects have been completed. In view of the Committee
this is a very sorry state of affairs. The Committee therefore strongly recommends that
all the projects must be completed in this fiscal year. The Ministry must also ensure
that the sanctioned projects do not suffer for want of funds and must ensure timely
release of funds to complete all the projects at the earliest.

gradation of existing airports in NER. The Committee is concerned with the low
budgetary allocation which is less than half of the projected demand. Moreover, the huge
outstanding liabilities of more than R80.00 crore will further affect the implementation
of projects. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the Ministry must urgently
pursue this matter with the Ministry of Finance and seek supplementary Grants for
meeting the outstanding liabilities as well as the existing project requirements.

th F. Y .P .Construction of hangars at Guwahati and extension of apron at

th Five Year Plan. Hanger facilities

at Imphal, Dibrugarh and Itanagar are yet to be provided; DPRs are ready and the

incidental facilities in the NE Region.
2.15 NER Livelihood Project ( NERLP) - Eap
2.15.1 North East Rural Livelihood Project (NERLP) is a multi-State central sector
externally aided project funded by World Bank which has become effective from March
2012. It covers four States of Mizoram, Sikkim, Tripura and Nagaland. It has four
components namely Social Empowerment, Economic Empowerment, Partnerships
Development and Management and Project Management, to be implemented in two districts
each of the four NE States.
2.15.2 The objective of the project is to improve rural livelihoods, especially that of women,
unemployed youth and the most disadvantaged in the four project states. The key outcomes
to be achieved through its various project activities are:
(i) Creating sustainable Community Based Organisations (CBOs)- women Self-Help
Groups (SHGs), SHG Federations, Community Development Groups (CDGs),
and Producer Organizations (POs);
(ii) Building capacity of the CBOs for self-governance, bottom up development
planning and democratic functioning with transparency and accountability;
Creating livelihood opportunities by managing natural resources, developing
employable skills of youths, providing complete value chain, providing bank
linkage and creating critical infrastructures;
(iii) Developing technical partnerships for community institutions.
2.15.3 The Ministry apprised the Committee with the review of past performance of the
Scheme which is as under:
(i) In the first year of 2012-13, the performance was slow with an expenditure of
R2.7l crore only. The project could cover 47 project villages, completed 18
village Entry Point Activities (EPAs) and identify 32 Community Service
Providers (CSPs). The two DPMUs in Tripura were made functional by
recruiting all the vacant positions and recruitments for all the vacant posts in

40
other DPMUs were completed. Out of 58 original project blocks, PFTs were
provided in 46 blocks.
(ii) During 2013-14, number of Village awareness programs increased to 935. A
total of 4414 Self Help Groups (SHGs) were formed including 2636 newly
formed and 1778 co-opted. A total of 505 Community Development Groups
(CDGs) were formed to look after overall development of the villages. R5.17
crore was transferred to the Community Based Organizations (CBOs) such as
SHGs and CDGs in the form of Seed fund (1607 nos.) towards corpus building,
Livelihood funds (474 nos.) to carry out various livelihood activities and
Community Development Fund (12 nos.) for implementing CDPs. The project
has engaged 760 CSPs, capacity building trainings for CBO Leaders and
completion of all major procurement of goods and services of the project. Skill
trainings for unemployed youths also started. Expenditure of the project
increased to R25.45 crore in 2013-14.
(iv) Despite glitches in financial transactions, social mobilization and institution
building was focused and by end of December 2014, as many as 7171
SHGs,720 CDGs and 92 SHG Federations were formed. Actions are also
initiated for taking up at least 5 livelihood clusters during the financial year
2014-15. The project has also partnered with The Energy and Resources
institute (TERI) and Kabil to provide technical and implementation support
Community Development Plans, Innovative Change Collaboration India (ICCo-
lndia) was engaged for value chain development to develop complete business
on selected product.

Operationally, NERLP and NRLM in those four participating States are made mutually
exclusive in districts where NERLP is operating. However, for better coordination and
convergence, Secretaries of the State Rural Departments who are looking after SRLM/NRLP
are also made Nodal Officers for NERLP. There are also District Project Advisory
Committees headed by Deputy Commissioners/Collectors to review the project at the district
level and advise necessary program convergence. NERLP stays engaged with other livelihood
projects for resources from institutions like Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP),
Andhra Pradesh, Pudhu Vaazhvu, Tamil Nadu, JEEVIKA, Bihar, MPDPIP, Madhya Pradesh,
Myrada Spoorthy Training Centre, Kamataka and NERCORMP in sharing their rich
experiences. To promote holistic development, convergence is being undertaken. For
example, in South Sikkim district, NERLP is promoting Dairy Cluster and construction of
cow sheds is being taken up under MGNREGA. D/o Animal Husbandry, Govt. of Sikkim has
been engaged as technical partner to train and guide village level para-vets for serving the
project villages. Similarly, technical trainings on livelihood (Agro/Horti, AH and Mushroom)
to community are being regularly conducted by KVKs, RSETi, ICAR. In West Tripura,
promotion of mushroom cultivation is being taken in association with D/o Horticulture. In
Tripura, Fishery development is taken up in joint collaboration with D/o Fisheries and
National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), North east centre. An important component
of NERLP is ‘Community Development Plan (CDP)’ which facilitates planning and
implementation of holistic village development. State line Departments are involved in the
process of CDP preparation for convergence and synergy with different programs such as
MGNREGA, IWMP etc.
2.15.7 The Committee notes the close coordination and strong linkages between
NERLP and other livelihood schemes in rural areas of NER. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry should keep up this scheme and try to expand it further
to create self-sustainable institutions and ensure ample livelihood opportunities for the
rural poor.

CHAPTER-III
ISSUES. SCHEMES. POLICIES AND PROGRAMMES
3.1 Withholding Or Diversion Of Funds By The State Governments
3.1.1 W ith regard to withholding or diversion of funds by the State Governments of North
Eastern Region for projects in the North East States, the Ministry informed that instances of
withholding of funds by States do happen and NEC informs the States from time to time to
release timely the funds sanctioned for the purpose. However, it confessed that NEC does not
have the information regarding diversion of funds. The Ministry also submitted that no penal
provisions were invoked as such a mechanism is not in place.
3.1.2 However, the Committee notes that in the Guidelines for Administration of
Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources, it is stated that:
· Funds released from the Pool must be transmitted to the implementing agency/
project authority (such as PWD, Housing Corporation, State Electricity Board,
etc.) by the State Government within 15 days from the date of release of
funds from Government of India and a certificate to this effect be sent to
Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region by the State Planning
Department. (Para 8.3).
· Funds released by the Government of India must be utilized within a period
of 12 months from the date of release. In case the funds are not utilized
within the stipulated time, such cases may be referred to the Ministry of
Development of North Eastern Region with sound reasoning for revalidation.
Revalidation for a limited period may be granted by Secretary of Ministry of
DONER on merit. (Para 8.4).
3.1.3 The Committee also notes that the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
vide its report on the performance audit of roads and bridges projects funded by Non-
Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR) and the North-Eastern Council (NEC) in Audit
Report of Arunachal Pradesh for the year ended 31 March 2013 pointed out that in three
projects, executing agencies diverted Rs.5.26 Crore from NLCPR/NEC funds to other
projects.
3.1.4 The Committee wonders why the Ministry and NEC are in the dark regarding fund
diversion instances when it has been explicitly highlighted by the supreme audit institution of
India, CAG, in its report. The Committee is unable to understand such a disconnection between
the NEC and the ground reality. The Committee feels that the Ministry of DoNER and NEC
must adopt a vigilant role to ensure intended utilization of funds for the designated purpose.
The Committee strongly recommends that continuous scrutiny of fund disbursal must be done
to ensure that no funds are diverted or leaked. Also the Ministry and NEC must urgently look

into all the instances of fund diversion, inadmissible expenditure incurred under NLCPR head
and other such anomalies related to financial mismanagement and take strict action against the

dissemination in an attractive, convincing and focused manner is necessary to attract
potential tourists. In this regard, the Committee finds that the efforts of Ministry and
Tourism Departments of State Government are not up to the mark. The Committee
feels that, to publicize the tourism potential, it is not only necessary to inform and
sensitise the general public but also it is required to take in the loop the services of
major tour operators and agencies in a focused manner because ultimately it is they who
prepare tourist routes and design packages for the tourists. There is a necessity to
establish strong linkages of long term nature with the tour operators and provide them
necessary information and facilities for promoting NE tourist routes.
3.2.6 The committee is disappointed by the official tourism websites of the various NE
States. It feels that the Government needs to ramp up the various official tourism
websites of various NE States. It is probably the first point of information and
sometimes the most definitive one for a potential tourist from outside North East. The
Committee observes that except one or two, most of the official tourism website of NE
States are lacking on various technical parameters like user friendliness, ability of
being one-stop portal of all information, multi-lingual content, optimization in mobile
and tablet computer formats, online payment portals, various set tour packages and
inter linkage between different websites and service providers. Therefore, the
Committee recommends that the Ministry must ensure that the official tourism
websites of different States incorporate these critical features. That is so because to
attract tourists from regions like west and south India and also from other countries,
the content and information has to be multi-lingual. The Committee observes that
most of the websites are not multi-lingual and even in case there is multi-lingual
option available (like Arunachal Pradesh) the approach is poor and not effective. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that professional translators may be hired to
create a vibrant and comprehensive multi-lingual content for the official tourism
websites.
3.2.7 The Committee feels that development of tourism requires NER specific as well
as integrated outlook. While a NE circuit train is still not possible due to lack of decent
rail connectivity in the region, however, the efforts for the conceptualization and
planning for the same must be started right away. The Committee recommends that a
special circuit train by the name of ‘North-East Seven Sisters Circuit’ or other such

54
name be conceptualized and planning for the same may be started so as to reap the
benefits as soon as the capitals of all the NE states are connected by the railway
network.
3.2.8 The Committee is surprised at the exclusion of important Buddhist cities of NER
from the Buddhist Circuit. It feels that including sites like Rumtek, Kalimpong in
Sikkim and Tawang, Bomdila in Arunachal Pradesh can help increase tourism prospects
in these regions. The Committee recommends that the Ministry must identify specially
focused projects to develop these sites and augment their capacity to attract as well as
sustain  increased tourist inflow. The Ministry must also explore a way to include them
in the Buddhist tourist circuit.

been cancelled nor withdrawn. The allocation for the Schemes under NEIIPP
has been fully utilized and liability has been incurred in excess of annual
allocations.
(c) A third party assessment/evaluation for the Schemes under NEIIPP, 2007 was
conducted in the year 2010 by North Eastern Development Finance Corporation
Ltd. (NEDFi) through an independent agency viz. M/s. Mott MacDonald Ltd.

DoNER.
(d) Further, a third party evaluation Study of Industrial Package of Incentives under
North East Industrial Investment Promotion Policy (NEIIPP), 2007 for the
States of NER (including Sikkim) was undertaken by Centre for Market
Research & Social Development (CFMRSD) on behest of this Department.
CFMRSD has submitted its draft evaluation report which is under consideration
of this Department and has not yet been finalized. Final evaluation report will

3.3.2 NEIIPP is an important policy that led to a minor beginning of industrial
development in North East. The Committee notes that it provides various subsidies and
exemptions to promote investment and industrial development in NER. A proper
accountability mechanism should have ensured a regular cost-benefit analysis and
impact assessment of the policy every year. However, after 2010 no such evaluation was
done till 2014. The Committee recommends that evaluation study of NEIIPP must be
done every two years and the Ministry must apprise the Committee of the results
regularly.
3.3.3 The Committee takes exception to the fact that even before the ongoing third
party evaluation study is completed and its report made public, the Government has
decided to suspend fresh registrations under this policy which can have serious
consequences to the progressive trend of growing investment in the region. Apparently,
‘Make in North East’ which could have been realized by this policy, has been subjected
to budgetary constraints. The Committee recommends that the Ministry must pursue the
Department of industrial Policy and Promotion to restore the benefits under the NEIIPP.
Evaluation study should be examined and decision taken at the earliest.

3.6 Extinction of Many Tribal Languages of North East Region
3.6.1 The Committee was concerned about the issue of extinction of many tribal languages
of North East Region especially in Arunachal Pradesh. Therefore it wanted to know the steps
being taken to address this issue in particular and preservation of tribal cultures in general. The
Ministry informed that the issue of preservation of tribal culture is being addressed under the
Research Scheme of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs under which Grant-in-Aid is provided to
Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) situated in 18 States and the UT of Andaman & Nicobar
Islands for activities which includes, documentation of intangible heritage/arts and crafts of
tribal communities, developing database for Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Particularly Vulnerable
Tribal Groups (PVTGs) including collection of documentation, translation and publication on
the tribal heritage, festivals, oral and visual folklore, arts, local games, sports, songs, literature
etc; development and printing of primers in tribal languages and local official language,
publication of books/dictionaries of tribal languages and translating policy provisions in major
tribal languages for dissemination of the same amongst tribals etc; and organization of tribal
festival and exchange of visits by tribals. Conservation and preservation of tribal culture and
heritage is one of the key components of recently launched approach “Van Bandhu
KalyanYojana”.
3.6.2 Committee is dismayed to note the routine and evasive reply of the Government
on such a specific and important issue. The Committee has been given to understand
that according to UNESCO Atlas of the World’s Languages in Danger data published in
the year 2009, 26 languages of Arunachal have been identified as endangered and it is
even more worrying that even languages of largely populated tribal groups like Adi,
Galo, Nyishi too have been categorized as unsafe by UNESCO due to the heavy influence
of Hindi language. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should
look into this matter seriously and take concrete steps for preservation of tribal
cultures and their languages in NER. Separate budgetary provision may be made for this
purpose.
3.7 Bru Tribal Families’ Repatriation And Rehabilitation in Mizoram:
3.7.1 The Committee took cognizance of the issue of Bru tribal families’ repatriation and
rehabilitation in Mizoram as there were reports of inadequacy of funds provided for their
rehabilitation and enquired about the details of the issue and how the Government intends to

59
resolve this issue. The Ministry, in this regard submitted that due to ethnic violence in Mizoram
in October, 1997, approximately 30,000 (5,000 families) Bru migrants were migrated from
Mizoram and sheltered in relief camps set-up in Kanchanpur district of North Tripura. The
Ministry of Home Affairs has been extending following assistance/Grants-in-Aid to Govt. of
Tripura since 1997-98 for maintenance of Bru migrants sheltered in relief camps in Tripura and
to Govt. of Mizoram w.e.f. 2004-05 for rehabilitation & resettlement of Brus in Mizoram:
i. Housing assistance to each family of Rs.38,500.
ii. Cash assistance to each family of Rs.41,500.
iii. Free ration to each adult and minor member for one year.
iv. Reimbursement of transportation cost incurred by Govt. of Mizoram.
v. Blankets and utensils to each Bru family.
3.7.2 The Bru migrants are being repatriated from Tripura to Mizoram in a phased manner.
As envisaged, the repatriation process was disrupted/stopped due to protests by certain Mizo
NGOs in 2011 and 2012. Hence, Grant-in-Aid to Government of Mizoram could not be released
in 2012-13 and 2013-14 as no repatriation took place. Though, steps have been taken to
complete the repatriation process and as a result of regular follow up, 173 families have been
repatriated in the 6th Batch including self-repatriation, making a total repatriation of about
1,210 Bru families (approx. 5,000 people) as on 28.2.2015. During the financial year 2014- 15,
Rs. 35 crore and Rs. 5 crore were provided to the Government of Tripura and Mizoram
respectively under the scheme. As per Action Plan submitted by the Govt. of Mizoram, the Bru
repatriation process is expected to be completed by August/September, 2015. Now more funds
have to be released to the Government of Mizoram in 2015-16 for rehabilitation of Bru
migrants with the corresponding decrease of funds for the Government of Tripura.
3.7.3 The Committee is overwhelmingly concerned that even after almost two decades
the Bru tribe is suffering from the aftermath of ethnic violence. It is disappointed with
the efforts of the Governments of Tripura and Mizoram and is worried about the fact
that till now the complete repatriation and rehabilitation of Bru migrants has not taken
place. The Committee recommends that Bru migrants must be accorded all support and
protection and their repatriation and rehabilitation be completed at the earliest. The
Committee also recommends that Ministry must ensure that shortage of funds must not
come in the way of full and final repatriation and complete rehabilitation of Bru
migrants.

OBSERV ATIONS /CONCLUSIONS/ RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE-
AT A GLANCE
Total Revenue and Capital Outlay
The Committee is concerned about the huge shortfall of Rs.714.71 crore in the
approved budgetary allocation as compared to projected demands and wonders as to how
the Ministry will make up for this huge deficit. It recommends that the Ministry of
DoNER should take up this matter with the Ministry of Finance to get an enhanced
allocation at the RE stage so that all the planned expenditure and committed liabilities
are fulfilled. (Para 2.2.5)
The Committee is disappointed to note the inability of the Ministry to utilize
the funds completely which were reduced at RE stage for various plans schemes like
NLCPR, NESRIP etc. This shortfall in financial targets is unacceptable in these critical
schemes as it casts a shadow over the absorption capacity of the implementing
agencies of the programmes. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the
Ministry of DoNER must impress upon all the concerned line Ministries/Departments/
Agencies to take urgent steps for enhancing their capacity to utilize allocated funds
completely. (Para 2.2.8)
North Eastern Council
The Committee notes with serious concern the trend of decreasing allocation of
funds to North Eastern Council. The substantial cut in allocation at RE stages in
consecutive years may be a result of non-submission/ late submission of Utilization
Certificate by State Governments who in turn are unable to do so due to severe weather
and heavy monsoon that lead to stoppage of work in various projects. The Committee
also note that the assessment period for determining budgetary allocation at RE stage,
coincides with the immediate aftermath of the longer monsoon season in North East
Region. In view of the Committee, this period of assessment is not realistic as not only
NE Region but also whole country except few pockets witness monsoon rains; thus
causing disruption in construction activities. The Committee recommends that the
Ministry of Finance should take a realistic and practical approach to the important issue
of deciding supplementary allocations and revised allocations and adopt a liberal
approach or may desist from making any substantial cut while allocating funds at RE
stage for schemes and projects particularly of North East Region. Alternatively, the
Ministry of DoNER may in consultation with North East States, NITI Aayog and Ministry
of Finance may explore a different mechanism like considering a different time period
for Northeast region having normal weather for assessment of utilization of funds and
consequent increase/decrease in allocation at RE stage. (Para 2.3.8)
60

61
The Committee is dismayed with the tentative division of allocated funds in
different sectors by NEC and is unhappy to see very low allocation being made to
critically and potentially important sectors like health, industries and tourism. The
Committee strongly feels that while it is important to give higher allocation to critical
sectors like transport and communication, HRD etc., socially and economically
important sectors cannot be afforded to be neglected. The Committee Therefore,
recommends that NEC and Ministry of DoNER should revisit the appropriation of
allocation to different sectors and evolve a more equitable and comprehensive method
of sectoral division of funds so that no important sector gets neglected and a
wholesome development is achieved. (Para 2.3.9)
The Committee is disappointed with the issue of non-release of funds by State
Governments to implementing agencies becoming a major bottleneck in project
implementation and optimal fund utilization. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the State Governments must ensure timely release of funds to implementing
agencies for completion of projects without time and cost overruns. The Committee
further recommends that the monitoring mechanism must also be further strengthened
by including strict penal provisions for delay/non release of funds on one hand and also
giving incentives to those States who comply with timelines and guidelines in the
completion of projects. (Para 2.3.10)
Construction/Improvement of Roads of Economic Importance:

is yet to be completed even when the project has been handed over to BRO. The

The Committee strongly recommends that the latest deadline of March 2016 for

begin identification of other such projects which can be implemented under this
head. (Para 2.4.3)
Non Plan Loans To North Eastern Handicrafts And Handlooms Development Corporation
(NEHHDC)
The Committee notes that some progress is being made for implementation of
the revival plan of NEHHDC but is disappointed that the complete revival of NEHHDC
has yet not taken place. NEHHDC is a crucial organization for providing support to
livelihood of numerous artisans, weavers and small scale producers and entrepreneurs.
The Committee therefore recommends that the revival of NEHHDC must be completed
at the earliest and towards this end, the sanctioned amount in the form of equity must
be released to the Corporation as early as possible. (Para 2.5.5)
Loan To North Eastern Regional Agricultural Marketing  Corporation (NERAMAC)
The Committee is not convinced with the contention of the Ministry that the cut
of nearly 50 percent at RE stage was done with a view to curtail the trend of

62
incremental financial losses especially in view of the increased demand and allocation in
BE 2015-16. In view of the Committee this trend was being followed since many years
and all of a sudden, this plea is being advanced. However, the Committee feels that the

interest rates. Therefore, the Committee recommends that either the Ministry should
facilitate NERAMAC and enable it to access cheaper funds from the market or the
Ministry must provide loans to it at relaxed rates of interest and favorable terms and
conditions. The Committee desires that the revival plan of the Corporation should be
expedited. It is very strange that entities in private sector in the same field are

years even to the such level that its working capital has wiped out. (Para 2.6.4)

direction but the pace needs to be hastened. The Committee recommends that the
proposed e-auction centers must be established at the earliest to ensure better and

centers must be spread throughout the region and a centralized e-auction system may
be devised to ensure a wider market for the growers. (Para 2.6.6)
Food processing units are necessary for value addition to agricultural produce;
prevent post-harvest losses and providing better remuneration to farmers. The
Committee is perturbed to note that various processing units are lying defunct and
suffering from various ailments. The Committee recommends that NERAMAC should
guide its efforts to revive these processing units by providing assistance for better
equipments, technical know-how and affordable finance. (Para 2.6.7)
Loans to North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Limited (NEDFi)
The Committee notes the progress of NEDFi towards becoming a self-sustainable
Corporation and also its efforts to promote economically and socially weaker sections of
society in NER. Regarding the identification of beneficiaries for NEDFi’s support, the
Committee feels that while voluntary enquiries are a valid basis, however, those not
knowing about the Corporation and its services may not be able to approach it always.
Therefore, the Committee recommends that NEDFi should intensify its efforts towards
increasing the scope and coverage of its activities to reach more number of
entrepreneurs in need of affordable finance. (Para 2.7.7)
Non-Lapsable Central Pool Of Resources For North Eastern Region And Sikkim
The Committee reiterates its recommendations made in a preceding para
No. 2.3.8 that there is need to revisit the whole process of allocation of funds under
