rebuilding the economy of the State within a set time frame.  (Para 2.50)

1.7.2 In the wake of severe unprecedented floods and landslides in Jammu and Kashmir in
September 2014, the State Government of Jammu and Kashmir submitted a memorandum for a
financial assistance of R44000 crore, out of which R2926.11 crore was sought for immediate relief

Chairmanship of Union Home Minister approved an assistance of R1602.56 cr. to the State from

tion measures for the flood affected State of Jammu & Kashmir.

1.7.7 The Committee would like to be apprised of the details of long term plan for
reconstruction of State of J&K in the aftermath the severe floods and as and when  the same
is prepared.

CHAPTER- II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS ON WHICH THE COMMITTEE
DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE THE MATTER IN VIEW OF THE
GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
2.1 ARRANGING SATTELITE PHONES AS BACK UP COMMUNICATION
Recommendation
2.1.1 The Committee notes that even when the State of J&K had an early warning, the State
had not enough satellite phones available which resulted into break down of communication
system and there was no way to contact the officials at district level. Secondly, even with an
early warning, the personnel available with the State Government were not trained making
them therefore incapable to mobilize resources sufficiently in advance.  (Para 2.29)
Action Taken
2.1.2 All States/UTs have been advised during the Relief Commissioner’s conference to take
adequate preparedness measures including arranging satellite phones as back up communication.
2.1.3 The Central Government facilitates training of State Disaster Response Force personnel
through National Disaster Response Force.
2.2 SUPERVISION AND MONITORING OF FUNDS RELEASED
Recommendation
2.2.1 The Committee takes into account the funds provided to the State Government of
J&K by the Central Government. The Committee feels that funds so released by the
Central Government must be utilized for the purpose and its utilization must be under
close supervision and monitoring. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Gov-
ernment should constitute Joint Team consisting of the representative of State Govern-
ment and the Central Government for better administration and implementation of
programmes with fair deal of justice and equitable distribution.  (Para 2.37)
Action Taken
2.2.2 The recommendation of the Committee is noted. Distribution of relief at ground level is
done by the concerned State Administration. As our constitution has federal provision, the role of
Central Government in distributing the relief directly to affected people is limited. However, the
representatives of Central Governments are frequently visiting the State to review the post disaster
relief and rehabilitation works.
2.3 PREPAREDNESS OF RESCUE AND THE RELIEF MACHINARY
Recommendation
2.3.1 The Committee is not quite satisfied with the preparedness of rescue and relief
machinery and disaster Management set up in the State of Jammu and Kashmir. Despite
all disaster management set up in the State as well as the national level, the Committee
7

8
does not understand as to how there was not enough preparedness. The Committee is of the
opinion that there is no use of referring to the provisions of National Disaster Management
Act 2005 and to reiterate that Disaster management Activities fall within the jurisdiction of
the State Government and Central Government only provides logistic support to the State
Government. Therefore, the moot issue is the actual implementation of the provision of the
Act. The Committee therefore, recommends that necessary steps may be taken to
strengthen the National Disaster Management mechanism. The Committee has already
given its one Hundred and Seventy Eight Report on Disaster management in the Country.

recommendations contained in that report would definitely lead to better functioning of
disaster management machinery at the national and State level. (Para 2.49)
Action Taken
2.3.2 There are institutional mechanisms at the National and State level for effective management
of natural disasters. The rescue and relief at the ground level is done by the concerned State

2.3.3 In this regard, it may be noted that as per Ministry of Finance, the World Bank has
sanctioned a loan amount of US $ 250 million for J&K Flood Recovery Project.  One component
of the scheme is imparting training and skills for better Disaster Management response at a cost
of 25 million US dollar.

CHAPTER- III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE
GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
3.1 HEA VY CASUALTIES OF HUMAN LOSS AND PROPERTIES
Recommendation
3.1.1 The Committee is concerned to observe that the State Government of Jammu &
Kashmir received forewarning that State would receive heavier rainfall than the normal
rain but the kind of preemptive measures taken by State Government were not sufficient
to withstand the fury of the nature and the result was heavy casualties in terms of human
loss and properties including public infrastructure in the State. The Committee notes that
in the previous year when Phailin struck Odisha, the State Government of Odisha had
done a commendable job in terms of evacuation and other facilities that were provided but
comparatively, Jammu and Kashmir had more death toll.  (Para 2.19)
Action Taken
3.1.2 All State Governments/ UTs are required to take requisite preparatory measures based on
the warning issued by the different forecasting Agencies. In this regard, the Ministry of Home
Affairs organizes Annual Conference of the Relief Commissioners/ Secretary (Disaster Management)
of the States and Union Territories to sensitise the States/UTs about the requisite preparedness
measures to deal with disasters. In this year conference was held on 16.05.2015. The Union Home
Secretary has advised all the State Governments/ UTs to take each and every warning seriously and
take requisite preparedness measures for dealing with the disasters. It was also decided to organize
the conference twice a year, so that preparedness of the State Governments/ UTs can be reviewed
more frequently. It may also be noted that response time for slow developing weather phenomena
like cyclone is more compared to response time for disaster, like landslides, flash flood/floods,
avalanche, earthquake etc. The strengthening of the disaster management mechanism is a continu-
ing process of the governance.  However, on the basis of the recommendation of the Committee,
the State Governments/ UTs have been advised to immediately act upon the warnings of early
warning agencies vide MHA letter dated 18.06.2015.
Further Recommendation
3.1.3 The Committee observes that the Central Government is furnishing routine reply,
and in fact, is shrugging off its responsibility in guiding the State Government to combat
the Disaster by just pleading that Union Ministry of Home Affairs had issued Advisory to
all State/UTs Government to strengthen the Disaster Management set-up. The Committee is
not satisfied with the steps taken even after the disaster had taken place. This shows the
lack of preparedness. The Committee, therefore, strongly, recommends that the Central
Government must guide the State/UTs Government to re-orient the disaster management
set-up in consonance with region specific geographical features, climate and keeping in view
the frequency and possibility of striking of the Disaster in the region.

3.4 BETTER DISASTER MANAGEMENT
Recommendation
3.4.1 The Committee is therefore of the view that in order to combat the natural
calamities/furies, the Central Government needs comprehensive National Planning with
resilient system for better disaster management throughout the country, irrespective of the
frequency of disasters in a particular area/region. For combating the possible onslaught of
natural fury, there is urgent need for better coordination between national and State
agencies. The Committee, therefore, feels that at the national level, the country should
have a much better pre-emptive action from the Central authorities, particularly for the
States which are not used to this kind of disaster frequently. The Central Government
should apprise the State Governments some kind of advanced planning and mechanism that

13
the State Governments must put in place invariably without any failure. The Committee
believes that the State Government must realize the consequences of nature fury and
should not be complacent at any time and must have comprehensive planning for enhancing
capabilities at the time of natural calamities.  (Para 2.30)
Action Taken
3.4.2 In order to strengthen the existing disaster management system, the Disaster Management
Act, 2005 was enacted and notified on December 26, 2005. The Act provides for institutional
mechanisms for drawing up and monitoring the implementation of the disaster management plans,
which includes holistic, coordinated, and prompt response to any calamity situation in the country
and ensures measures by various wings of Government for prevention, mitigation and for mini-
mizing the effects of calamities. Further, the strengthening of the disaster management is a
continuing process of the governance.
3.4.3 There are institutional mechanisms at the National and State level for effective management
of natural disasters. The Government of India extends all the possible logistics and financial
assistance to the States to supplement their efforts to meet the situation effectively.
3.4.4 In this regard it may be noted that there is already a National Disaster Management Plan
prepared by the Central Government. The Plan elaborates various phases of disaster management
like preparedness, response, capacity building and mitigation.
Further Recommendation
3.4.5 The Committee notes the provisions for institutional mechanism under DM Act, 2005
for implementation of Disaster Management Plan. Though strengthening of the Disaster
Management is a continuous process but the resilience of existing disaster apparatus gets
exposed at and unfortunate time when a disaster strikes.  The Committee, therefore,
strongly recommends that MHA should review all aspects of Disaster Management and
accordingly pursue State/UTs Government to take appropriate action on the ground level to
combat the fury of any disaster.

CHAPTER- IV
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH FINAL REPLIES OF
THE GOVERNMENT HA VE NOT BEEN RECEIVED
4.1 RELIEF NOT REACHING THE EFFECTED PEOPLE IN J&K
Recommendation
4.1.1 While appreciating the feelings of the Home Secretary, the Committee feels that
resource reach was not there in the interior valley, particularly in those villages which are
known to have extremism problem. It was pointed out to the committee that apart from all
the issues of preventive planning, the reach of relief to the people and other things was
grossly inadequate despite the claim of both the Central Government and the State
Government that there was no dearth of resources. It was also pointed out that there was
increased feeling among the affected people that relief was not reaching to them in spite
of generous help from all quarters/countries. The Committee in this background is of the
opinion that both the Central Government and the State Government should understand the
complexities involved in the matter as it is not merely a question of providing relief to the
people who are victims of natural disaster but of winning hearts with relief service in their
distress. The Committee feels that if there is any truth in the allegation that relief is not
reaching the affected people in J&K, the Government should ensure that all the loopholes
should be plugged.  (Para 2.33)
Action Taken
4.1.2 The feeling of the Committee is noted. The distribution of relief at the ground level is done
by the concerned State Administration. However, whenever any inadequacy was noticed by this
Ministry, the State Government has been advised to look into the matter and take corrective
measures.
4.1.3 Further the State Government of J&K has been requested to provide Action Taken Report
on the recommendation of the Committee. The information is awaited.
4.2 RAMPANT ENCROACHMENT ON RIVER BANKS AND NATURAL DRAINS
Recommendation
4.2.1 The Committee desired to highlight that so far as Srinagar is concerned, it was
patently obvious that flood pathways that have been in existence since Moghul times have
all been heavily populated, The Committee notes the submission of the representative of
the State Government that the colonies like Badami Bagh Cantt., where the Army Corps
headquarter is located, Rajbagh, Mahjong Nagar are basically flood plains which were meant
to serve as flood plains. The Committee was given to understand that there was rampant
encroachment on river banks and natural drains, for instance, in Poonch near Sher-e-
Kashmir bridge there was reportedly a colony of 250 buildings and in another area there
was brick kiln which were washed away by the floods. It has also been alleged that the real
estate in Jammu and Kashmir, especially, the Srinagar Valley, has been rampantly violating
the established norms and modalities. Needless to say it is well established fact that fiddling
with natural courses of rivers and drains by constructing buildings, etc. whether legal or
illegal, will, not only, have adverse impact on the ecology and environment  but will also

18
invite natural disasters. Knowing fully well that these are the traditional pathways for the
outflow of water, the Committee wonders as to how the State Government and the
administration permitted constructions in such areas.
4.2.2 The Committee observes that on both the banks of Jhelum River where the disaster has
taken place and in the major areas of Srinagar city, there was water for three weeks. The
Committee believes that the accumulated water was not just allowed to flow through its normal
and natural route, as the same was blocked,. The Committee is constrained to express its
displeasure as to why the local authorities allowed such encroachments on a large scale which led
to such disaster. The Committee is, therefore, of the considered view that the Government should
bring into force building bye laws keeping in view the topology of the State so that encroachments
on river banks are avoided. (Para 2.38)
Action Taken
4.2.3 The State Government of Jammu and Kashmir and the Ministry of Water Resources have
been requested to furnish action taken report on the same vide letter dated 16
th June 2015, 26 th June
2015 and 24 th July 2015. The information is awaited.
Further Recommendation
4.2.4 The Committee desires to be informed of the Action Taken Report received from the
Ministry of Water Resources and then State Government.
4.3 DREDGING ASPECT OF THE WATER BODIES
Recommendation
4.3.1 The Committee notes that it has become normal to ignore dredging aspect of the
water bodies be it sea or rivers and the projects for deepening and dredging hang fire for
long, gathering dust in the shelfs. The Committee takes serious note of this and desires
that dredging proposals of the rivers submitted by the State Government particularly flood
prone States should be cleared at the earliest so that the work on this is finished before
next monsoon. The Committee also desires that the State Governments should be asked to
adhere to the time limit.  (Para 2.41)
Action Taken
4.3.2 The State Government of Jammu and Kashmir has been requested to furnish action taken
report on the same vide letter dated 16
th June 2015, 26 th June 2015 and 24 th July 2015. The
information is awaited.
4.3.3 However, CWC has informed that a project report for flood management of river Jhelum was
prepared by the State Government in 2009 at an estimated cost of R2083.90 cr. The proposal was
examined by the CWC and offered some comments. However, no compliance was made by the State
Government. After the Jammu and Kashmir flood in 2014, a three member group was constituted by
the Ministry of Water Resources to conduct an in depth study and analysis of the recent unprecedented
floods in J&K for preventing such floods in future. The Committee submitted its report and recom-
mended different measures to be adopted for immediate, short term, and long term. Accordingly, the
State Government is formulating a comprehensive flood management programme of river Jhelum and
its tributaries to manage 1 in 100 years flood of 3260 cumec at Sangam in two phases.

19
4.3.4 Further, it is informed by CWC that meanwhile, the State Government has prepared a
project report to address the immediate problems of existing flood spill channel and main river
Jhelum at an estimated cost of R399.29 cr.  The proposed work will partially mitigate the flood
problems of Srinagar, Budgam, Baramulla, Anantnag, Pulwama and Bandipora on emergent basis.
The project would be implemented in 2 years. The scheme is expected to benefit more than 1.35
lakh people. The scheme after concurrence of State Governments has been cleared by the Advisory
on Irrigation, Flood Control and Multipurpose projects of Ministry of Water Resources on 25.05.15.
4.3.5 In the past, 4 flood management schemes with an estimated cost of R128.75 cr. has
already been taken up on river Jhelum in Jammu and Kashmir by the State Government and an
amount of R114.64 cr. as Central Assistance has been released to the State by the Ministry of
Water Resources, RD&GR.

20
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS — AT A GLANCE
MEDIUM AND LONG TERM REHABILITATION PLAN
The Committee desires to be apprised medium and long term rehabilitation plan
finalized. (Para 1.4.3)
DE-SILTING OF AGRICULTURAL LAND
The Committee hopes that the earmarked amount i.e. RRRRR3.99 crore from SDRF/NDRF
would be sufficient for de-silting of agricultural land and a further sanctioned amount of
RRRRR1.96 crore would be sufficient for removal of debris from agricultural land. The State
Government may prepare proposal for further assistance for medium and long term work.
(Para 1.5.4)
LONG TERM RECONSTRUCTION PLAN
The Committee would like to be apprised of the details of long term plan for
reconstruction of State of J&K in the aftermath the severe floods and as and when the
same is prepared. (Para 1.7.7)
HEA VY CASUALTIES OF HUMAN LOSS AND PROPERTIES
The Committee observes that the Central Government is furnishing routine reply,
and in fact, is shrugging off its responsibility in guiding the State Government to combat
the Disaster by just pleading that Union Ministry of Home Affairs had issued Advisory to all
State/UTs Government to strengthen the Disaster Management set-up. The Committee is
not satisfied with the steps taken even after the disaster had taken place. This shows the
lack of preparedness. The Committee, therefore, strongly, recommends that the Central
Government must guide the State/UTs government to re-orient the disaster management
set-up in consonance with region specific geographical features, climate and keeping in view
the frequency and possibility of striking of the Disaster in the region. (Para 3.1.3)
RELIEF AND REHABILITATION WORK
The Committee notes the details of the financial assistance extended to the State
Government of J&K for rescue & relief operation from SDRF/NDRF and as special package,
restoration and rehabilitation under PM’s Special Project Assistance and long term
assistance for reconstruction plan being monitored by Ministry of Finance in consultation
with the .N.ITI Ayog. Against the projected assistance of RRRRR44000 crore by the State
Government ( RRRRR2827 crore claimed from SDRF/NDRF and balance as special package) HLC
approved RRRRR1602.56 crore from NDRF, that too, subject to adjustment of 90°,10 balance in
SDRF and book adjustment to the tune of RRRRR500 crore as air bill and after all adjustment the
financial assistance from Central Government under NDRF is merely RRRRR43.53 crore. The
Ministry of Finance, however, also approved RRRRR1000 crore under SPA for restoration and
rehabilitation.        (Para 3.2.12)
The Committee further wishes to point out that out of an additional central
assistance of RRRRR1667.71 crore, an amount of RRRRR834 crore has been earmarked for short term

21
relief and reconstruction measures but to the utmost surprise an amount of RRRRR838 crore has
been posted on account of pending liabilities of Prime Minister’s Reconstruction Plan 2004
at the time when the people of the State are shocked due to unprecedented flood and
landslide. Against this backdrop, the Committee strongly recommends that the Central
Government must first ameliorate the State from the shock ofpood through relief and
restoration and infuse sufficient fund to State’s kitty for rehabilitation and long term
reconstruction plan. The Committee recommends that all the financial packages must get
a kick-start with sufficient fund.       (Para 3.2.13)
The Committee, however, cautions the Central as well as the State Government that
concerted efforts must be made to ensure that all announced packages and reconstruction
project plan are implemented within set time frame for putting State economy back on rail.
(Para3.2.14)
SUSTAINABLE COMPENSATION AMOUNT
The Committee understands that the assistance provided from SDRF and NDRF is for
immediate relief and not for compensation of losses. The Committee notes that the
Government has come forward with revised norms with effect from 8th April, 2015 on relief,
rescue and rehabilitation scheme in the aftermath of disaster. The Committee, however,
observes that relief amount is not sufficient enough even for providing immediate relief,
therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that compensation amount must be
substantial for the affected persons. (Para 3.3.3)
BETTER DISASTER MANAGEMENT
The Committee notes the provisions for institutional mechanism under DM Act, 2005
for implementation of Disaster Management Plan. Though strengthening of the Disaster
Management is a continuous process but the resilience of existing disaster apparatus gets
exposed at and unfortunate time when a disaster strikes. The Committee, therefore,
strongly recommends that MHA should review all aspects of Disaster Management and
accordingly pursue State/UTs Government to take appropriate action on the ground level to
combat the fury of any disaster. (Para 3.4.5)
STRENGTHING OF DISASTER RISK MANAGEMENT
The Committee observes that World Bank has sanctioned a loan amount of US$ 250
million for J&K flood Reconstruction Project and out oJ that US$ 25 is earmarked for
strengthening of Disaster Risk Management, therefore, the Committee strongly
recommends that all out efforts must be made towards the objective of strengthening of
Disaster Risk Management capacity in J&K. (Para 1.5.5)
DEFORSTATION CAUSING FLOODS
The Committee, taking into account that deforestation in the State invited
unprecedented flood, recommends that the Central Government may follow up with state
government in the matter for report and as and when the same is received may be sent
to this Committee. (Para 3.6.3)

22
LEARING OF DRAINS AND RIVERS
The Committee reiterates its observation made in Para 2.42 of 182nd Report and
further recommends that Central Government must pursue with the State Government
about the utilization of funds to the tune of RRRRR60 crore sanctioned to the State
Government for clearing drains and rivers by removing silts and sand from the agricultural
lands to make it cultivable. (Para 3.7.3)
COMPREHENSIVE FLOOD MANAGEMENT
The Committee takes note that a comprehensive proposals of State Government of
J&K involving an expenditure of RRRRR2013 for flood management of river Jhelum is under
consideration of Government of India. Out of the said proposal, RRRRR400 crore, which has got
approval of Ministry of Water Resources, is pending under consideration of Ministry of
Finance. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Finance must
examine and consider the proposal of J&K Government expeditiously so that the State does
not face unfortunate flood situation again. (Para 3.8.4)
TOURISM AS MAINSTAY OF J&K ECONOMY
The Committee hopes that the earmarked central assistance amount to the tune of
R100 crore for rebuilding of tourist infrastructure would be sufficient for intended purpose.
In nutshell, the Committee desires tliat concerted efforts be undertaken by the State
Government to ensure that the tourism sector is developed to fullest potential. The
Committee further recommends that the Central Government may release the requisite
funds at the earliest. (Para 3.9.3)
RAMPANT ENCROACHMENT ON RIVER BANKS AND NATURAL DRAINS
The Committee desires to be informed of the Action Taken Report received from the
Ministry of Water Resources and then State Government. (Para 4.2.4)

1.1 NON PLAN LOANS TO NORTH EASTERN HANDICRAFTS AND  HANDLOOMS 
DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION (NEHHDC) 
 
Recommendation  
  
1.1.1 The Committee notes that some progress is bei ng made for implementation of the revival 
plan of NEHHDC but is disappointed that the complet e revival of NEHHDC has yet not taken 
place.  NEHHDC is a crucial organization for provid ing support to livelihood of numerous 
artisans, weavers and small scale producers and ent repreneurs.  The Committee therefore 
recommends that the revival of NEHHDC must be compl eted at the earliest and towards this end, 
the sanctioned amount in the form of equity must be  released to the Corporation as early as 
possible. 
(Para 2.5.5 of 186 th  Report) 
Action Taken 
 
1.1.2 The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs in its meeting held on 21 
st  February, 2013, 
approved the Revival plan of NEHHDC as under: - 
i) Infusion of fresh equity of Rs. 6.5 crore (Rs. 4.00  crore in first year and Rs. 2.5 crore in 
second year) 
ii) Infusion of Rs. 2.00 crore in the form of equity fo r implementing VRS for 20 employees, 
which is a pre-condition for operationalisation of the revival plan. 
iii) Conversion of Government of India of Rs. 36.02 cror e and outstanding interest of Rs. 
47.04 crore as on 31.12.2011, into equity and simul taneous write off of equity against 
accumulated losses incurred by the Corporation 
1.1.3 All the above steps have been taken by the Go vernment over the last two years.  The 
balance amount of equity of Rs. 2.5 crore was sanctioned on 26.03.2015.  The fund received under 
the Revival Plan has been kept in the escrow accoun t opened by NEHHDC for the purpose. The 
expenditure on implementation Revival Plan was comm enced by NEHHDC in 2014-15.  The 
following steps have also been taken for Revival of the NEHHDC: 
 
1. Closure of Loss making Units : Two loss making Showrooms at New Delhi and 
Bangalore were closed down in September 2013. This has resulted in savings of Rs.40.00 
Lac per annum to the Corporation. 
2. Change in existing Consignment Sales Policy:  Modified Consignment Sales Policy in 
Emporia introduced at Shillong, Guwahati and Kolkata emporia. 
3. Sourcing and Procurement of Handicrafts & Handlo oms : Higher volume of 
procurement made from various states of the North Eastern Region. 
4. Development of Clusters for strengthening supply chain: 
a) Five clusters at Barpeta, Tezpur, Silchar, Agart ala and Imphal identified for 
development by organizing awareness camps, training and procurements etc. 
b) MoU signed with the Tripura Bamboo Mission (TMB) to strengthen supply chain. 
5. Thrust on Institutional Sales:  
Emporia and Sales Promotion Offices have been given  targets for Institutional Sales 
(Rs.2.00 crore) for the year 2015-16 
 
6. Product Line Standardization:  

a) Set up a Design Bank at Guwahati for the benefit s of the artisans and weavers of 
the North Eastern Region. 
b) Set up a production Centre at Craft Promotion Ce ntre, Guwahati for production 
of cane and bamboo based furniture items 
c) Set up a Common Facility Centre at Guwahati for processing bamboo and for 
production of bamboo sticks, sticks and splits etc. 
d) Set up a Handlooms Production cum Training Centre at Guwahati for production 
of value added handlooms items and for imparting training to women weavers. 
e) Set up a Handicrafts Museum at Guwahati showcasi ng the handicrafts and 
textiles of the North Eastern Region for the benefi ts of the artisans and weavers 
community.  
7. Renovation of Showrooms:  
Showrooms at Shillong, Guwahati, Kolkata and Chenna i has been renovated which has 
resulted in improved sales compared to earlier years. 
8. Computerization of the activities in the Corporation :  
Inventory Management, Bar-coding facilities install ed in Emporia at Shillong, Guwahati 
and Kolkata and necessary training to staff on application of software conducted. 
9. E-Commerce:  
a) A new Web Portal 
www.nehhdc.in  launched for e-marketing. Details of products 
and services will be up loaded and the portal will be made functional within three 
months.  
b) MoU signed with Snapdeal for facilitating e- commerce. 
c) Tie up with Indiamart.com made for bulk sale. 
10.  Strategic Partnering with Tribal Cooperative Marke ting Development Federation of 
India Limited (TRIFED), Central Cottage Industries Emporium (CCIC) and Handicrafts

1.2 NER LIVELIHOOD PROJECT (NERLP) - EAP  
 
Recommendation  
 
1.2.1 The Committee notes the close coordination an d strong linkages between NERLP and 
other livelihood schemes in rural areas of NER. The  Committee recommends that the Ministry 
should keep up this scheme and try to expand it fur ther to create self-sustainable institutions and 
ensure ample livelihood opportunities for the rural poor.

2.3 LOAN TO NORTH EASTERN REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MAR KETING 
CORPORATION (NERAMAC) - REVIVAL PLAN 
 
Recommendation 
 
2.3.1  The Committee is not convinced with the contention of the Ministry that the cut of nearly 
50 percent at RE stage was done with a view to curt ail the trend of incremental financial losses 
especially in view of the increased demand and allo cation in BE 2015-16. In view of the 
Committee this trend was being followed since many years and all of a sudden, this plea is being 
advanced. However, the Committee feels that the wor king capital loan being given to NERAMAC 
carries unduly high interest and penal interest rat es. Therefore, the committee recommends that 
either the Ministry should facilitate NERAMAC and e nable it to access cheaper funds from the 
market or the Ministry must provide loans to it at relaxed rate of interest and favorable terms and 
conditions. The Committee desires that the revival plan of the Corporation should be expedited. It 
is very strange that entities in private sector in the same field are flourishing while entity in 
Government sector is making continuous losses since  many years even to such a level that its 
working capital has wiped out. 
(Para 2.6.4 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
2.3.2 During 2013-14, NERAMAC could draw Rs. 1.00 c rore only out of a budgetary provision 
made for Rs. 2.00 crore as working capital loan. The utility of working capital loan to NERAMAC 
during 2014-15 was carefully scrutinized by the com petent authority in Ministry of DoNER. 
NERAMAC authorities could not satisfactorily presen t essential information on critical resource 
management functions of NERAMAC either in the form of a sound action plan for utilization of 
working capital loan over the financial year or a s ector-wise application module for such loans 
funds and the recovery cycles of the working capita l during the entire financial year (2014-15).  
Therefore, it appeared to the authorities in Minist ry of DoNER after careful consideration of 
circumstances, that there was hardly any scope for proper utilization of an additional spell of 
working capital loan with an efficient outcome for NERAMAC.   
 
2.3.3 As regards provision of cheaper funds to NERA MAC, the net worth of the organization 
and its loan repaying capacity are critical conside rations.  However, NERAMAC has been found 
to have made provision for interest payment on work ing capital loan sanctioned to it till date but 
has not deposited any amount with Ministry of DoNER  either as accrued interest or recovery of 
principal amount of the loan.  Further spell of the  working capital loan at concessional rate or 
waiver of accrued interest till date depends on future course of the decisions on NERAMAC, to be 
taken by the Central Government.  
 
2.3.4 The revival plan for NERAMAC has to be such t hat the organization can run on 
commercial principles in future and flourish with i ts own momentum. There is a need to consider 
the market demand and factors such as forces of com petitions being thrown open in both regional 
and national markets. Therefore, before formulating  plans and revival package, there is a need to 
carefully anticipate the market forces and factors beforehand through a techno-economic study in 
the present context of the growing NER markets and in the backdrop of increased incidence of 
private sector participation under an upcoming free market environment.

2.9 TRADE AND INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT SECTOR 
 
Recommendation  
 
2.9.1 NEIIPP is an important policy that led to a m inor beginning of industrial development in 
North East. The Committee notes that it provides va rious subsidies and exemptions to promote 
investment and industrial development in NER.A prop er accountability mechanism should have 
ensured a regular cost-benefit analysis and impact assessment of the policy every year.  However, 
after 2010 no such evaluation was done till 2014.  The Committee recommends that evaluation 
study of NEIIPP must be done every two years and the Ministry must apprise the Committee of the 
results regularly. 
(Para 3.3.2 ibid) 
Action Taken  
 
2.9.2 As per the DIPP a third party evaluation stud y of  Package of Incentive under North East 
Industrial Investment Promotion Policy (NEIIPP), 2007 for development of industries in the States 
of NER (including Sikkim ) was undertaken by an ind ependent agency i.e. Centre for Market 
Research & Social Development (CFMRSD) at the behes t of DIPP. CFMRSD has submitted its 
final evaluation study report vide letter dated 16.03.2015. 
 
2.9.3 Following are highlights of the key findings of the report: 
(i) The main hindrances for slow pace of industrialization as identified by the study report 
inter-alia include absence of dedicated and regular  power supply, transport bottleneck, 
lack of communication facility, prevailing law and order situation, shortage of 
technical and skilled manpower, lack of credit flow  from Bank/financial institutions, 
geographical isolation, etc.  
(ii) A positive investment climate has developed after c ommencement of NEIIPP-2007 
policy. A total of 151929 gainful employments have been generated in the NER since 
the commencement of NEIIPP-2007.  
(iii) Out of total 323 units provided subsidy under NEIIP P-2007, 95% industries represents 
manufacturing and 5% industries represents service sector.  
(iv) There had been lopsided disbursement of subsidy. As sam and Meghalaya availed the 
maximum benefits of the policy whereas States like Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland have 
availed little or no benefit. Large scale industrie s have received a lion share in the 
disbursement.    
(v) Compatibility exists in NEIIPP-2007 and National Ma nufacturing Policy as both 
complement each other as far as industrialization issue is concerned.   
 
(vi) Post-NEIIPP 2007, 23212 MSME units registered out of which 301 have so far availed 
subsidy benefits. In order to realize the real indu strial growth of the region, NEIIPP 
2007 may be modified to exclude service sectors and  focus on manufacturing may be 
given through MSME. 
(vii) NEIIPP is poised to demonstrate huge impact on the industrial development of NER by 
the end of 10 years of operation as envisaged. 
 
2.9.4 Highlights of the recommendations / Suggestio ns given in the report are: 
 

(i) Of the total disbursement as subsidy, 46.6% has gon e to large industries whereas 
53.4% has gone to MSME units. Focus may be given on promotion of MSME.  
(ii) The Government may plan out a cap on subsidy for th e large scale industries to 
enlarge the scope of the policy to reach more number of beneficiaries in MSME sector. 
While large units may continue to be within ambit o f NEIIPP-2007, Comprehensive 
Insurance Subsidy, Central Capital Investment Subsi dy, Interest Subsidy on working 
capital loan, may be limited to investment of Rs. 10 crore on plant and machinery. 
(iii) Slow pace of industrial development in NER is mainl y attributable to lack of 
infrastructure and therefore emphasis may be given on development of infrastructure 
like roads, electricity and water since number of i nitiatives have been taken by DIPP 
for systematic improvement and for clarity in the p olicy guidelines, which are to be 
implemented by the respected state governments. 
(iv) In order to attract more industrial investment, the  state government may create 
provisions for relaxation in inner-line passes, pro tected area permit & restricted areas 
permit.  
(viii)  NEIIPP 2007 should continue and it may be may be aligned with NMP  
(v) Service sector promotion such as IT industries, Cal l Centres, Medical Transcription 
units, BPOs etc. and industries and ventures in tou rism sector should be left to 
respective ministries like the Ministry of IT and Ministry of Tourism. 
(vi) Training should be provided to the Industry Official. 
(vii) Focus may be given to transfer benefits to industri al units in the States of Manipur, 
Mizoram, Nagaland and Sikkim as these States have least benefitted under the policy. 
(viii) Activities may be planned for awareness generation within and outside the States 
about the policy to attract more number of industries in the region. 
(ix) State Governments may be requested for adopting the MIS on e-enablement of subsidy 
schemes developed by DIPP. 
(x) Various committees formed under DIPP guideline for effective implementation and 
monitoring of the policy needs to be strengthened and supported further at State level. 
(xi) In order to ensure a continuous   engagement proces s and possible mid-term 
corrections, DIPP and State Government(s) may conduct periodic review /appraisals to 
take stock of implementation issues and address potential problem areas.

3.1 NORTH EASTERN COUNCIL  
 
Recommendation  
 
3.1.1 The Committee is dismayed with the tentative division of allocated funds in different 
sectors by NEC and is unhappy to see very low alloc ation being made to critically and potentially 
important sectors like health, industries and touri sm. The Committee strongly feels that while it is

(Para 2.3.9 of 186 
th  Report)

3.1.3 The Committee expresses its displeasure on ob serving the declining trend in the Five 
Year Plan allocation to NEC which has limited NEC's  capacity to take up new projects. The

certain part of funds, at least 40% every year for new projects. It must also be cautious in its 
project selection mechanism so as to avoid taking u p projects having huge throw forward 
costs and must ensure timely project implementation . The Committee, therefore, strongly 
recommends that the Ministry of DoNER  may take up the matter of shortfall of actual 
allocation with the Ministry of Finance and demand higher allocations in future under this

3.3 LOAN TO NORTH EASTERN REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MAR KETING 
CORPORATION (NERAMAC) 
 
Recommendation  
 
3.3.1 Food processing units are necessary for value  addition to agricultural produce; prevent 
post-harvest losses and providing better remunerati on to farmers. The Committee is perturbed to 
note that various processing units are lying defunc t and suffering from various ailments. The 
Committee recommends that NERAMAC should guide its efforts to revive these processing units 
by providing assistance for better equipments, technical know-how and affordable finance. 
(Para 2.6.7 ibid)  
Action Taken 
 
3.3.2 The suggestions of the Committee have been no ted. The seasonal nature of the food 
processing units under NERAMAC makes their operatio ns unviable. Further development of farm 
techniques is likely to enable multiple production cycles for fruits and vegetables; large scale 
processing facilities with effective cost reduction  techniques, warehousing, marketing (domestic

3.3.3 The Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry of DoNER should not 
shrug off its responsibility to ensure revival of f ood processing units on the pretext of

plan is required to ensure sustainable operations.    The Committee in this regard suggests 
that in the short run, to counter seasonal nature o f the food items, the Ministry can establish 
cold storage centre and warehouses.  Moreover, mult iple production cycles can be promoted

entire package and take up the matter with the Stat e Government to ensure that such thing does

(Para Nos. 2.10.4 and 2.10.5)

st  installment in respect of 3 projects

Recommendation

stipulated time frame. After the project staff is p ut in place and the project has begun to pick up 
momentum, the budget allocation has been a meager R s.30 crore, which compelled M/o DoNER

nd  quarter of the 2015-16.

3.12 NE ROADS CORPORATION  
 
Recommendation  
 
3.12.1 The delay in incorporation of NE Roads Corpo ration shows a lack of coordination 
between Ministries of DONER and Road, Transport and  Highways. It seems that the accessibility 
and transport issues of NER will keep on suffering due to bureaucratic procedural delays. NITI 
Aayog and Ministry of Finance should also have been  prompt in clearance of the projects.

with this lacklustre approach and recommends that b oth the Ministries must work out the 
formalities at the earliest and begin with the task of identification of projects. 
(Para 2.19.3 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
3.12.2 The Government has announced a new scheme in  the Budget 2014-15 under Central Plan 
with an initial allocation of Rs.200Cr for North Ea st Road Corporation for development of roads 
in NER under Major Head 3601. The objective of the North East Road Sector Development 
Scheme (NERSDS) is to develop road transport sector  in NER by extending financial support for 
construction/upgradation of roads and corridors. NE RSDS aims to fund alternative road link 
between NER and rest of India, road connectivity wi th neighboring countries, strategic 
regional/Inter-state roads and roads required for development of other infrastructure sectors. 
 

3.12.3 However, the concerned line Ministries of D/ o Expenditure and NITI Aayog have 
communicated as below: 
(i) Department of Expenditure: D/o Expenditure have  conveyed that the Cabinet has 
approved the proposal of the MoRTH to set up a Nati onal Highways Connectivity 
Company Ltd (NHCCL), dedicated exclusively to the t ask of constructing/upgrading, etc 
of national highways in parts of the country which share international boundaries with 
neighboring countries in order to promote regional connectivity which would also have a 
special focus in the NE States. DoE conveyed that N ERSDS is not included in the current 
plan. The Budget Speech 2014-15 referred to the inv estment in NHAI of Rs.37,880 Cr 
including Rs.3000Cr in NE. It also concedes that th e scheme will overlap with other 
schemes being implemented by various central and st ate Departments. Therefore, to avoid 
unnecessary administrative/organizational expenditu re and duplication of activities, 
Ministry of DoNER was advised to place the allocate d budget with MoRTH to get suitable 
schemes in consultation with NE States, NEC, MoRTH, etc. Accordingly, Budget Division 
(DEA) was advised to shift the budget line to MoRTH , which is already building roads in 
the North Eastern Region. 
 
(ii)  NITI Aayog: NITI Aayog has conveyed that the Union Finance Minister’s Budget 
Speech indicates provision of Rs.3000Cr for NE Road s. This should suffice. It has stated 
that more than 25 organisations/institutions are in volved in Funding/Constructing/ 
Maintaining Roads in NER. Therefore, there is no justification for introducing another new 
central sector scheme which requires Government fun ding of Rs.600Cr in the current Five 
Year Plan. 
  Action taken by M/DoNER: 
 
(iii) M/DoNER after receiving the comments of NITI Aayog and DoE as above, have 
replied that MDoNER does not wish to create any new  entity but is content to work 
through MORTH and NHIDCL. However, it wishes to cha ir the IMC which will prepare 
lists of works to be executed since NE local priori ties are best left to this 
Ministry.  M/DoNER have repeatedly requested DoE to  convene the EFC meeting so that 
the scheme could be rolled out in the financial yea r 2014-15.  However, no action has been 
taken by DoE or DEA (Budget). Hence, the entire bud get had to be surrendered in 2014-
15.  
 
(iv) As the Budget for NERSDS has increased to Rs.2 25 crore for 2015-16, M/DoNER has 
been reminding DoE to convene EFC meeting at the ea rliest so that the next necessary 
steps such as Cabinet Note etc. can be taken up.  M /DoNER has also communicated to 
Cabinet Secretary for his kind intervention to expe dite the decision of Finance Ministry in 
any matter they consider appropriate.   
 
Further Recommendation 
 
3.12.4 The Committee feels that the Government is n ot taking up the infrastructure issues of 
NER on a priority basis causing delay in implementa tion of related schemes inordinately. 
The Committee fails to understand as to why the EFC  meeting has still not taken place. At 
this pace, it seems that even this year's budget as  well will have to be surrendered. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Governmen t must urgently convene the EFC 
meeting and complete all the pending formalities so  as to roll out the North-East Road 
Sector Development Scheme in the current financial year itself. The Department of 
Expenditure should take immediate action to convene EFC meeting at the earliest.

3.17 BRU TRIBAL FAMILIES’ REPATRIATION AND REHABILI TATION IN 
MIZORAM  
 
Recommendation  
 
3.17.1 The Committee is overwhelmingly concerned th at even after almost two decades the Bru 
tribe is suffering from the aftermath of ethnic vio lence. It is disappointed with the efforts of the 
Governments of Tripura and Mizoram and is worried a bout the fact that till now the complete 
repatriation and rehabilitation of Bru migrants has  not taken place. The Committee recommends 
that Bru migrants must be accorded all support and protection and their repatriation and 
rehabilitation be completed at the earliest. The Co mmittee also recommends that Ministry must 
ensure that shortage of funds must not come in the way of full and final repatriation and complete 
rehabilitation of Bru migrants.  
(Para 3.7.3 ibid)  
Action Taken 
 
3.17.2 MHA have informed that due to ethnic tension  between Reang tribals and Mizos, about 
30,000 Reang (Bru) people (about 5000 families) fro m Western Mizoram migrated from October 
1997 onwards. The Bru migrants are sheltered in the  six relief camps set up in Kanchanpur Sub-
Division of North Tripura. 
 
3.17.3 Ministry of Home Affairs has been extending grants-in-aid to Govt. of Tripura since 1997-
98 for maintenance of of Brus lodged in various rel ief camps for providing relief items like Rice, 
Ration/Cash dole etc and to Govt. of Mizoram for re habilitation and repatriation of Bru migrants 
since 2004-05.As on date approx. Rs 246 crore has b een released to Govt. of Tripura and Rs 40 
crore to Govt. of Mizoram. 
 
3.17.4 As a result of regular follow-up by Ministry  of Home Affairs with the state Govt. of 
Mizoram and Tripura, the repatriation of Bru (Reang ) refugees started in Nov.2010 and (approx. 
7000-8000 people) have been repatriated as on date. 
 
3.17.5 On a PIL filed in the Supreme Court in W.P ( C) 1/2005 by Akhil Bhartiya Vanvasi Kalyan 
Ashram and in W.P. (C) 694/2007 filed by Indigenous  &Tribal People And Ors, the Hon’ble 
Supreme Court in its hearing dated 16-01-2015 has s trongly viewed that the steps taken by the 
central Govt. and the State Govts. Regarding Bru re patriation is highly inadequate. The Hon’ble 
Supreme Court also expressed its strong displeasure  on measures taken to improve the living 
conditions of the Brus in the relief camps in Tripu ra. The  Hon’ble Court further directed to take a 
concrete action plan for early repatriation. 
 
3.17.6 Subsequently a meeting was chaired by JS (NE ), MHA on 30 
th Jan, 2015 to work out the

4.1 NORTH EASTERN COUNCIL - DECREASING ALLOCATION O F FUNDS 
 
Recommendation  
 
4.1.1 The Committee notes with serious concern the trend of decreasing allocation of funds to 
North Eastern Council. The substantial cut in alloc ation at RE stages in consecutive years may be 
a result of non-submission/ late submission of Util ization Certificate by State Governments who in 
turn are unable to do so due to severe weather and heavy monsoon that lead to stoppage of work 
in various projects. The Committee also note that t he assessment period for determining 
budgetary allocation at RE stage, coincides with th e immediate aftermath of the longer monsoon 
season in North East Region. In view of the Committee, this period of assessment is not realistic as 
not only NE Region but also whole country except fe w pockets witness monsoon rains; thus 
causing disruption in construction activities. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of 
Finance should take a realistic and practical appro ach to the important issue of deciding 
supplementary allocations and revised allocations a nd adopt a liberal approach or may desist 
from making any substantial cut while allocating fu nds at RE stage for schemes and projects 
particularly of North East Region. Alternatively, t he Ministry of DoNER may in consultation with 
North Eastern States, NITI Aayog and Ministry of Finance may explore a different mechanism like 
considering a different time period for Northeast r egion having normal weather for assessment of 
utilization of funds and consequent increase/ decrease in allocation at RE stage.

th  Report)

realistic and practical approach while deciding allocations at RE stage.  A reference has been made 
to Ministry of Finance in the matter.  It is felt t hat depending upon the ultimate outcome on the 
same, the question of considering the alternate option could be appropriately considered.

4.11 TOURISM  
 
Recommendation  
4.11.1 The Committee notes the steps taken by the G overnment in promoting tourism in the North 
East Region. However it is of the considered view t hat information dissemination in an attractive, 
convincing and focused manner is necessary to attra ct potential tourists. In this regard, the 
Committee finds that the efforts of Ministry and To urism Departments of State Government are 
not up to the mark. The Committee feels that, to pu blicize the tourism potential, it is not only 
necessary to inform and sensitise the general publi c but also it is required to take in the loop the 
services of major tour operators and agencies in a focused manner because ultimately it is they 
who prepare tourist routes and design packages for the tourists. There is a necessity to establish 
strong linkages of long term nature with the tour o perators and provide them necessary 
information and facilities for promoting NE tourist routes. 
(Para 3.2.5 ibid) 
Recommendation  
 
4.11.2 The committee is disappointed by the officia l tourism websites of the various NE States. It 
feels that the Government needs to ramp up the vari ous official tourism websites of various NE 
States. It is probably the first point of informati on and sometimes the most definitive one for a 
potential tourist from outside North East. The Comm ittee observes that except one or two, most of 
the official tourism website of NE States are lacki ng on various technical parameters like user 
friendliness, ability of being one-stop portal of a ll information, multi-lingual content, optimization 
in mobile and tablet computer formats, online payme nt portals, various set tour packages and 
inter linkage between different websites and servic e providers. Therefore, the Committee 
recommends that the Ministry must ensure that the o fficial tourism websites of different States 
incorporate these critical features. That is so because to attract tourists from regions like west and 
south India and also from other countries, the cont ent and information has to be multi-lingual. 
The Committee observes that most of the websites ar e not multi-lingual and even in case there is 
multi-lingual option available (like Arunachal Prad esh) the approach is poor and not effective. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that professio nal translators may be hired to create a 
vibrant and comprehensive multi-lingual content for the official tourism  
(Para 3.2.6 ibid)  
Recommendation  
 
4.11.3 The Committee feels that development of tour ism requires NER specific as well as 
integrated outlook. While a NE circuit train is sti ll not possible due to lack of decent rail 
connectivity in the region, however, the efforts fo r the conceptualization and planning for the 
same must be started right away. The Committee reco mmends that a special circuit train by the 

name of ‘North-East Seven Sisters Circuit’ or other such name be conceptualized and planning for 
the same may be started so as to reap the benefits as soon as the capitals of all the NE states are 
connected by the railway network. 
(Para 3.2.7 ibid)  
Recommendation  
 
4.11.4 The Committee is surprised at the exclusion of important Buddhist cities of NER from the 
Buddhist Circuit. It feels that including sites lik e Rumtek, Kalimpong in Sikkim and Tawang, 
Bomdila in Arunachal Pradesh can help increase tour ism prospects in these regions. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry must identif y specially focused projects to develop these 
sites and augment their capacity to attract as well  as sustain increased tourist inflow. The 
Ministry must also explore a way to include them in the Buddhist tourist circuit. 
(Para 3.2.8 ibid)  
Action Taken 
 
4.11.5 Ministry of Tourism are in the process of fo rmulating a comprehensive National Tourism 
Policy during 2015.  Ministry of DoNER has already communicated the views of the Hon’ble 
Committee to Ministry of Tourism so that the same are taken into account appropriately by them.

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE
GOVERNMENT
1.1 DEMAND NO. 56
Recommendation
1.1.1 The Committee strongly recommends that the Government must give emphasis on return of
migrants to the valley. (Para 3.3.18)
Action Taken
1.1.2 The Government is committed to facilitate the return of the Kashmiri migrants to the
Kashmir V alley and their proper rehabilitation there. The Government has earmarked `320 crore for
the rehabilitation of the Kashmiri Migrants in the Union Budget of 2015-16.
1.1.3 An integrated proposal for the return and rehabilitation of the Kashmiri migrants is also
being prepared in consultation with the stakeholders.
Further Recommendation
1.1.4 The committee while acknowledging the efforts of the Government of India
recommends that the initiatives of the Government should reflect on the ground.
Recommendation
1.1.5 The Committee took note of the fact that under Plan Scheme “Special Industry Initiative
for J&K”, the Ministry had projected 
` 130.00 crore in 2014-15, however, it was allocated ` 90.00
crore in BE 2014-15 which was further reduced to ` 52.45 crore at RE stage.  The Committee
observes with dismay that in spite of the 100% utilization of funds under this scheme, the Finance
Ministry has allocated a meager amount of ` 45.00 crore for this scheme against projected demand
of ` 120.00 crore for 2015-16.  The Committee recommends that the Finance Ministry should look
positively into  the projected demand of ` 120 crore of the Ministry while sanctioning additional
amount at RE stage as this scheme is targeted to bring back Kashmiri youths into mainstream so
that they do not fall prey to anti national activities. (Para 3.3.19)
Action Taken
1.1.6 Depending upon the pace of expenditure, proposal for additional amount will be submitted
to Ministry of Finance, at the RE stage.
1.2 DEPRESSION IN CAPFs
Recommendation
1.2.1 The Committee is sympathetic to the desperate situation of paramilitary forces personnel.
2

3
The Committee feels that the Government should look into their agonies through which they pass
while working in difficult circumstances.  The Committee understands that when the personnel of
paramilitary forces pass thorough stress and feel de-motivated and demoralized it would have far
reaching negative repercussions.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should
look into the long pending grievances of the paramilitary personnel and address them in a time
bound manner. (Para 4.3.6)
Action Taken
1.2.2 On receipt of the grievance from the serving/retired personnel or from their spouse or from
NOKs of the deceased personnel regarding maintenance of family, non receipt of pension/family
pension, and other terminal dues etc., the same is forwarded to all concerned offices i.e. Sector,
Range, Group Centre and unit with the instructions to settle their grievances within prescribed time
frame. The applicant is also apprised with the factual position/ status with reference to his/her
grievance within the stipulated time.
1.2.3 Further, the Force Headquarters also take care of the personal grievances of the officials
regarding their promotions/transfers and other related service matters through personal audiences,
representations/ petitions etc.
Recommendation
1.2.4 The Committee understands that years of working in hostile conditions by CAPFs personnel
and staying away from their family, long working hours, sleep deprivation, denial of leave, etc.
take a toll on their lives.  The Committee recommends that the paramilitary forces should introduce
Yoga and other stress management techniques in the CAPFs to de-stress these personnel. The
Committee also recommends that the personnel long posted in difficult areas should be transferred
to relatively normal area after a fixed duration. Special allowances aspect should also be examined.
(Para 4.3.7)
Action Taken
1.2.5 Sufficient periods of Yoga and Stress Management have been included in the Training
Syllabus in order to promote the Yoga and to de-stress the CAPFs personnel working in
uncongenial condition and far flung areas.
1.2.6 As regards posting of the personnel from difficult areas to relatively normal areas after a
fixed duration, it is submitted that each CAPF has a transfer policy for rotational transfer of its
personnel between hard and soft/static locations. The transfer policy is followed uniformly in the
Force. Choice postings given by the Force personnel are considered by the Force to post them at
the desired place of posting as far as practicable and administratively possible.
Further Recommendation
1.2.7 The Committee is of opinion that these techniques should not only become part of
training syllabus but also be added in their everyday routine. Regarding transfer posting in
these forces, the Committee hopes that mechanism to decide over  choice postings remains
transparent and free from nepotism etc.

4
1.3 SENSITISATION TOWARDS ETHICAL AND MORAL VALUES
Recommendation
1.3.1 The Committee notes the submissions made by the Home Secretary and Delhi Police
Commissioner for making Delhi Police a true reflection of cosmopolitan composition of Delhi
Police.  The Committee recommends that the recruitment to the posts of constabulary should also
be done by Staff Selection Commission (SSC) as has been done in the case of post of Sub-
Inspectors. The recruitment on the basis of All India test conducted by SSC in itself is a practical
solution in this regard where people from the whole country can apply. The Committee hopes that
Delhi Police would soon have all India character and be more representative and broad based.
(Para 4.4.32)
Action Taken
1.3.2 In order to give the Delhi Police a true cosmopolitan character, the Delhi Police is going
to get online exam of Delhi Police Constable (Executive) on All India basis through Staff Selection
Commission as is being done in case of Sub-Inspector (Exe.). Recently the Senior Officers of
Delhi Police had attended a meeting in DOPT on 11.05.2015 for online exam through SSC. In the
meeting it was decided to prepare MOU in this regard.  Further steps are being taken by Delhi
Police on priority basis.

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS ON WHICH
THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE THE MATTER
IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
2.1 OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF DEMANDS FOR GRANTS
Recommendation
2.1.1 The Committee notes the courses of actions undertaken by the Government in terms of
maintaining internal security scenario in the country. The Committee also notes the submission that
multi pronged strategies being followed in the short and medium term have led to a declining trend
in the level of Left Wing violence as well as the resultant killings since 2011. The Committee,
however, desires that the Ministry of Home Affairs as per its topmost priority should strive
diligently to improve the capacity infrastructure of Central Para Military Forces and upgrade the
much necessary institutional mechanisms for further enhancing internal security of the country.
(Para 2.17)
Action Taken
2.1.2 The Central Government has adopted an integrated approach to deal with the problem of
Left Wing Extremism (LWE) simultaneously pursuing the issues relating to security, development,
enforcement of rights and entitlements of local communities and public perception management.
The State Governments spearhead all efforts to control the LWE activities in the States. The Central
Government closely monitors the situation and supplements the efforts of the State Governments
over a wide range of security and development related interventions. The underlying philosophy is
to enhance the capacity of the State Governments to tackle the menace of LWE in a concerted
manner.
2.1.3 Apart from providing Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) battalions to assist the State
Police Forces in counter-LWE operations, the Government of India has been providing assistance
for capacity building of the States through the Security Related Expenditure (SRE) Scheme, the
Special Infrastructure Scheme and the Scheme for Construction/ Strengthening of Fortified Police
Stations.
2.1.4 At present, a total of 110 battalions of CAPFs are provided to the States of Andhra Pradesh,
Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh
and West Bengal in counter-LWE operations.
2.1.5 It is the belief of Government of India that through a combination of security and
development related interventions, the LWE problem can be successfully contained. It is worth
mentioning that due to the measures adopted by the Government, LWE violence has significantly
declined in the last four years i.e. 2011 to 2014.
5

6
Institutional Mechanism: -
2.1.6 State Governments are primarily responsible for Law and Order, countering internal
disturbances, terrorists and naxalite activities. The CAPFs are made available to the State
Governments on the latter’s request to assist them in maintenance of public order.  As per SOP ,
during deployment, infrastructure and other logistics are provided by the State
Government However, before any deployment of CAPFs on long term basis, a joint meeting of all
the stake holders is organized to firm up the infrastructural plan and deployment plan of CAPFs.
CAPFs are deployed once the requisite infrastructure outlined in the SOP is put in place by the
State Government concerned. Further, there is a mechanism of quarterly meeting of Joint Audit of
CAPFs and the State Governments about the review of the operations as well as infrastructure. The
report of the joint audit are further reviewed in MHA and corrective measures are undertaken to
further strengthen the infrastructure required. The periodical review is aimed at ensuring the
optimum utilization of the CAPFs in the overall interest of the internal security of the country. 
2.1.7 To improve the basic infrastructure of CAPFs and upgrade essential institutional
mechanisms for further enhancing internal security of the country, during 12
th Five Year Plan,
(financial years 2012-13, 2013-14 and 2014-15), 15306 nos. of dwelling units and 278 nos. of
Barracks were targeted for construction. Out of this 9379 nos. of dwelling units and 245 nos. of
Barracks have been constructed till 31.03.2015. For remaining financial year 2015-16 and 2016-17,
8900 nos. of dwelling units and 160 nos. of Barracks have been targeted for construction.
Recommendation
2.1.8 The Committee notes the national policy and action plan document which adopted an
integrated strategy comprising security related measures, development related measures, ensuring
rights and entitlements related measures and public perception management to contain Left Wing
Extremism in the country.  The Committee understands that only security related measures cannot
check growth of Left Wing Extremism. It should go along with development measures and
strategies. (Para 2.18)
Action Taken
2.1.9 The National Policy and Action Plan to address LWE problem has been documented with
the approval of the Union Home Minister and has been sent to States and other stakeholders for
its implementation. The policy document has adopted an integrated four pronged strategy
comprising Security related measures, Development related measures, ensuring Rights and
Entitlements related measures and Public Perception Management.
2.1.10 Development remains a key prong of National strategy and Ministries of the Central
Government as well as the State Governments are working in synergy towards this end. Some
important development initiatives currently under implementation are:-
(a) Road Requirement Plan;
(b) Improvement of Rail Connectivity;
(c) Installation of Mobile Towers project;
(d) Improvement of education and health infrastructure;

7
(e) Minimum Support Price (MSP) for minor forest produce;
(f) Support for Adivasi festivals/ cultural programmes; and
(g) Increased reach of All India Radio (AIR/FM) and Doordarshan in LWE affected
areas.
Recommendation
2.1.11 The Committee is of the opinion that the development of socio-economic infrastructure and
services such as schools, Primary Health Centres, roads, bridges, etc. should go hand in hand with
security operations in Left Wing Extremism Affected areas. The Committee is of the considered view
that providing basic infrastructure and other facilities can help check growth of influence of left
wing extremism in these areas. (Para 2.19)
Action Taken
2.1.12 The Central Government has adopted an integrated approach to deal with the menace of
Left Wing Extremism (LWE) in the areas of security, development, enforcing rights and
entitlements of local communities and public perception management. The State Governments
specifically deal with various issues related to LWE activities in the States. The Central Government
closely monitors the situation and supplements the efforts of the State Governments over a wide
range of measures both on security and development fronts.
2.1.13 On the development front, the Central Government is implementing special schemes like the
Road Requirement Plan for improvement of roads, projects for installation of mobile towers,
improvement of rail connectivity, education and health infrastructure in the LWE affected areas.
2.1.14 The scheme titled ‘Additional Central Assistance (ACA) for LWE affected districts’ is also
under implementation for accelerated development of the affected areas. The aim of this initiative
is to provide public infrastructure and services such as School Buildings, Anganwadi Centres,
Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Drinking Water Supply, Village Roads, Electric Lights in public
places such as PHCs and schools etc. in the affected/contiguous districts. As on 19.5.2015, a total
amount of ` 9,059.00 crore of central fund has been released under the ACA to the 88 districts
covered under the Scheme and against which an expenditure of ` 8,450.85 crore (93.29 %) has
been reported. The number of Projects completed so far under the ACA is 1,32,708. However, as
a policy decision starting from the year 2015-16, it has been left to the States to continue with
this scheme out of their increased resources in consequence of the recommendation of the 14
th
Finance Commission.
2.2 DEMAND NO. 53 - MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS
Recommendation
2.2.1 The Committee in this connection also notes that the proposal for issuance of National
Identity Card to the Citizens of India, who are of age 18 years and above, is under consideration.
The Committee feels proposal of  having National Identity Card to the Citizens of India  needs
to be examined  keeping in mind  presence of successful Voter I Card scheme, which is given to

8
the citizens of India of 18 years age and above. The Committee also understands that linking of
Aadhar numbers with the voter I-cards is underway and therefore voter I cards will also have
biometric details. In view of the Committee, this arrangement seems sufficient. The Committee
therefore desires that all possible steps should be taken to avoid the duplication of efforts between
different agencies of the Government as well as avoidable expenditure from public exchequer.
(Para 3.1.9)
Action Taken
2.2.2 The Citizenship Act 1955 was amended in 2004 by inserting Section 14A which inter-alia
provides for the following:
z The Central Government may compulsorily register every citizen of India and issue
National Identity Card to them.
z The Central Government may maintain a National Register of Indian Citizens (NRIC)
and for that purpose establish a National Registration Authority (NRA).
2.2.3 Accordingly, the creation of National Population Register (NPR), the first building block
towards carving out NRIC, has been undertaken as per the provisions of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
The demographic data for NPR has already been collected for the entire country in 2010 and got
digitized, thereby creating an electronic database of approx. 119 crore persons. Biometric enrolment
has been completed for more than 28.42 crore persons.
2.2.4 To minimize the duplication of efforts, in terms of the capture of biometrics, a synergy was
developed between NPR & UIDAI. 12 States/ UTs were given to NPR and 24 States/ UTs to
UIDAI for biometric enrolment. Further, if a person indicates she/ he is already enrolled for
aadhaar, the biometric data was not captured for NPR instead the aadhaar number was recorded
to source the biometric data from UIDAI.
2.2.5 W ith regard to other databases already in place, viz., Ration Card, Passport, Driving License
etc. in general and Election Commission of India’s Electoral Rolls in particular, which are provided
to Citizens of India,  these are based on self verification and not on physical verification at the
ground level.  Accordingly, after due deliberations within the Government, a decision was taken by
the Government to let the NPR complete its mandate by scrupulously following the laid down
approved procedures in the statute book.
2.2.6 The proposal to carve out NRIC from NPR is under consideration of the Government.
This would further address national security concerns and facilitate more effective execution of
social programmes and ensure a robust delivery mechanism.
Recommendation
2.2.7 The Committee recommends that the allocation under NCRMP should be enhanced at RE
stage as to address cyclone risks and mitigation in two States – Odisha and Andhra Pradesh during
phase I of this scheme and  also for Phase - II where States like West Bengal, Kerala and four
other States are to be taken up.  The Committee feels that 
` 416 crores is much lower than what
was projected by  the Ministry which already have liability of over ` 100 crores of the previous
year to be met out of allocation made in this fiscal year . (Para 3.1.12)

9
Action Taken
2.2.8 MHA had requested for Budget allocation of `783 crore for the current financial year.  Only
416 crore has been allocated.
2.2.9 However, the additional demand for funds will be made at RE stage if required for NCRMP
Phase-I & II.
2.3 DEMAND NO. 56
Recommendation
2.3.1 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry but would like to be informed whether the
Government is satisfied with infrastructure facilities in the refugee camps for which no allocation
has been sought or made as claimed by the Ministry. The Committee, while noting that relief camps
in State of Tamil Nadu and Odisha for Sri Lankan refugees have been running successfully with
full Central Assistance, recommends that the Government should also pursue with State
Governments of Tamil Nadu and Odisha to fast pace relief measures for Sri Lankan refugees
staying in camps in their respective States. (Para 3.3.7)
2.3.2 The Committee also desires that visit of inter-ministerial delegation to the camps in both
States may be organized at the earliest. (Para 3.3.7)
Action Taken
2.3.3 The Government of India has already provided funds to the State Government of Tamil
Nadu for infrastructure facilities in the refugee camps as per the demand made by the State
Government. There is no fresh demand for infrastructure facilities in the camps either from the
State Government of Tamil Nadu or Odisha. The relief materials are being given to the Sri Lankan
Tamil Refugees staying in the camps as per the approved rate and quantity.
2.3.4 Regarding the visit of inter-ministerial delegation to the camps, this Ministry had requested
the Ministry of External Affairs and also the Government of Tamil Nadu vide its letters dated
13.05.2013 and dated 21.05.2013 respectively to finalize the programme for visit of the Inter-
Ministerial delegation to the Sri Lankan Tamil refugee camps in Tamil Nadu. The Ministry of
External Affairs vide their letter dated 15.05.2013 had also written to the Government of Tamil
Nadu in this regard. Further, the Home Secretary in his D.O. letter 17.01.2014 had also requested
the Foreign Secretary to fix a suitable date for the proposed visit of the Inter-Ministerial delegation
to the Sri Lankan refugee camps in Tamil Nadu. The Government of Tamil Nadu has reported that
the voluntary repatriation could be considered only after concrete and credible measures taken by
Sri Lankan Government and as such, repatriation at this stage is pre-mature and should be deferred
for the present. The Ministry of External Affairs has again been requested vide this Ministry’s letter
dated 23.07.2015 to organize the Inter-Ministerial Delegation to both the states of Tamil Nadu and
Odisha at the earliest.
2.4 DEMAND NO. 56
Recommendation
2.4.1 The Committee is dismayed to note that discrepancies crept in disbursal of Central Samman
pension by the banks due to confusion about the policy of Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension

10

3.1 OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF DEMANDS FOR GRANTS
Recommendation
3.1.1 In principle, the Committee is in favour of the financial autonomy of the States as
recommended by the 14
th Finance Commission. However, the Committee is of the considered view
that the matter of national pursuits ranging from national security to territorial integrity cannot
be left at the dispensation of the State Governments alone with no monitoring and accountability
of Union Government in spite of clear constitutional mandate to the Union Government to the
effect. As also highlighted by the Home Secretary that the issue of transferring the national security
related Scheme to the States should be reviewed and the Central Government must have a say in
the matter of national importance, particularly pertaining to internal security. The Committee is of
the considered view that the Government must be cautious while transferring such schemes/ projects/
plans having grave national ramifications, to the States so that national security is not
compromised in the name of the financial autonomy to the States. Moreover, the Committee strongly
recommends that even if any centrally Sponsored Scheme is transferred to the States, the Central
Government must have resilient monitoring mechanism over the progress of implementation of those
schemes. The Committee recommends that the Finance Ministry should positively look into the
matter and reconsider its decision of transferring eight Centrally Sponsored Schemes of MHA
merged into an Umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme called ‘National Scheme for Modernization
of Police and other Forces’. (Para 2.10)

th Finance Commission, budget allocation of eight major
