3.7.5 The Committee is not satisfied with the reply given in the context of action taken against
erring officials not registering FIRs. The Committee believes that the number of instances when
police officials refuse or discourage to register FIR may be bigger than what has been claimed
officially. The victims out of fear do not complain against police officials. The Committee is
displeased to note that during the last two years (2013 & 2014) out of 30 and 20 complaints, only
two complaints were found to be genuine. The Committee smells a rat here and finds that this is
a clear case of conflict of interest where police officials themselves are investigating such cases.
It would be better if complaints of non-registration of FIRs are inquired by an independent body.
The Committee is of the considered view that there is an urgent need to have an independent body
consisting of civil society groups, judiciary, etc. to look into such cases and stringent action must
be taken against the officials  for not registering or discouraging people who come for registering
FIRs as just seeking of explanation is not going to serve any purpose. The Committee in this
connection is also of the view that a police station is a vital organ of the society and its
responsibility and duties to the society are of very much significance for maintaining law & order .
In the absence of police system, the society may turn into anarchy. The Committee, therefore, feels
that social audit of police system is the need of the hour and the Government may think consider
social audit of policing in the country to improve its functioning in a transparent manner.
(Para 4.4.22)
Action Taken
3.7.6 In all the 50 cases, where FIRs are not lodged by the concerned police stations, the
complainant made a call to Vigilance Unit for registration of FIR.  All these calls were thereafter
referred to the concerned districts and, in turn, their replies were received mentioning therein that
in all the 50 cases wherever a cognizable case was made out, FIRs have already been registered

30
in the concerned police stations.  It was also intimated that the allegations of non-registration
leveled in these 50 complainants were duly enquired into independently by an ACP-rank officer, and
in 48 cases the allegations were not substantiated since there was no willful or negligent delay in
the concerned police stations.  In 2 cases, however, allegations have been substantiated and action
against the erring police officials has already been taken.
3.7.7 As and when information is received in the Vigilance Unit regarding inaction in registering
FIR, an Action Taken Report is immediately taken from the District concerned. The Vigilance Unit
is an independent Unit which monitors complaints against police personnel. This is in addition to
the option available to the complainant to directly approach local police authorities at senior level
and have necessary action taken on their complaint.
3.7.8 At present, Delhi Police has an inbuilt mechanism to address complaints of non-registration
of FIR.  Apart from the Vigilance Unit of Delhi Police, all supervisory officers of the Districts and
Ranges promptly look into any complaint of non-registration of cases. Complaints of non-
registration are also scrutinized in the Police Headquarters and the defaulting staff are identified for
suitable corrective action.  Calling of explanation is mandatory as the officer needs to be given an
opportunity to explain the reasons for not registering the FIR. If the reasons are not found
convincing, based on the seriousness of the situation, further necessary departmental action is
taken.
3.7.9 As for constitution of independent body to look into such complaints, at present Delhi
Police is accountable to several Commissions such as National Human Rights Commission, Public
Grievances Commission, Central Vigilance Commission, etc. and complaints of non-registration are
also monitored by the Courts of Law.
Further Recommendation
3.7.10 The committee is dismayed to note that out of 50 complaints for not lodging of FIRs,
only 2 complaints were found to be genuine. The committee is not convinced with the
information provided and  surprised to find that complainants made complains for non-
registration of their FIRs and it was found by vigilance unit that FIRs were already lodged
in respective police stations which indicates that even though a FIR was lodged the
complainant made complaint that FIR was not lodged which apparently seems unacceptable.
The Committee would like to be apprised of time and date of such complaints and FIRs
lodged in such cases. The committee reiterates its earlier recommendation that there should
be non-official Members of vigilance unit drawn from other government agencies, human
rights organizations, civil society organizations etc. to look into such complaint. It is then
only, impartiality and proper check and balance can be ensured and conflict of interest can
be avoided.

4.5 SENSITISATION TOWARDS ETHICAL AND MORAL VALUES
Recommendation
4.5.1 The Committee raised the issue of duty hours of Delhi police personnel and allowances paid
for extra working hours. The Commissioner of Police, Delhi replied that officially there is fixed
duty hour, however, it is not possible to follow. He added that there is no provision of
compensatory leave and extra working hours allowances to Delhi Police personnel. The Committee
understands that in view of the nature of work, it is not practically possible to follow fixed duty
hours in Delhi Police. However, the Committee feels that the police personnel working extra hours
should be given allowance/compensation, etc. to keep them motivated. Subject to the exigency of
work, there should also be provision for compensatory leave for personnel deployed during
holidays. (Para 4.4.33)
Action Taken
4.5.2 In 1979, the Government of India sanctioned one month’s extra pay as compensatory pay
to the non-gazetted police personnel of Delhi Police in lieu of performing long hours of duty and
their inability to avail themselves of the holidays and weekly off days as they are not only required
to be on duty on most of the public holidays like Republic Day, Independence Day, Dussehra,
Diwali and Moharram etc. but also have to put in extra hours of work so as to maintain public
peace and order. Further, the police personnel, on a number of occasions, are not able to avail
holidays even on Sundays. Restrictions are also imposed on grant of casual leave/earned leave
depending upon the prevailing law and order.  Thus, the number of days of extra work put in by
Delhi Police personnel is much more than the compensatory pay of 30 days payable to the rank
of Constable to Inspector.

35
4.5.3 Besides this, the pay scales of police personnel in the UT of Chandigarh and in the State
of Punjab are higher than what are being paid in Delhi. Pay scales of police personnel in U.P . are
more or equivalent to that of Delhi Police. All these three UT/States are giving one month’s pay
as compensatory pay to their police personnel in addition to other benefits which are not available
to Delhi Police.
4.5.4 Commitments of Delhi Police have also increased manifold. The terrorists activities and
threats to VVIPs and other persons, to be provided with security of Delhi Police under various
categories, have been increasing day by day. Similarly, the number of agitations, demonstrations/
processions and other law & order situations have been on the increase all through and more so
during recent times.
4.5.5 In view of above, a proposal to enhance the compensatory pay upto 60 days in a calendar
year for all the ranks of Delhi Police has been submitted by Delhi Police to 7
th Central Pay
Commission for their recommendation.

Action Taken
ANDAMAN & NICOBAR
4.8.2 At present 05 vessels of various capacities are being operated in inter-island sector for

their economic life span and taking into account the facts mentioned above the Ship Acquisition
Committee of MoS recommended acquisition of 4x500 pax vessels for improving connectivity in

Scheme have been transferred to the State Governments. Out of these components, Modernization
of State Police Forces, Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS) to ensure
centralized database for crimes and criminals, and special infrastructure scheme for LWE are

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
recommendations contained in its One Hundred Eighty Third Report on the Problems being Faced
by Refugees and Displaced Persons in J&K. The said Report was presented to the Rajya Sabha
on 22nd December, 2014 and laid on the Table of the Lok Sabha on 22nd December, 2014.
2. Action Taken Notes were received from the Ministry of Home Affairs in respect of the
recommendations contained in the Report on 24th June, 2015 whereupon Rajya Sabha Secretariat
vide its communication dated 5th November, 2015 forwarded a detailed questionnaire to the
Ministry of Home Affairs which in turn furnished the replies thereof on 4th December, 2015.  The
Committee considered the Action Taken Notes and the said replies of the Ministry and the same
have been categorized as under:
Chapter-I: The Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 3.2.4.3, 3.2.5.4, 3.2.6.3, 3.2.15.3, 3.2.16.3, 3.3.4.3, 3.3.5.3 and 3.3.6.3
(of One Hundred and Seventy Third Report)  Total Recommendations - 8
The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations
as mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report.
Chapter-II: The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue
in view of the Government’s replies: Para Nos. 3.2.7.3, 3.2.12.3, 3.2.13.3, 3.2.11.2
and 3.3.3.3 (ibid) Total Recommendations - 5
The Committee is convinced with the explanations furnished by the Ministry and,
therefore, does not want to pursue the recommendations further.
Chapter-III: The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee is not
satisfied with the replies of the Ministry: Para Nos. 3.1.1.6, 3.1.2.3, 3.1.3.3, 3.1.3.4,
3.1.4.2, 3.1.5.3, 3.1.6.3, 3.1.7.3, 3.2.1.4, 3.2.2.3, 3.2.3.3, 3.2.3.4, 3.2.5.5, 3.2.8.3,
3.2.16.4, 3.2.17.3, 3.2.18.3, 3.2.19.3, 3.3.1.3, 3.3.2.3, 3.3.7.3, 3.3.8.3 and 3.3.9.3
(ibid) Total Recommendations - 23
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of its
recommendations contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should
furnish convincing explanations in respect of those recommendations.
Chapter-IV: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government
have not been received: Para Nos. 3.2.9.3, 3.2.10.3 and 3.2.14.7 (ibid)  Total
Recommendations - 3
In respect of three recommendations in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished
interim reply or couched its response in vague terms. Therefore, the Committee
desires that the Ministry should furnish pointed and detailed Action Taken Notes in
respect of the recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in keeping with the spirit
of the recommendations.
3. The details of the A TRs have been analyzed in various Chapters in the succeeding chapters.

CHAPTE-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED
BY THE GOVERNMENT
1.1 ONE TIME COMPENSATION
1.1.1 The Committee desires that one time compensation of ` 30 Lakh may be included in the
package and Ministry may ensure that the package is finalized.
                                                 (Para 3.2.4.3 of the 183 rd Report)
Action Taken
1.1.2 The Government of J&K has sent a proposal for one time settlement of displaced Persons
from PoJK, 1947 and Chhamb Displaced Persons of 1965 and 1971 wars to this Ministry. The
Ministry vide its letter dated 21.11.2014 has requested the State Government of J&K to send
certain more information with regard to the DPs of PoJK and DPs of Chhamb 1965 and 1971.
This Ministry has also requested the State Government to send one time proposal in respect of
WPRs also.
1.1.3 The Ministry of Home Affairs further informed the Committee that the required information
has not been furnished by the Government of J&K.  However, they have been again requested vide
letter dated 10.11.2015 to furnish the requisite information.
Further Observation
1.1.4 The Committee appreciates the initiative taken by the Ministry of Home Affairs for
seeking proposals for one time settlement of DPs from PoJK 1947 and Chhamb DPs of 1965
and 1971 as well WPRs and desires that all necessary action must be taken within a set
time frame, as all these affected persons continue to lead their lives under depression due
to extreme suffering. Any positive action on the part of the Government would be of great
satisfaction to them.
Recommendation
1.2 SLOW DISBURSAL OF COMPENSATION
1.2.1 The Committee expresses its deep concern that the payment of compensation in respect
of fund/package sanctioned in 2008 is being implemented at snail pace affecting the lives
of PoJK DPs. The process should have been completed much earlier. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Union Government must pursue the matter with the State Government
to expedite the implementation of the package without further delay. (Para 3.2.5.4)
Action Taken
1.2.2 For expediting disbursal of compensation to the beneficiaries, meeting with State
Government Officers is being held on monthly basis. A committee under the Chairmanship of
Divisional Commissioner Jammu is in place for monitoring the progress of implementation of the
2

3
scheme. During 12-14 February, 2015, the Officers of this Ministry visited Jammu and had meeting
with the State Government Officers in which 47 land deficiency claims and 14 applications for
cash in lieu  of urban plots have been approved.
1.2.3 In response to a question as to the status of approved 47 land deficiency claims and 14
applicants for cash in lieu  of urban plots, the Ministry of Home Affairs apprised the Committee
that the Government of J&K has reported that about 10 cases of compensation in lieu  of urban
plots and 10 cases of compensation in lieu   of deficiency of land are in all respects complete but
are pending  for want of transfer of fund from State Headquarter to field office.   In other cases,
it has been reported that the list of approved cases was published through print media. However,
the responses from the claimant are not adequate.
Further Observation
1.2.4 The Committee hopes that all approved 47 land deficiency claims and 14 applicants
for cash in lieu  of urban plots are settled in a dedicated time frame.  Central Government
may pursue the matter with the State Government.
Recommendation
1.3 INCLUSION OF POJK DPS IN DIALOGUE ON J&K
1.3.1 The Committee is of the view that this demand needs to be examined cautiously.
The Committee feels that concerns of the displaced persons of PoJK should be taken into
consideration before addressing their grievances for redressal.  The channel for discussion
with the representatives should be kept open so that they may have no feeling of being
neglected. (Para 3.2.6.3)
Action Taken
1.3.2 The Government has encouraged policies to ensure sustained peace process and to provide
adequate opportunities to all sections of the people in the State who eschew violence to effectively
represent their view points and to redress their genuine grievances.  Regarding the concerns of the
displaced persons of PoJK who migrate/ came to J&K in 1947 being taken into consideration,
channels for discussions with the representatives is open, so that they have no feeling of being
neglected.
Recommendation
1.4 OPENING OF JAMMU – SIALKOT ROAD
1.4.1 The Committee is in agreement with the view of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.
Efforts may be made to open Jammu-Sialkot road for trade and other activities through the
diplomatic channels. (Para 3.2.15.3)
Action Taken
1.4.2 The Task Force on National Security (TFNS) had recommended for opening of 9 additional
routes including the Jammu- Sialkot for cross LoC Trade and Travels as per the recommendation
of the Joint Working Group II. Comments/ Views were called for from the State Government but

4
the same is still awaited.  The issue regarding opening of additional routes for cross LoC Trade
and Travel was also considered in the meeting held on 26.06.2014 under the Chairmanship of
Financial Commissioner, Industries and Commerce, Government of J&K and again in the meeting
dated 05.01.2015 held under the chairmanship of JS(J&K). It was decided that the State
Government of J&K should send a proposal with detailed justification in this regard to MHA. The
proposal is still awaited from the State Government of J&K.  Further, the recommendation of the
Task Force on National Security (TFNS) for opening of 9 additional routes including the Jammu-
Sialkot for cross LoC Trade and Travels as recommended by the Joint Working Group-II has also
been taken up with MEA requesting them to take up the matter at appropriate level.
Recommendation
1.5 ACTUAL LINE OF CONTROL CERTIFICATES
1.5.1 The Committee feels that the need of issuance of ALC Certificate to DP families of
1947 staying in the vicinity of border areas in Jammu may be taken up due to the fact that
such certificate would enable the DPs to avail the benefits of reservation by proving that
they are the residents of areas falling under ALC.  Mere notification might not be sufficient
for proof.  Government should arrange for issuance of ALC Certificates to DP families of
1947. (Para 3.2.16.3)
Action Taken
1.5.2 The benefit of reservation is being provided to such persons who settled along the ALC by
the State Government. The areas falling under ALC have already been notified by the State
Government of J&K. The State Government has been requested that arrangement should be made
for issuance of ALC Certificates to the DP families of 1947.
Recommendation
1.6 RESERV ATION IN EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS AND EMPLOYMENT
1.6.1 The Committee recommends that wards of displaced persons of 1965 and 1971 may
be given preference for getting admission in educational institutions as a level – playing
mechanism. The Government may consider the request of DPs of 1965 and 1971 for
reservation for employment in Government jobs to ensure guaranteed means of livelihood.
Employment drive for the youths belonging to PoJK DPs should also be conducted. Since the
State Government has agreed to consider request for reservation to DPs living within
notified backward areas, the Committee recommends that an early decision may be taken
in the matter. (Para 3.3.4.3)
Action Taken
1.6.2 The benefit of reservation is being provided by the State Government to such persons who
have settled along the ALC. The areas falling under ALC have already been notified.
Recommendation
1.7 ISSUANCE OF ALC CERTIFICATES
1.7.1 The Committee feels that due to lack of awareness and low level of education, the

5
DPs may be finding difficult to follow procedure in getting ALC Certificates. The Procedure
for getting ALC certificates could be cumbersome, and if it is so, the procedure may be
simplified and a drive may be undertaken to encourage eligible DPs for procuring ALC
certificates. (Para 3.3.5.3)
Action Taken
1.7.2 The benefit of reservation is being provided by the State Government to such persons who
have settled along the ALC. The areas falling under ALC have already been notified.
Recommendation
1.8 CONSTITUTION OF DEVELOPMENT BOARD-
1.8.1 The Committee is of the view that plethora of institutional arrangement  is not going
to ameliorate the conditions of DPs as the same would complicate the system causing delay
in seeking justice. Therefore, an institutional structure should be created to address all the
issues of DPs at a single window. (Para 3.3.6.3)
Action Taken
1.8.2 The State Government has informed that there is a separate organization, headed by the
Provincial Rehabilitation Officer, Jammu for extending the benefits of rehabilitation of PoJK DPs,
which is under the charge of Custodian, Evacuee Property in the State of J&K.

CHAPTER - II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS ON WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT
DESIRE TO PURSUE THE MATTER IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
Recommendation
2.1 CONSTITUTION OF WELFARE AND RELIEF COMMISSION/ DEVELOPMENT BOARD:
2.1.1 The Committee understands that the demands of the representatives of PoJK DP of
1947 for constitution of a Welfare and Relief Commission/ Board for DPs of PoJK, 1947 can
be attributed to the reason that the existing office meant for addressing their problems is not
functioning effectively. The committee, therefore, recommends that a Welfare and Relief
Commission/ Development Board with adequate infrastructure may be constituted in view of
the large number of people involved and number of issues to be addressed. (Para 3.2.7.3)
Action Taken
2.1.2 The State Government has informed that at present there is no proposal for constitution of
Development Board.
Recommendation
2.2 GRANTING STATE SUBJECT TO POJK REFUGEES LIVING OUTSIDE THE STATE
2.2.1 The Committee desires that the matter may be discussed with the representatives of
PoJK DPs for solution. The Committee also desires that one nodal officer may be appointed
in Delhi for granting Permanent Resident Certificates status to PoJK DPs living outside the
State of J&K as being done for Kashmiri migrants.  A campaign may be initiated to attract
more and more PoJK DPs living in other parts of the country by issuing advertisements in
national dailies and the rules for applying the Permanent Resident Certificate may be
simplified. (Para 3.2.12.3)
Action Taken
2.2.2 The State subjects are being issued as per the J&K Permanent Residence Certificate Act
(PRC).  Any person who has been or who is resident of State and fulfils the criteria of the Act
can obtain the PRC. The PRCs are required either for purchasing of property within the State or
seeking employment within the State and there is no other use for such PRC’s outside J&K.
Recommendation
2.3 REFUGEE STATUS TO POJK DPS
2.3.1 The Committee agrees that since PoJK DPs are the citizens of India and also
permanent residents of the State, their mere displacement cannot make them refugees as
such.  Government may, however, consider the benefits and other packages as admissible
6

7
under the law. (Para 3.2.13.3)
Action Taken
2.3.2 The PoJK DPs are the citizens of India and also the permanent residents of the State of
J&K. Hence, they are not treated as refugees.
Recommendation
2.4 MONTHLY CASH, RATION MONEY, EXEMPTION FROM INCOME TAX
2.4.1 As mentioned earlier, the Committee is of the view that the rehabilitation
assistances have been awfully insufficient with very poor track record of implementation.
In view of the pathetic conditions of the displaced persons, the Committee feels that the
Government may consider these demands in the package meant for PoJK DPs, keeping in
view rising inflation and consequent impact on cost of living. (Para 3.2.11.2)
Action Taken
2.4.2 The DPs of PoJK are the citizens of India and also the permanent residents of the State
of J&K. They are enjoying benefits of the State Government schemes and also the centrally
sponsored schemes like any other citizen of the country. The Government of India, from time to
time, have provided relief and rehabilitation assistance/compensation in lieu of land deficiency to
these displaced persons.
Recommendation
2.5 LAND DEFICIENCY COMPENSATION AND EQUAL TREATMENT
2.5.1 The Committee is of the view that  since cash compensation in lieu of land deficiency
is being given to DPs of 1947, on the similar line, cash compensation must also be given
to DPs of 1965 and 1971 in lieu of land deficiency. The Committee fails to understand as
to why State Government is delaying formulation of the proposal and forwarding the same
to Central Government for consideration. The Committee, therefore, strongly, recommends
that Ministry of Home Affairs may impress upon the State Government to formulate the
proposal without any further loss of time and send the same to the Ministry of Home
Affairs for approval. (Para 3.3.3.3)
Action Taken
2.5.2 The DPs of 1965 and 1971 were sanctioned compensation @ upto ` 5000/- per kannal in
lieu of land deficiency in 1990 by the Government of India whereas the DPs of 1947 were
sanctioned compensation @ ` 5000/- per kannal in 2000 which was enhanced to ` 25000/- per
kannal in 2008. As such, the cash compensation to these categories cannot be equated.

CHAPTER - III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE
GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
Recommendation
3.1 WEST PAKISTANI REFUGEES (WPRS)
3.1.1 The Committee expresses its serious concern that the West Pakistani Refugees, who
are very much citizens of India and eligible for voting in Parliamentary elections do not
possess right to vote in the State legislature Assembly elections on the pretext that they
are not permanent residents of the State in terms of the J&K constitution. The Committee
feels that through they are living there for more than 60 years, they are not leading the
life of free citizens despite having voting rights for Parliament. This right has not earned
them any special benefits.  The Committee strongly recommends that the Central
Government must impress upon the State Government to consider, as a one time measure,
the demand of West Pakistani Refugees to grant them the status of permanent residents
of the State sympathetically so that they can live as state subject in a dignified way, with
all legal rights including right to vote in State Legislative Assembly. (Para 3.1.1.6)
Action Taken
3.1.2 The Government of India, on a number of occasions had taken up the issues relating to
the West Pakistani Refugees, including the conferment of Permanent Resident Status. The Union
Home Secretary vide his D.O. letter dated 07.11.2014 addressed to the Chief Secretary to the
Government of J&K has again requested for conferment of Permanent Resident Status to West
Pakistani Refugees settled in the State.
Further Recommendation
3.1.3 The Committee is aware that WPRs are not considered permanent residents of the
State of J&K in terms of the Constitution on the ground that WPRs does not  have
ownership of land i.e. sahib-e-jaidad of J&K in the year 1944, a pre-condition to acquire
a Permanent Residency Rights  but the fact that WPRs are living there since 1947
running from pillar to post in search of permanent source of livelihood.  Moreover, WPRs
arrived there even before enforcement of Article 370. The Committee observes that WPRs
are very much citizens of India having voting rights in Parliamentary elections, therefore,
there is no reason as to why WPRs should not be given voting rights for State Assembly
elections particularly when the ruling establishment at the centre and State Government
at the time of partition advised WPRs to stay at border villages and made assurance to
them for a decent life.  The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that there should

not be any hitch in proposing amendment to the constitution of J&K in favour of WPRs

Assembly election in J&K. The Ministry of Home Affairs must pursue the matter with the

3.19.4 The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in response to the action taken
by Government in compliance to its recommendation made in para 3.1.5.3 of its 183
rd
Report.
Recommendation
3.20 OCCUPANCY/TENANCY RIGHTS
3.20.1 The Committee takes note of the fact as narrated by the Ministry of Home Affairs
that the issue of conferring occupancy/ tenancy rights of evacuee land has not yet been
addressed. This right is necessary to eliminate the disparity with DPs of PoK 1947. The
Committee also taken note of the hope expressed by the Government that in the coming
Session, this issue may be resolved. The Committee is disappointed with the latest situation
at hand and feels that nothing has moved at the ground level. The Committee would like to
impress upon the Government that necessary amendment in the Agrarian Reforms Act of
1976 may be brought at the earliest to settle the long pending issue. (Para 3.3.2.3)
Action Taken
3.20.2 The State Government has been requested to make necessary amendment in the Agrarian
Reforms Act, 1976 to eliminate the disparity with DPs of PoK, 1947.
3.20.3 Replying to a pointed question as to why there has been delay in removing the differential
treatment of Government on the issue of conferring occupancy/tenadency right of evacuee land
being conferred to DPs of PoJK of 1947 but denied to Chhamb DPs of 1965 and 1971, the
Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Committee that Action Taken Report from the Government
of J&K is awaited. However, they have been again reminded vide letter dated 10.11.2015 to
apprise the Ministry about action taken by them.
Further Recommendation
3.20.4 The Committee expresses its displeasure on the delay in elimination of differential

21
treatment on the issue of conferring occupancy/tenancy right of evacuee land being
conferred to DPs of PoJK of 1947 but denied to Chhamb DPs of 1965 and 1971. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that necessary amendment in Agrarian Reform
Act, 1976 be made to eliminate the disparity amongst the DPs at the earliest and the
matter may be vigorously pursued with the State Government.
Recommendation
3.21 EXEMPTION FROM PAYING RENT
3.21.1 The Committee feels that payment of even the meager rent may be difficult for DPs.
The committee recommends that this issue may be reconsidered. Repair work and minor
modification may be allowed without permission from any authority but major change may
be done only after seeking permission from appropriate authority. (Para 3.3.7.3)
Action Taken
3.21.2 The State Government has been requested to consider exemption from paying rent in
respect of evacuee properties allotted/ occupied by the displaced persons/refugees. They may also
be allowed to undertake repair work and minor modification without having to take permission
from the Government
3.21.3 The Committee has been further informed that the Government of J&K vide this Ministry’s
letter dated 13.11.2015 has been requested to furnish the views/information in the matter.
Further Observation
3.21.4 The Committee feels that the practice of charging rent in respect of evacuee properties
allotted/occupied by the DPs and existing mandatory provision of seeking permission to
undertake repair work and minor modification in their dwelling units should not be there.
The Ministry of Home Affairs may pursue the matter with the State Government.
Recommendation
3.22 REGISTRATION OF LEFT OUT DPS
3.22.1 The Committee recommends that Ministry of Home Affairs may impress upon the
State Government to take up early decision on the issue of registration of left out Displaced
Persons families of 1965 and 1971. (Para 3.3.8.3)
Action Taken
3.22.2 The fresh registration of DPs will have practical problems. However, the Ministry of Home
Affairs informed the Committee that the Government of J&K vide this Ministry’s letter dated
13.11.2015 has been requested to furnish the views/information in the matter.
Further Observation
3.22.3 The Committee reiterates its recommendation as   contained in para 3.2.1.4 of 183
rd
Report that the issue of registration of left out DPs families of 1965 and 1971 must be
resolved immediately.

22
Recommendation
3.23 IMPLEMENTATION OF WADHWA COMMITTEE AND INTERLOCUTORS’ REPORTS
3.23.1 The Committee desires that early decision may be taken for implementing the
recommendations of Wadhwa Committee and Interlocutors’ Report. The Ministry of Home
Affairs may pursue the matter with the State Government. (Para 3.3.9.3)
Action Taken
3.23.2 In so far as the report of Wadhwa Committee is concerned, the same was under the
consideration of State Cabinet Sub–Committee. The State Government has been again requested for
taking a decision on implementation of the Wadhwa Committee Report.  As regards Interlocutors’
Report, it is mentioned that most of the recommendations made by Group of Interlocutors on J&K
relate to the State Government. Despite repeated requests, the State Government has not yet
furnished their comments to this Ministry. State Government is being pursued vigorously to offer
their comments on the report.
3.23.3 The Ministry of Home Affairs further informed the Committee that the Government of J&K
vide this Ministry’s letter dated 13.11.2015 has been requested to furnish the views/information in
the matter.
Further Observation
3.23.4 The Committee desires that the Central Government must expedite the
implementation of Wadhwa Committee’s recommendation without further procrastination.

Recommendation
4.1 PUBLICITY OF NODAL AGENCY/OFFICER
4.1.1 The Committee is of the view that the Government should post on the internet the
details of the name and telephone numbers of Provincial Rehabilitation Officer, and other
associated agencies/officers for extending benefits of DPs of 1947 of PoJK along with its
jurisdiction and powers as well as the procedure, in simplified way, to be followed for
making claims or redressal of grievances.  This may also given wide publicity particularly
in the areas where PoJK DPs are living and other places. (Para 3.2.9.3)
Action Taken
4.1.2 The State Government has been requested to put the name and telephone number of
Provincial Rehabilitation Officer, and other associated agencies/officers designated for extending
benefits of DPs of 1947 of PoJK on their official website.
4.1.3 The Ministry of Home Affairs has further informed the Committee that Action Taken Report
from the Government of J&K is awaited. However, they have been again reminded vide this
Ministry’s letter dated 10.11.2015 to necessary action in the matter.
Recommendation
4.2 RESERV ATION IN TECHNICAL AND OTHER PROFESSIONAL COLLEGES, SPECIAL
PACKAGE FOR EMPLOYMENT AND INTEREST FREE LOANS FOR BUSINESS
4.2.1 The Committee feels that since the concern of PoJK DPs for reservation in technical
and professional colleges has already been accepted by the Government, its implementation
on ground level should, not be delayed. The Committee also desires that the Government may
facilitate interest free/subsidized loans to PoJK DPs to establish their business so that they
can lead a settled life banking on their permanent source of livelihood Employment drive for
5-10 years for the youths belonging to PoJK DPs should also be conducted. (Para 3.2.10.3)
Action Taken
4.2.2 The Displaced Persons of PoJK of 1947 settled in J&K are already enjoying benefits of the
Permanent Resident Status of the State. As such, they can get their children admitted into State
Educational institutions including the professionals and technical institutions. They also avail the
opportunities of applying for jobs in the State Government services.  As regards interest free/
subsidized loans to PoJK DPs the D/o Financial Services has been requested to consider the
recommendation of DPSC.

24
Recommendation
4.3 ALLOTMENT OF LAND AND INADEQUATE LAND DEFICIENCY COMPENSATION
4.3.1 The Committee recommends that the amount of compensation for land deficiency
may appropriately be reviewed. All those families that have not received compensation may
be given compensation immediately without any delay. (Para 3.2.14.7)
Action Taken
4.3.2 The rate of compensation announced in 2000 i.e ` 5000/- per kanal in lieu  of land
deficiency to the displaced persons from PoJK of 1947 has already been enhanced in 2008 to
` 25,000/- per kanal subject to the maximum of ` 1.5 lakhs.  State Government has been asked
to expedite the payment of compensation to these DPs.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS – – –  AT A GLANCE
ONE TIME COMPENSATION
1.1.4 The Committee appreciates the initiative taken by the Ministry of Home Affairs for seeking
proposals for one time settlement of DPs from PoJK 1947 and Chhamb DPs of 1965 and 1971 as well
WPRs and desires that all necessary action must be taken within a set time frame, as all these
affected persons continue to lead their lives under depression due to extreme suffering. Any positive
action on the part of the Government would be of great satisfaction to them. (Para 1.1.4)
SLOW DISBURSAL OF COMPENSATION
The Committee hopes that all approved 47 land deficiency claims and 14 applicants for cash
in lieu of urban plots are settled in a dedicated time frame.  Central Government may pursue the
matter with the State Government. (Para 1.2.4)
WEST PAKISTANI REFUGEES (WPRs)
The Committee is aware that WPRs are not considered permanent residents of the State of
J&K in terms of the Constitution on the ground that WPRs does not  have ownership of land i.e
sahib-e-jaidad of J&K in the year 1944, a pre-condition to acquire a Permanent Residency Rights
but the fact that WPRs are living there since 1947 running from pillar to post in search of permanent
source of livelihood.  Moreover, WPRs arrived there even before enforcement of Article 370. The
Committee observes that WPRs are very much citizens of India having voting rights in Parliamentary
elections, therefore, there is no reason as to why WPRs should not be given voting rights for State
Assembly elections particularly when the ruling establishment at the centre and State Government
at the time of partition advised WPRs to stay at border villages and made assurance to them for a
decent life.  The Committee feels that there should not be any hitch in proposing amendment to the
constitution of J&K in favour of WPRs conferring Permanent Residence Certificate and voting
rights for State Legislative Assembly election in J&K. The Ministry of Home Affairs may pursue
the matter with the State Government. (Para 3.1.3)
PROVISION OF STATE GOVERNMENT JOBS
The Committee strongly reiterate its recommendation that pending conferment of Permanent
Resident Status to the WPRs, a temporary waiver may be made for admission of the children in the
professional institutions in the State. (Para 3.2.4)
RESERV ATION IN CENTRAL GOVERNMENT JOBS/CENTRAL PROFESSIONAL COLLEGES
The Committee, expresses its deep concern over the apathetic attitude of the State Government
of J&K on the issue of giving reservation to wards of WPRs in Central Government Jobs/Central
Professional Colleges and strongly reiterates its recommendation made in Para 3.1.3.3. of 183rd Report
and desires that  the Union Ministry of Home Affairs may  pursue the matter with the State Government
25

26
for an early decision in the matter so that the direction of Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of B.L.
Kalgotra Vs. States & Others is complied without  further delay. (Para 3.3.4)
RESERV ATION TO THE WARDS OF WPRs FOR ADMISSION IN ENGINEERING AND MEDICAL
COLLEGES
The Committee is anguished to note that the Ministry of Human Resource Development
has not responded to the request of the Ministry for taking a decision in regard to providing
reservation to the wards of WPRs in engineering, medical and other related institutions of higher
education across the country. The Committee, therefore, strongly reiterates its recommendation
that the Department of Higher Education, Government of India must take early decision with
regard to according priority in admissions to children of WPRs  in engineering, medical and other
institutions outside J&K.  A separate reservation may be provided to them.  The Ministry of Home
Affairs may pursue the matter with the Ministry of Human Resource Development to get the
assurance implemented given by Home Secretary to the Committee on ground level.
(Para 3.4.4)
OPENING OF KVS/NVS FOR WPRS
The Committee takes a strong note of the inaction on the part of the Ministry of Human
Resource Development.  The Committee recommends that the Department of School Education,
Ministry of Human Resource Development should take all necessary steps in the matter.  The
Ministry of Home Affairs may pursue with Ministry of Human Resource Development for early
implementation of the recommendation. (Para 3.5.4)
ONE TIME PACKAGE, MONTHLY MONETARY ASSISTANCE AND ACCOMMODATION
The Committee is constrained to express its displeasure over the indifferent attitude of  the
State to the problems of WPRs as State Government of J&K has not furnished proposal to Union
Ministry of Home Affairs to procure one time financial package/compensation to WPRs who are
otherwise in dire need for immediate relief and rehabilitation for sustenance. (Para 3.6.4)
Creation of separate battalion in State Police, Army and Para Military Forces
The Committee notes the various instructions/guidelines issued and request made to the
Ministry of Defence to issue such instruction allowing recruitment of WPRs/Wards of WPRs settled
in J&K to the Central Para Military Forces/CPAFs and in the Indian Armed Forces without the
condition of having a domicile certificate from the designated authority of the State of Government
of J&K, and in lieu of that Sarpanch/Numberdar certificate accompanied by the electoral roll could
be accepted as proof of their being WPRs.  The Committee, however, desires that the Ministry of
Home Affairs must monitor or undertake requisite follow-up action in tandem with the State
Government to ensure the compliance of its instruction in the matter.  The Committee strongly
recommends that the Ministry of Defence must actively consider the request made by the Ministry
of Home Affairs vide its letter dated 7
th January, 2015 and 09.02.2015 in regard to recruitment of the
wards of WPRs in the Indian Armed Forces.  The Committee may be informed of the find action
taken. (Para 3.7.4)
RESERVATION OF SEATS IN LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY AND LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL
The Committee hopes that once the WPRs are granted permanent resident status in the

27
State of J&K, WPRs would  enjoy all democratic rights including right to elect and get elected in all
representatives bodies.  The Committee further desires that the Union Home Ministry may apprise
the Committee of response of State Government of J&K to its recommendation regarding reservation
of seats in the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council of the State for WPRs. (Para 3.8.4)
DISPLACED PERSON FROM PoJK IN 1947
Official registration of DPs of 1947
The Committee is not in agreement with the plea of the Ministry of Home Affairs that since
there would be practical problems in fresh enumeration of Displaced Persons (DPs), the demand for
official registration of DPs of 1947 could not be accepted.  The Committee is of the view that

DEFREEZING OF SEATS IN LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY
The Committee wishes to pin-point that India is a representative democratic country, therefore,

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred Ninety Fourth Report on Action Taken by Government on the
observations/recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Seventy Third Report on the
Strengthening of the working of the Ministry of DoNER for effective implementation of Policies,
Programmes, Schemes and Projects meant for North Eastern Region.
2. The One Hundred and Seventy Third Report of the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Home Affairs was presented/laid to the Rajya Sabha and on the Table of the
Lok Sabha on 29th August, 2013. After presentation of the Report, the copies thereof were sent
to the Ministry of DoNER requesting them to furnish Action Taken Notes on the recommendations
of the Committee contained in the Report. The Action Taken Notes thereon were received from the
Ministry of DoNER on 22nd September, 2014. Based on the ATN the Secretariat forwarded a
Questionnaire to the Ministry of DoNER and the replies thereon were received.
3. The Committee visited the States of Assam, Meghalaya and Manipur from 25th to 29th May,
2015 for on-the-spot assessment of action taken on the recommendations contained in 173rd Report.
During the visit, the Committee held discussions with the Chief Secretaries and other officers of
the State Governments of Assam, Meghalaya and Manipur including local/district administrations and
other stakeholders on development projects in North-East Region.
4. The Committee in its meeting held on 29th June, 2015 decided to hear Chief Secretaries of
remaining five North Eastern States in Delhi which could not be heard during the aforesaid visit.
Accordingly, the Committee, in its meeting held on 27th July, 2015 heard the Secretary, Ministry
of DoNER along with the representatives of States viz. Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Nagaland,
Sikkim and Tripura in Delhi itself. In the said meeting, the Committee, after a detailed assessment,
observed that the Ministry of DoNER has furnished superfluous, evasive and unsatisfactory response
to 31 recommendations out of a total of 49 recommendations as contained in 173rd Report. The
Committee observed that the Ministry of DoNER responded to six recommendations were found to
be incomplete and unsatisfactory. The Committee further observed that with regard to eight
recommendations of the Committee, the Ministry of DoNER just responded by indicating ‘noted for
compliance’ and while six recommendations were communicated to the other agencies without any
follow up action and eleven recommendations of the Committee were without exclusive response.
The Committee thereon directed the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER to hold detailed discussions with
State Governments and other Central Ministries and Departments and furnish revised action taken
notes to the Committee for examination and consideration.  The Ministry of DoNER furnished the

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE
GOVERNMENT
1.0 After hearing the views of various stakeholders viz. Ministry of DoNER, line Ministries,
representatives of North Eastern State Governments, Secretary, Department of Expenditure, Secretary,
Planning Commission and Cabinet Secretary on the subject, the Committee has arrived at the following
conclusions observations/ recommendations.
Recommendation
1.1 AVOIDANCE OF PROCEDURAL DELAY
1.1.1 From the evidence available, the Committee takes note of the fact that the major drawback in
the timely implementation and completion of the projects lies in the procedural delay. The Committee
is of the view that in order to give fillip to the development process in the region, the whole
Government machinery involving both the Central Government and State Governments need to pull up
their socks right from the stage of conceptualisation of schemes, allocation of funds, formulation of
DPRs, technical vetting of DPRs, obtaining environment/forest clearances to actual take-off of projects
on ground involving land acquisition, capacity building, conducive law and order situation, etc. This
requires a well balanced planning, good coordination between various agencies and time bound
clearances/rejections of projects. The Committee, therefore, recommends that a robust monitoring
mechanism should be put in place so that procedural delays at every stage of the projects are brought
down to minimum level, though ideal situation would be to remove all delays.
                                                 (Para 5.2.1 of the 173rd Report)
Action Taken
1.1.2 In pursuance of the directions given by Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Home Affairs, in its meeting held  on 27/07/2015, detailed discussions were held with the NE States
on 03/08/2015 through video conferencing so as to put in place a simplified procedure for expeditious
processing/execution of projects  under the NLCPR scheme. After  consultations and after examination
of feasibility, the following simplified procedure, which includes pre as well as post sanction of the
projects,  is proposed to be put in place so as to remove the bottlenecks and delays in the timely
completion of the projects:-
(i) The NE States to submit Priority Lists by September of the year for the next financial
year commencing from this year itself.
(ii) The normative allocation for the States will be intimated well in advance based on past
years’ trend after taking account of their infrastructure development indices, absorption
capacity as shown in pending projects and after accommodating needs for ongoing and
retained projects.
2

3
(iii) A project should be at a single location and should not a composite of several locations
as already specified in the Guidelines of NLCPR.
(iv) Priority List should be continuous and in a running format (No sector-wise, district-wise
categorisation of projects should be in the Priority List).
(v) The total value of projects included in the Priority List should not exceed 1.5 times of
the total normative allocation so intimated.
(vi) Projects exceeding 1.5 times of the allocation shall be summarily rejected.
(vii) The current specification in guidelines for reserving 25% of new projects for backward
areas is vague and will be specified as intended for Autonomous Territorial/District
Councils.
(viii) The concept paper for each project should clearly specify if the expenditure is to be
incurred on creating public assets, the nature of landholding, Government control and
management etc.
(ix) Chief Secretary/Planning Secretary/Departmental Secretary (when concerned) shall alone
attend the meeting of the NLCPR Committee, convened for initial screening of concept
papers and later for sanction of finalised DPRs of the projects included for the State. In
case these officers are unable to attend the meeting, another authorised representative,
who is able to take on the spot decisions, may alone attend the meeting.  In case the
authorised representative is unable to satisfactorily answer the queries of the Committee,
the project shall be rejected as unsupported and the funds diverted to next in priority or
to approved projects of other States.
(x) Once the project(s) are cleared, the States will be invariably (by default) required to
submit DPRs within a period of two months. In case more time is sought by the State
at the time of approval of concept, such time not exceeding two months beyond the
default period shall be given.
(xi) DPRs should invariably include all the mandatory certificates viz. Environment and forest
clearance, availability of land, free from encumbrances,  non-duplication certificate and
availability of stone and sand quarry in the proximity of the project (in case of road
projects) etc.
(xii) The DPRs should be prepared as per the check-list prescribed by respective line Ministries
and on standard software for which the Ministry will arrange training/workshops for the
State Government officials and for potential vendors nominated by States as part of the
Ministry’s Vendor Development efforts.
(xiii) During the consultation process, many State Governments requested that the cost of
preparation of DPRs may be included in the project cost. In response to query by
Secretary, DoNER with regard to the cost incurred by the States on preparation of DPR,
the State representatives assured him that they would advise the same shortly after
consultations. After receiving response from all NE State Governments, the same shall be
considered suitably for incorporating the costs of soil testing for buildings and bridges and
DPR preparation in the NLCPR guidelines.

4
(xiv) The State shall also certify that these projects have not been taken up or proposed to be
taken with any other funding mechanism in the past or during the current financial year.
(xv) On the receipt of DPRs, Technical Wing of Ministry of DoNER will carry out  preliminary
scrutiny. The consolidated queries of Technical Wing, if any, shall be circulated, online/
through e-mail, to the State Planning and Implementing Department within 15 days. In
case the reply is not received within the period of 15 days from receipt of query, it shall
be presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the project and the project will be
deleted within seven days thereafter without any further notice.
(xvi) On receipt of reply to the queries raised by the Technical Wing, the DPRs will be sent
to the vetting agency/line Ministries, with the request to vet the DPRs. The vetting agency
shall raise consolidated queries, if any, which will be forwarded to the State Government
through Ministry, which will be required to furnish replies to the same within a period of
15 days. If these queries are not settled within 15 days of communication, the State
Government will be given another 15 days for furnishing replies to the query from the
vetting agency, failing which it will presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the
project and the said project will stand rejected. However, if the State Government finds
it difficult to collect data for a reply and gives cogent and substantial reasons, further time
of up to 30 days may be provided and not beyond.
(xvii) Vetting agency will give techno-economic vetting of the projects within one month from
receipt of replies to the consolidated queries within a period one month. In case any further
query is raised because of unsatisfactory replies or issues arising, these should be settled
before or on the date the project is placed for sanction before the Screening Committee.
(xviii) The line Ministries/NITI Aayog/NEC will be approached in parallel for non-duplication
certificates and for certifying if the project is fit for gap funding. The line Ministries/NITI
Aayog/NEC shall give their comments/observations within one month else it will be
presumed to be clear for non-duplication and gap funding angle. In any event, these views
shall be finally provided at the time of project sanctions.
(xix) NLCPR Committee meeting shall be convened periodically to consider sanctioning of the
cleared projects, duly vetted by the vetting agency and will also record the information/
views on non-duplication and gap funding character.
(xx) Release of funds:
     States laid great priority on streamlining the release of funds by the Ministry.
Therefore, after sanction of the project by the inter-ministerial NLCPR Committee, the
administrative and financial sanction shall be issued after following the laid down
procedures. Tendering process shall be finalised within two months by following
transparent process of bidding and Work Order issued. A copy of the tender shall
mandatorily also be placed on the NEC and NLCPR websites. Ministry of DoNER would
release funds in three instalments comprising 30%, 50% and 20%.
Release of first installment of funds:  30 % of the central share i.e. 90% of the total
approved cost of the project, shall be released along with administrative and financial
sanction.

5
Release of second installment of funds:  50% of the central share subject the condition
that 50 % of the funds released as first instalment has been utilised by the State for the
project and commensurate physical progress.
Release of third and final installment of funds: 20% of the central share subject to
the condition that 90% of the released amount, including full State share of 10% stands
utilised and  on achievement of 70% of physical progress of the project.
(xxi) States shall release funds to the implementing agency within a period of 15 days from
receipt from this Ministry. A copy of the release order shall be uploaded on the NLCPR
website and/or sent to the Ministry and will be taken note of for further releases in this
and other projects of the State as an instance of diversion of funds.
(xxii) In case of delayed projects, not more than two extensions shall be given, with overall
cumulative ceiling of one and half years (two working seasons) from the original date
of completion of the project. Reasons for delay shall be approved by Principal Secretary/
Secretary, Planning, on the recommendations of Secretary of the Implementing
Department. In the event that the project remains incomplete, the State may retain the
projects for pursuit by themselves so that the Ministry may transfer the funds to other
projects selected for the States. In case the delay is on account of reasonable
justification acceptable to the Ministry, this requirement may be waived on a case to
case basis.
1.1.3 On the issue of expeditious implementation of programmes/schemes, the Secretary, Ministry of
DoNER apprised the Committee during its meeting held on 27th July, 2015 as under:-
“ On expeditious implementation, ...., we have advanced the timeline. Last year, we had the
Committee meeting for approving projects in November, but this year, we are having it in
September. We have already asked the States to give the priority list in September .....and they
come with the DPRs. They take some time to prepare the DPRs. They come back to us, we
sanction it, and then it goes on with that, .... The idea is that they don’t miss a season. The
working season is only from September to March-April. Therefore that season should not be
missed. After a project is sanctioned, they tender it and all that, and they will be ready for the
next season.”
1.1.4 In regard to use of software in preparation of detailed project report, the Secretary, Ministry
of DoNER stated as under:-
“ we have written to the States to use software for the preparation of DPRs so that there is
no occasion to see that once a DPR is approved and sanctioned and the funds are released,
the Project Officer should not suddenly discover that the project parameters, the ground depth,
the hill slopes or whatever are different from what were mentioned in the DPR and, therefore,
it is not feasible to implement it. Therefore, we have told them to use software, go by realistic
field parameters and then send us the DPR. ....... We have also asked our contractors – now
we have appointed one CPSU as a contractor for below 
` 50 crores projects and another for
above ` 50 crores projects – to use the software to vet the DPRs, and this is likely to lead to
efficiency.”

1.1.5 As reg ards, the procedural delay in vetting of the DPRs, the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER
explained the action taken by the Ministry as under:-
“ The vetting of  DPRs can be expedited only if there is a common agreed system of developing
the DPRs, and that common system is possible through use of common softwares.  There are
softwares available in the market, which are specifically utilized for such purposes — for
building roads and bridges.  It is used in all the large projects all over the country and across
the world also.  This is easily available even in the North-Eastern Region.   So, that is what
we feel is a method of having a commonality in approach for preparing DPRs so that it can
be prepared fast and also vetted fast... on the issue of enhancing transparency,  we are
developing a software... But we are preparing a software with the help of NIC on the uploading
of DPRs, on the transfer of information between  the DoNER and States, on issuing SMS alerts
on responses that are required from DoNER and from States, so that those SMS alerts go to the
concerned officer.  And, if the concerned officer does not take action, it goes to the next higher

1.1.6 Apprising the Committee of the need for the software and arrive at a common approach to the

“ When we have a software the State agencies that are responsible for preparing DPRs are

Further Recommendation
1.1.8 The Committee observes that in compliance with the Committee’s recommendation for
avoidance of procedural delay and direction given it its meeting held on 27 th July, 2015, the
Ministry of DoNER in tandem with the State Governments and the concerned line Ministries has
undertaken a number of measures from the stage of conceptualization of scheme, preparation
and submission of priority list, expeditious processing/execution of projects under NLCPR
scheme, setting detailed guidelines and simplification of procedures for preparing and
submission and vetting of DPRs, sanctioning, allocation and release of funds for timely
implementation and completion of projects.  The Committee, however, would like to be apprised
of perceptible outcome of the measures so undertaken on the ground level in the form of period
of time reduced in clearance of projects and its completion in comparison to pre and post
reforms phase on removal of all unnecessary procedural delays.  The kernel spirit of the
Committee’s recommendation made in para 5.2.1 of the Committee’s 173
rd Report is to give
fillip to developmental process in NER through procedural facilitation and timely implementation
of policies, programmes, schemes and projects meant for all round balanced development of the
region.
1.1.9 The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should take up the
issue of revisiting the instant specification in guidelines for reserving 25% of new projects for
backward areas which is at present vague and therefore needs modification on the lines of
autonomous territorial/district council.
1.1.10 The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should persuade the line
ministries to arrange training/workshops for the State Government officials and for potential
vendors nominated by States as part of the Ministry’s Vendor Development efforts.  The
Committee believes that such measures would enable the State Government officials for
preparation of DPRs with great specification and on rationale basis to take into account detailed
survey and baseline facts. The Committee further desires that the request of the State
Governments for incorporating the cost of preparation of DPRs in the project cost should be
considered at the earliest and the same may be laid down in the NLCPR guidelines.
1.1.11 The Committee observes that no guidelines have been set up on frequency of meeting
of the NLCPR Committee and timeline for consideration  and sanctioning of cleared projects.
Therefore, the Committee desires that the meeting of the NLCPR should be convened
periodically with a set time-frame, known to the State Governments so that requisite
information may be furnished to the NLCPR Committee well in advance.  Also, timelines for
consideration and sanctioning of projects should be let up to avoid delays on their part.
Recommendation

queries/clarifications of the Line Ministries are not sought in one go rather they are sought in 2-3
installments which are then replied to by the State Governments to the Line Ministries through the
Ministry of DoNER.  The entire process takes about 1-2 years and sometimes more, for sanction of

projects after submission of the DPRs, thus resulting in time/cost escalation of the projects. The

meetings held for sanctioning of the projects, to give clarifications on the spot. The Committee,

Recommendation
1.3 REPRESENTATIVES FROM STATE GOVERNMENT IN NLCPR
1.3.1 The Committee agrees with the demand of the North Eastern State Governments that there
should be a representative of the State, possibly the Chief Secretary or the Commissioner/Secretary, in
charge Planning Department of the State in the NLCPR Committee for retention and sanctioning of
projects and recommends that necessary steps be taken to ensure representation of the concerned State
Governments in the NLCPR Committee. (Para 5.3.4 ibid)
Action Taken
1.3.2 Representatives of State Governments concerned are invariably invited to attend the meetings of
the inter-ministerial NLCPR Committee for retention and sanction of the projects taken up for funding
under the scheme of NLCPR. To further strengthen the procedure, it has been agreed that Chief
Secretary/Planning Secretary/Departmental Secretary (when concerned) shall alone attend the meeting of
the NLCPR Committee, convened for initial screening of concept papers and later for sanction of
finalised DPRs of the projects included for the State. In case these officers are unable to attend the
meeting, another authorised representative, who is able to take on the spot decisions, may alone attend
the meeting.  In case the authorised representative is unable to satisfactorily answer the queries of the
Committee, the project shall be rejected as unsupported and the funds diverted to next in priority or
to approved projects of other States.
Recommendation
1.4 CAPACITY CONSTRAINTS
1.4.1 The Committee finds that the State Governments have to do a lot of catching up as far as
capacity building is concerned.  The Committee takes note of the complaints regarding inadequate
investigations and project formulation which led to changes in scope and revision of drawings at later
stage. It also notes problems related to inappropriate and inadequate procurement and faulty contractual
management system. Poor selection of contractors due to low bids with no technical capability to handle
the project led to cost overruns, schedule delays, poor quality etc. The Committee also finds that in
some cases the project lengths are very large and there is lack of technical expertise in State PWDs
in implementing the projects. The Committee further observes that there is dearth of local contractors
with sound financial and technical capabilities and low participation of contractors from other parts

10
of the country in the tenders also. The Committee is, therefore, of the considered view that concerted
effort is required on the part of the Ministry of DoNER and Planning Commission to improve State
Governments’ capabilities for project preparation and execution. The Ministry of DoNER in consultation
with Finance Ministry and Planning Commission should chalk out a long-term plan for capacity
building of State Governments of NER keeping in mind huge infrastructure needs of the region. The
Committee also recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should extend technical and other related help
to the State PWDs to improve their technical capacities and execution capabilities. The State
Governments and Ministry of DoNER should also take necessary steps for assisting local contractors
to upgrade their skills. (Para 5.4.1 ibid)
Action Taken
1.4.2 It is proposed to enhance the technical and execution capabilities of the State agencies by
imparting training of their technical personnel, organising workshops etc.
Further Recommendation
1.4.3 The Committee may be apprised of the action plan prepared with regard to capacity
building i.e. technical and execution capabilities of State Government.
Recommendation
1.5 PROBLEMS RELATED TO LAW AND ORDER SITUATION
1.5.1 The Committee finds that the law and order situation is one of the biggest problems in NER
which is posing a threat to the projects by preventing them from taking off. The Committee has on
record the suggestion of Line Ministries that the local problems and law and order issues should be
addressed by State and local administrations to ensure smooth completion of projection. Agreeing with
the view of Line Ministries, the Committee suggests that all local issues including problems of law and
order should be addressed by the local administration and State Authorities.
(Para 5.5.1 ibid)
Action Taken
1.5.2 State Governments are responsible for the law and order situation and are expected to provide
conducive environment for execution of the projects.  Chief Secretaries of all the eight North Eastern
States have been requested to ensure safety of the personnel working at the respective work sites.
Recommendation
1.6 LACUNAE ON THE PART OF THE STATE GOVERNMENTS
1.6.1 The Committee is of the view that the onus of development in NER lies as much on the State
Governments as on the agencies of the Central Government. The Committee is constrained to express
its displeasure to find that the Line Ministries and State Governments pass the buck to each other while
facing bottlenecks during the course of implementation of projects for development. But, the need is
to exercise introspection. State Governments cannot get away just by pointing fingers towards the Centre
and vice-versa. The case in point is the 3,000 MW Debang Power Project to be executed by NHPC,
where  even holding of public hearings, which was one of the first things to happen, could not be
conducted because of law and order situation and had to be postponed 12 times. After a lot of

11
intervention by the Ministry of Power and the personal intervention of the Minister of Power, the public
hearing was conducted. Similar is the case with many projects which certainly hampered the process of
development in NER.
1.6.2 The Ministry of Surface Transport and Highways cited a case under Arunachal package for road
construction of 740 kms., in two packages—one of 300 plus kms. and the other of 440 kms.  But land
acquisition for these stretches could not be completed for a long period of two years.  Since the Ministry
had decided to award projects only when 90% of the land was available, the programmes could not
be executed for want of land acquisition.
1.6.3 Another case that has come to the notice of the Committee is that of a scheme of providing
100 per cent central assistance to the North-Eastern States for taking up river development works.
Apart from the National Waterway-2, that is, the Brahmaputra River , there are other river stretches also
which could be developed for cargo transportation.  The Committee is disappointed to note that
response or the initiative from the States of the North-Eastern Region is lacking. The Central
Government, on its own, engaged M/s. RITES to identify river stretches which could be developed for
such cargo transportation and RITES had identified 22 river stretches in all the States of North-Eastern
Region for development.  Those identified river stretches had been shared with the concerned State
Governments and they had been requested to send proposals for assistance.  However, so far, only three
proposals have been received, one of which had been sanctioned.  The Committee is of the opinion that
the North-Eastern States need to be more proactive in sending the proposals for development of these
river stretches for cargo transportation.
1.6.4 One more example that has come to the notice of the Committee is the case of fixed terminal
at Pandu which is supposed to be completed by June, 2014. Dedicated road connectivity has been
sanctioned at a cost of 
` 11 crore to connect National Highway-31 and for this, land was required from
the Railways.  The requisite amount had been paid but the land had not been transferred owing to
2,150 encroachments which are to be cleared by the State Government. The Committee was informed
that either the encroachment had to be removed or an alternative piece of land for an alternative
alignment has to be given. This dedicated connectivity from the Waterway Terminal to the National
Highway would be an essential requirement for smooth flow of cargo. The Committee observes that the
removal of encroachments by the concerned State Government at the earliest is the only option as there
is no other alignment possible.  In view of the above illustrations,  the Committee is of the firm view
that the Ministry of DoNER should play a pro-active role in resolving issues amongst Line Ministries
and State Governments for timely execution of projects and State Governments should also come
forward with their cooperation.  Unless States take initiative and cooperate, projects cannot take off
and development will continue to be hampered.
(Para 5.7.1, 5.7.2, 5.7.3 and 5.7.4)
Action Taken
1.6.5 Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region shares the recommendation that development
process in NER needs full cooperation between State Governments and agencies of Central
Government. State Government have been impressed upon to be more proactive in sending proposals
and taking initiative so that development process in the region does not hamper and also to hasten
process of land acquisition, wherever required. Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region has
taken due cognizance of the proactive role that is required to be played by it in resolving issues amongst

12
Line Ministries and State Governments for timely execution of the projects. Recognising the importance
of States’ cooperation, views of all stakeholders are now taken before deciding a policy. Changes in
policies are preceded by detailed stakeholder consultations.  In pursuance of this shift in policy, a Chief
Ministers’ Conference was organized on 21 & 22
nd August at Guwahati in Assam where aspirations of
the NE people were articulated by the States and Ministry of DoNER is now engaged in putting in place
appropriate mechanism for converting these into reality.
1.6.6 In the said C onference of the Chief Ministers of the North Eastern Region, the dignitaries, the
State Governments and the Task Groups constituted during the Conference presented and shared their
views on the state of development of transport connectivity, such as Rail, Road, Air and Waterways
in North Eastern Region; the factors/issues impeding the development of transport network and road-
map/vision for improvement thereof within North Eastern Region and of the region with other parts of
the country/adjoining countries. The conference also shared the view that dismal state of transport
network in North Eastern Region is one of prime factors impeding growth and development in the
region.  To address the issue, Ministry of DoNER has constituted a inter-ministerial Working Group on
development of transport network in North Eastern Region with the following terms and reference:-
(i) to assess and map the present state of development of transport network in North Eastern
Region;
(ii) to make recommendations for coordinated development, roadmap and vision of various
transport network/sectors in North Eastern Region in medium and long terms;
(iii) to make recommendations with regard to action plan, strategy and modalities for
implementation of its recommendations;
(iv) to identify issues, concern areas and challenges;
(v) to crystallize approach and make recommendations to address issues, concern areas and
challenges;
Further Recommendation
1.6.7 The Committee would like to be apprised of the recommendations of inter-ministerial
working group on development of transport network in North Eastern Region alongwith action
taken by the Government thereon.  The Committee would further desire to know about
progress on 3000 MW Debang Power Project that was to be executed by NHPC, Arunachal
Package for road construction of 740 km., decision granting scheme of providing 100% central
assistance to NER states for taking up river development works.
Recommendation
1.7 TELECOM SECTOR
1.7.1 The Committee takes note of the poor telecom connectivity in North-East.  The telecom system
is linear which if broken at a point disturbs the whole segment. The Committee agreeing with the
suggestion of the Department of Telecommunications, recommends that provision of having ducts
alongside the roads is a good suggestion and it should be made mandatory for road works not only
in NER but also in the whole country so that no OFC is damaged on account of road works. The
Committee recommends that the existing infrastructure available with organizations like Power Grid

13
Corporation, Railtel etc. as well as State Governments should provide Right of Way at a reasonable
cost for better connectivity in the region. The Committee also notes that the Department of
Telecommunications had suggested an alternative connection from Tripura to Akhora in Bangladesh to
provide an alternative path and the matter is being negotiated through the Ministry of External Affair
Ministry. The Committee desires that the negotiations in this regard may be concluded at the earliest
to ensure communication connectivity to the North East Region with the country.
1.7.2 The Committee also notes that the Power Grid Corporation is not ready to lend a pair of fibre
in the cable going on the transmission lines on cost sharing basis as it is rather interested in giving
the bandwidth on lease commercially to earn more money.  The matter had been brought to the notice
of the PMO and Cabinet Secretary, but with no avail.  The Committee in this connection would like
to impress upon the Government that connectivity to the North East Region should not be viewed solely
on commercial lines to make profit as it is for the national cause. The Committee therefore recommends
that the PMO and Cabinet Secretary should intervene in the matter to sort out the issue at the earliest.
1.7.3 As mentioned earlier, losses can make any activity unsustainable for long period and keeping
in mind that the viability gap funding is needed to ensure commercial feasibility for regular provision
of telecommunication services in North East, the Committee recommends that the issue of viability gap
funding may be examined and may be provided for regular provision of telecommunication services in
North East. (Paras 5.9.1, 5.9.2 & 5.9.3 ibid)
Action Taken
1.7.4 Use of OPGW (Optical Ground Wire) of PGCIL’s Transmission lines for setting alternate
telecommunications network:- MOU signed between BSNL and PGCIL in June, 2014 to augment
broadband capacities at 20 places on payment basis.  Implementation period is 12-18 months. Telecom
connectivity in border areas - MHA has agreed to fund strengthening of telecom services in border area
in general and BSF posts in particular for which survey is under progress. This will also address the
problem of use of mobile network of neighbouring countries in border areas. Setting of utility duct
along National Highways (as done in Mumbai - Pune Expressway) - Utility duct provisioning along NH
from Guwahati to Shillong is being taken up by MORTH on pilot basis. Alternate transmission
connectivity between Kolkata and Tripura via Dhaka: Dhaka - Akhaura - Agartala OF link (10G) - is
under discussion. Setting up International internet gateway at Agartala (for better and reliable internet
connectivity) through cox bazar by using existing submarine cable of BSCCL- is also under discussion.
Based on the request of the Department of Telecom, Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)
issued Recommendations on “Improving Telecom Services in North-Eastern States: An Investment
Plan”, dated 26
th September, 2013.  In its meeting held on 13.06.2014, the Telecom Commission
approved a proposal to implement the comprehensive telecom development plan at an estimated project
cost of ` 5336.18 crores. Union Cabinet has since approved the “Comprehensive Development Plan for
NER” on 15/09/2014. Main thrust areas identified for improvement and augmentation of telecom
services in North-Eastern Region (NER) are:-
(i) to provide 2G  mobile coverage in identified uncovered villages.
(ii) to provide seamless 2G mobile coverage along the National Highways in NER.
(iii) to ensure reliability of and redundancy in the transmission network at State capitals and
district headquarters in NER.

14
1.7.5 Nat ional Optical Fibre Network (NOFN):  NOFN project is planned to connect all Gram
Panchayats (approx. 2.5 lakh) in the country including those in the North Eastern Region (inclusive of
Sikkim) through optical fibre utilizing existing fibers of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and laying
incremental fiber wherever necessary to bridge the connectivity gap between Gram Panchayats (GPs)
and Blocks, for providing broadband connectivity. NOFN project is being executed by BSNL (in Sikkim
and Assam) and Rail Tel (in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura).
NOFN will deliver bandwidth of 100 Mbps at each Gram Panchayat. The roll-out of NOFN is planned
to be completed by 31.03.2017.
