1.9 FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO AIRPORTS IN NE
1.9.1 Attention of the Committee has also been drawn to the drawback in the Route Disbursal
Guidelines, under which airlines are obliged to deploy 10 per cent of their capacity, which they are

17
operating on the metro routes, to the North-East and however, by taking advantage of the drawback,
they are operating a lot of services to Guwahati and Bagdogra and the main problem of the
connectivity within the North-East is still very much there, thus defeating the very purpose of the
Guidelines in letter and spirit. It has been suggested that there may be Airport Connectivity Guidelines
(ACG) and Code Sharing with national and regional airlines to overcome this problem. The Committee
recommends that the matter of having Airport Connectivity Guidelines (ACG) and Code Sharing with
national and regional airlines may be examined earnestly to ensure air connectivity to all parts of the
North East, and not just Guwahati and Bagdogra in the name of obligation under Route Disbursal
Guidelines.  The Committee also received a suggestion that Ministry of DoNER/NEC should give 100%
financial support as all the airports are making losses. The Committee recommends that this suggestion
of Ministry of Civil Aviation may be examined. (Para 5.10.2)
Action Taken

Eastern Region: A meeting of Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) on 13.08.2014 under the

1.10 CONSTITUTION OF EMPOWERED GROUP OF MINISTERS TO REVIEW KEY
INFRASTRUCTURE PROGRAMMES
1.10.1 The Committee notes the suggestion made by Ministry of DoNER that suitable and adequate
institutional arrangements are the need of the hour for monitoring of infrastructure projects of key line
Ministries viz. Road Transport and Highways, Railways, Power, Civil Aviation, Telecommunications,
Communications Information Technology, Shipping, etc. The Committee is of the considered view that
NER being strategically significant considering its long international borders it is but natural that the
targets in the key infrastructural projects as planned by line Ministries are achieved to improve
connectivity, power generation and ward off security threat.  The Committee, therefore, agrees that there
must be some institutional arrangements/mechanism in the form of Empowered Group of Ministers to

18
review key infrastructural projects. The Committee notes that the Government is already seized of the
matter and the Prime Minister has directed the Cabinet Secretary for setting up of EGoM for the review
of NE projects etc.  The Committee, subsequent to the discussions it had with Cabinet Secretary, has
been informed that the EGoM has since been constituted to look into the major projects and issues of
NE Region. The Committee notes that this step will accelerate implementation of projects and
programmes in NE Region. (Para 5.12.1)
Action Taken
1.10.2 Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region shares the optimism of the Committee on the
recommendation.
Recommendation
1.11 ENGINEERING PROCUREMENT PROJECT (EPC) MODE OF DELIVERY
1.11.1 The Committee takes note of the submission of the Transport Secretary that in the case  of a
project consisting of four stretches  in the State of Nagaland at a total cost of 
` 1,300 crore, it was
enhanced to ` 2,900 crore in the revised estimate and  the local requirement for these four stretches
was completely at variance with the project report. Dealing with the same issue of cost escalation
though citing another example, the State Government also mentioned  that  sanction of projects under
Power sector for Nagaland was stalled on the ground that the cost of power projects appeared to be
‘two times’ the normal cost of projects compared to the process prevailing in the rest of India. The State
Government felt that the Ministry should take the ground reality of cost in hilly/terrain region such as
difficult terrain, lack of vendors’ response, etc.
1.11.2 The Committee takes note of the views of Secretary, RT & HW that for reducing escalation of
project cost, they are going towards EPC mode. Cabinet Secretary also emphasized the EPC mode.  The
Committee also notes that there is some resistance in accepting EPC mode.  The Committee, however,
strongly recommends that the Ministries should shift from ‘item rate’ mode-of-delivery to the
‘Engineering Procurement Contract’ mode-of-delivery so as to avoid the escalation of project costs and
delay.  The Committee is also of the view that where EPC model is not being followed, the contractors/
consultants should be penalized for faulty projections at the stage of project formulation itself by State
PWDs when they receive exaggerated or faulty project reports.
(Paras 5.13.1 and 5.13.2)
Action Taken
1.11.3 Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has since taken a policy decision to insist upon
awarding of all future contracts on “EPC” mode.  Ministry of DoNER has also already stipulating that
contracts under NLCPR projects be given on “Turnkey Basis”.
Recommendation
1.12 TAILORING OF SCHEMES
1.12.1 The Committee notes that the guidelines issued under various schemes in the way of
implementation in the NE States due to topographical and other disadvantages.  The Committee was
informed that for strengthening Trauma Centre, the conditions prescribing minimum number of beds and
doctors are difficult to be fulfilled, likewise, HRD Ministry has provided ten computers in a school,

19
but power connection under the scheme RGGVY does not permit this.  The Committee, therefore, is of
the view that Ministries should frame broad based schemes or a component within existing scheme to
suit NER and the guidelines of programmes with all-India nature may be tailored/modified and relaxed.
The Committee desires that Central Ministries should conduct analysis of their on-going schemes from
the view point of their suitability to the special needs of NER. The Ministries should prepare alternate/
sub-scheme for NER or have a broad based “umbrella scheme” within which individual projects suitable
for North East States could be implemented. The Line Ministries should, as far as possible, formulate
the schemes in consultation with the State Governments. The Committee is of the opinion that it would
be better if, under the broader guidelines, the State Governments are allowed to frame their own
schemes and States should have liberty in deciding the modus operandi for planning and implementation
of the programmes in the best interest of area specific requirements. In this regard, the Committee
welcomes the recent decision of the Government that State-specific guidelines within the overall core
guidelines of every Centrally Sponsored Scheme would be received from the States, in the first instance,
and would be looked into by a Committee comprising of Secretary, Planning Commission, the
Expenditure Secretary and the Chief Secretary or any other representative of the State so that the
schemes could be better tailored to the requirements of the States.  Another decision that there would
be a Flexi fund of ten per cent in each Centrally-Sponsored Scheme which would be available to the
State to try innovations and tailor these schemes to their own requirements is a step in right direction.
The Committee recommends that concerted steps be taken to implement the above decisions of the
Government at the earliest so that the grievances of State Governments in this regard are addressed
appropriately. (Paras 5.14.1)
Action Taken
1.12.2 All the Ministries/Departments concerned have been advised to take note of the observations
made by the Hon’ble Committee.
Recommendation
1.13 WITHHOLDING OF FUNDS
1.13.1 The Committee took note of the issue of holding of funds by State Governments. The Committee
takes into account the views of the Finance Secretary that the Government normally prescribe that the
money should go through the State Government and for any particular project, State Government must
release the fund within fifteen days time for that particular project and if the State Government fails
to do so, it has to pay penal interest on that amount. The Committee came across the specific case
where funds were transferred to Assam for the Bodoland Territorial Council under a package on the
basis of a peace accord signed by the Government and the funds were withheld for a considerable time.
However, some State Governments are averse to the idea of direct funding to the implementing agencies
and feel that the system of direct funding will have repercussions on the federal structure of the
Constitution and is fraught with chances of impropriety and will also reduce the oversight of the State
administration on the implementation of the directly funded projects/programmes. In view of the
Committee, this is a peculiar situation where the Central Government can’t do anything except appealing
the State Governments to release the funds. The Committee is therefore, of the view that the State
Governments must follow the guidelines of the Ministry of Finance for releasing the fund within fifteen
days time for any particular project. The Committee recommends that a system may be developed under

20
which all the State Governments must rationalize the existing process of repetitive clearance so that
money can be transferred to the implementing agencies as soon as it is received from Government of
India. (Para 5.20.1)
Action Taken
1.13.2 In the proposed simplified procedure, States shall release funds to the implementing agency
within a period 15 days from receipt from this Ministry. A copy of the release order shall be uploaded
on the NLCPR website and/or sent to the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region and will
be taken note of for further releases.
Recommendation
1.14 GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS
1.14.1 Besides the above mentioned issue specific recommendations, the Committee would also like to
make the following recommendations:
• There should be a separate fund of strategically national important projects in the region.
• Use of video-conferencing in various Ministries/Departments may be adopted with the
State Governments of the North Eastern Region as it takes officers one day to reach Delhi
and one day to come back for a meeting, apart from financial burden on the cash-
deficient States.
• It is relevant to point out that non-availability of construction materials is creating further
hurdle in the development drive. Non-availability of construction materials like cement,
steel etc. and long procurement time makes many projects especially the hydro projects
costly and unviable. The Committee feels the need for setting up industries for
construction material in NER to meet the infrastructural requirement. The Committee
desires that Ministry of DoNER should consult Ministry of Heavy Industry and Planning
Commission and draw a plan for setting up industries in NE Region.
• The Committee observes that Ministry of DoNER is still to come up with a regional
perspective plan to implement Vision-2020. The Committee therefore desired that a
comprehensive plan for NER development should be mooted by the Ministry of DoNER
with flexibility for State-specific modification.
• Provision for third party monitoring for quality and quantity of works of the projects
sanctioned by the Ministry of DoNER should be done by the States through their own
Consultants/Experts appointed by them.
• The Committee also takes note of the issues raised and suggestions made by various other
line Ministries/Departments.  The general issues raised by those Ministries have been dealt
under the various categories. In regard to the specific suggestions made by those Ministries
and the issues raised therein (the list is at Annexure- IV) the Committee desires that the
Ministry of DoNER may examine all the issues and take appropriate action in consultation
with the State Governments to address the issues.
(Para 5.25.1)

21
Action Taken
• Separate Fund for strategically national important projects:   Ministry of Finance has
since been apprised with the recommendations of the Committee.
• Use of Video Conferencing:  The facility of video conferencing is already in place in the
Ministry of DoNER. It will be ensured that maximum use of the same is made in
interacting with the State Governments of the North Eastern Region.

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS ON WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE
TO PURSUE THE MATTER IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
Recommendation
2.1 Detailed Project Reports (DPRs)
2.1.1 The Committee observes that the State Governments do not have sufficient wherewithal to make
proper analysis and investigations. This has been agreed by all sides. Because of this, most of the DPRs
submitted by the State Governments entail a lot of short comings. The Ministry of DoNER has to send
them to the States back again and again for clarifications and sometimes advise the States that they
should outsource this work so that State Governments can have inputs of experts in DPRs. The State
Governments on the other hand suggested for the preparation of DPRs only after the projects are
retained by the Ministry as it involves huge expenditure to prepare DPRs. The State Governments
suggested that the Ministry of DoNER should accept the idea of concept papers for proposing projects
under NLCPR and only after retention, the specific details in the form of DPRs may be called for . The
Committee is of the view that the Ministry of DoNER and Planning Commission should look into the
feasibility of the suggestion of the State Governments or else the State Governments should outsource
their DPRs to improve the quality. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of DoNER
in consultation with Planning Commission and the State Governments should workout the best course
in this regard so that unnecessary delays do not take place at the DPR stage itself.
2.1.2 The Committee takes note of the complaint of the line Ministries that while preparing DPRs,
the State Governments/agencies do not make proper survey and study of the local situation.  This leads
to cost escalation many a time.  This calls for development of efficient agencies for preparing DPRs
and outsourcing DPRs to them. Ministry of DoNER should prepare a plan and for this purpose and
get it implemented by States. The Committee feels that if the above recommendation is implemented,
this can be taken care of. (Paras 5.3.1 and 5.3.2)
Action Taken
2.1.3 The recommendation made by the Hon’ble Committee that the State Governments may be asked
to submit DPRs only after retention of projects based on the Concept Papers submitted by them, is
already in vogue. State Governments have also been advised to submit, alongwith with DPRs, all the
mandatory certificates viz. Environment and forest clearance, availability of land free from all
encumbrances,  non-duplication certificate and location of stone quarry, in case of road projects.  This
will considerably speed up the process of sanction and release. The Ministry has engaged PSUs for
expeditious vetting of DPRs submitted by the State Governments. The following measures have been
taken to optimally reduce the time taken for vetting of DPRs submitted by the State Governments:
(a) On receipt of DPRs from the State Governments, the Technical Wing of the Ministry of
DoNER will do the preliminary scrutiny. The consolidated  query, if any, of the Technical
Wing shall be given within 15 days to the Programme Division, which will be forwarded
22

23
online/through e-mail, to the State Planning and Implementing Department. In case the
reply is not received within the period of 15 days from receipt of query, it shall be
presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the project and the project will be
deleted within seven days thereafter without any further notice.
(b) On receipt of reply to the queries raised by the Technical Wing, the DPRs will be sent
to the vetting agency/line Ministries, with the request to vet the DPRs. The vetting agency
shall raise consolidated queries, if any, which will be forwarded to the State Government
through Ministry, which will be required to furnish replies to the same within a period of
15 days. If these queries are not settled within 15 days of communication, the State
Government will be given another 15 days for furnishing replies to the query from the
vetting agency, failing which it will presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the
project and the said project will stand rejected. However, if the State Government finds
it difficult to collect data for a reply and gives cogent and substantial reasons, further time
of up to 30 days may be provided and not beyond.
(c) Vetting agency will give techno-economic vetting of the projects within one month from
receipt of replies to the consolidated queries within a period one month. In case any further
query is raised because of unsatisfactory replies or issues arising, these should be settled
before or on the date the project is placed for sanction before the Screening Committee.
(d) The line Ministries/NITI Aayog/NEC will be approached in parallel for non-duplication
certificates and for certifying if the project is fit for gap funding. The line Ministries/NITI
Aayog/NEC shall give their comments/observations within one month else it will be
presumed to be clear for non-duplication and gap funding angle. In any event, these views
shall be finally provided at the time of project sanctions.
(e) NLCPR Committee meeting shall be convened periodically to consider sanctioning of the
cleared projects, duly vetted by the vetting agency.
2.1.4 Besides, the Ministry is in the process of developing through NIC, a Project Management
software for monitoring the implementation and execution of NLCPR funded projects.
Recommendation
2.2 ISSUES RELATED TO ENVIRONMENT/FOREST CLEARANCES
2.2.1 Regarding forest clearance at the State level and the Central level, the Committee finds that
time limits are generally not adhered to and they do not even have sub-limits. It appears that there is
no time limit for any particular agency to give the clearance. The Committee is, therefore, of the
opinion that the clearances should be given within the prescribed time limits and there should be sub-
limits for different stages. The time limit for the Central and State Governments and their concerned
agencies should be fixed and strictly adhered to.
2.2.2 The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Environment and Forest should apply
different standards in the cases of strategically important projects such as the ones located on
international borders or near to it, as these locations are of strategic importance for the safety and
security of the country. The absence of such infrastructure will severely hamper the movement of
artillery and logistics in times of border tension.

24
2.2.3 The Committee also desires that the Cabinet Secretary may hold review meetings particularly on
the projects pending for environmental clearances and issue instructions to Ministry of Environment and
Forests to give clearances within specific time limits.  The State Governments also need to be instructed
in this regard as all the projects, after all, are going to create assets in the respective States.  Ministry
of DoNER may take initiative in this regard and take up with the State Governments.
(Paras 5.6.1, 5.6.2 and 5.6.3 )
Action Taken
2.2.4 The NLCPR scheme is basically meant for bridging the infrastructure gaps in the NER. The
projects under the scheme are generally of smaller value. Clearance of such projects are normally well
within the delegated powers for grant of environment/forest clearance to the State Governments or
within the powers of regional offices. In case any reference comes to the Ministry of DoNER, the same
shall be co-ordinated, on case to case basis, by according highest priority.
Recommendation
2.3 MoUS FOR POWER TRANSMISSION
2.3.1 The Committee recommends that Ministry of DONER should tie up with NE States for quick
decision making for finalisation of MOUs for Power Transmission projects and for resolving issues like
Right of Way and forest clearance by the States. (Para 5.8.4)
Action Taken
2.3.2 Secretary, DoNER has taken a review of projects of Ministry of Power in NER on 02.09.2014.
During the review, Ministry of Power has stated that presently that Ministry is not facing any significant
road blocks in implementing its schemes in all North East States.
Recommendation
2.4 KEEPING NLCPR FUNDS IN A REVOLVING FUND
2.4.1 Regarding the suggestion that NLCPR funds should be kept in a Revolving Fund to be operated
by DoNER, and it should  be made available to the States based on their demand and capacity without
being constrained by yearly budgetary ceilings, the Committee agrees with the view of the Finance
Ministry that creating a Revolving Fund for NLCPR would practically be not feasible. It also agrees
with the view that such funds being made available based on demand and capacity of States without
constraint of yearly budgetary ceilings would have implications on Government of India finances,
adversely affecting fiscal deficit, etc., besides, withdrawals from such funds , in Public Account, would
also require Parliamentary approval. Keeping in mind such practical difficulties, the Committee
recommends that a better course of action is required to make line Ministries spend the mandatory
allocation for the North East, which will automatically result in lesser accruals to the NLCPR funds,
through administrative oversight mechanism having sufficient teeth to pressurize the line Ministries to
spend their share of money. The Committee is of the view that the Government should vigorously
sensitize Ministries to spend 10% GBS meant for NE States more quickly and effectively.
(Para 5.17.1)

25
Action Taken
2.4.2 Ministry of DoNER fully agrees with the views expressed by the Committee. The basic
objective of earmarking of at least 10% of GBS of the ministries is that each ministry should utilise
fund in the respective sectors for the North East so that every sector gets equal attention for overall
and balanced development of the region.
2.4.3 It is observed that wherever schematic guidelines of programmes are not suitable for the North
East utilisation of funds under such programmes invariably goes down resulting in transfer of unutilised
balance to the non-lapsable “notional pool”. In many cases the concerned ministries are also asking for
exemption of such schemes from earmarking for NER. The stand taken by Ministry of DoNER in such
cases is that the broad guidelines issued by the erstwhile Planning Commission mandates earmarking
10% of GBS allocation to the Ministries and does not require 10% schematic earmarking, which the
concerned Ministries can alone decide.  Ministries are invariably advised to formulate suitable schemes
for north east or modify schematic guidelines for better utilisation of earmarked fund. Some ministries
have also positively responded to M/o DoNER’s suggestion and changed the guidelines relating to
eligibility criteria or funding pattern. For example, eligibility criteria for PMGSY for unconnected
habitations was brought down from initial 500 persons to 250 persons for the North East. Similarly,
M/o Textiles formulated an umbrella scheme, namely, “North East Region Textile Promotion Scheme
(NERTPS)” to cover various sub-schemes for the North East. Subsequently, utilisation of funds for the
north east by the Ministry of Textiles is quite encouraging. There are number of schemes for which
funding pattern was changed for better utilisation.
2.4.4 Apart from sensitising the non-exempted Ministries and the States of North East, for better
utilisation of funds, Ministry of DoNER and NEC is focusing on the monitoring of utilisation on regular
basis. Web based information of the Ministry of Finance on schematic fund releases is a good source
of information on day to day monitoring and timely intervention by the ministries and the States. NEC
has already initiated sectoral programme reviews at the State level based on available information.
Recommendation
2.5 FINANCING PATTERN OF SCHEMES UNDER NLCPR
2.5.1 Most of the representatives of the State Governments expressed before the Committee their
inability to finance State share of 10 percent under NLCPR Schemes. Their grievance is that NLCPR
financing pattern of 90% grant and 10% loan implied borrowing of huge amounts of funds from open
markets to finance projects, thus proving a burden for the States’ finances. The State Governments felt
that the requirement of 10% loan component should be done away with so that the heavy financial
burden of the State can be eased. Various Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) administered by various
Central Ministries have varied funding patterns of 50:50, 75:25, 80:20, 90:10, and 100:00 etc. The
State Governments were of the view that since the requirement of the State share is met out of the
limited untied Plan Fund, the States are left with less funds for implementation of their own prioritised
schemes and projects. The State Governments, therefore, requested for full funding of the schemes/
projects.  The Committee, however, is not in agreement with the views of the State Governments and
is of the considered view that the State Governments should also show their involvement/interest/
ownership/commitment/participation in the implementation and execution  of the projects which could
only be ensured with their being financial  stakeholder in the projects. However, wherever the cost

26
escalation increases the share of the State, the Ministry of DoNER and Planning Commission may
consider the component of cost escalation to reduce the financial burden on the States.
(Para 5.18.1)
Action Taken
2.5.2 It is a fact that capacity to provide State share for a programme depend on the resource
position of the State as well as the funding pattern of various programmes implemented by the States.
It may be mentioned there is a drastic change in the pattern of resources flow to the States after the
14
th Finance Commission (FC) devolution. According to the Department of Expenditure, FC has
awarded devolution of Taxes @ 42% to the States in comparison to 32% recommended by the 13 th
FC. Further, the share of devolution of taxes to the North Eastern States, including Sikkim,
recommended by 14 th FC has been 7.91% as against 6.15% recommended by the 13 th FC. Therefore,
there will be significant enhancement of transfer of resources to NE States.  Apart from the Devolution
of Taxes, 14 th FC has recommended Revenue Deficit Grant to the eligible States.
2.5.3 However, S tates of NE have expressed their reservations about the enhancement in the
resources flow. According to them Central Assistance provided through certain plan programmes (like
Special Plan Assistance, Special Central Assistance, Normal Central Assistance and other block grant
programmes excluding NEC, NLCPR and ACA for EAP) has been de-linked from plan and subsumed
in the 14
th FC award resulting in shrinkage in the total flow of resources. States have also expressed
concern about likely change in the funding pattern of certain Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) and
committed liabilities of the delinked programmes. Presently, NITI Aayog has constituted a Sub-group
for consultation with the States on Rationalisation of CSS and funding pattern. The concerns expressed
by the NE States have been brought to the notice of NITI Aayog. It is expected that the final report
of the Sub-group will take into account the views expressed by the NE States.
2.5.4 Notwithstanding the facts explained above, the view expressed by the Committee with regard
to accommodating cost escalation of the sanctioned scheme in the scheme itself, it may be mentioned
that the extant NLCPR Guidelines have provision for bearing the cost escalation upto 10-20% of the
approved cost by the Ministry of DoNER and the State Government concerned as per the existing
pattern of funding
Recommendation
2.6 SEPARATION OF ALLOCATIONS FOR NLCPR AND NEC SCHEMES FROM ANNUAL
PLANS OF STATES
2.6.1 The Committee notes the overwhelming demand of the North Eastern States that the allocation
of NLCPR and NEC schemes, which have been included in the Annual Plan allocations during 2013-14,
should be separated from State Plan. According to the State Governments the present dispensation of
including NLCPR/NEC within the State Annual Plan would give rise to undue procedural delay as any
additionality over and above the projection made in the Plan would call for revision of State Plan and
thus obtaining of again a second approval from the Planning Commission. In their view resources of
Ministry of DoNER are distinct from and additional to what the States were entitled to get as part of
their normal planning process and devolution from the Planning Commission. By making them part of
the Plan outlays, the States have not only been denied their legitimate share in the plan resources meant
for the States, it had also affected their flexibility in use of these resources. The State Governments
were of the opinion that the Central Government should either revert to the earlier practice wherein

27
NEC and NLCPR outlays were kept beyond the ambit of State Plan or agree to this regime only if the
Ministry of DoNER was given a larger political role in deciding the developmental priorities of the
region and financial outlays under the Plan for the Region as a whole, as determined by the State
Governments through a democratic interaction with the Ministry of DoNER.
2.6.2 The Committee also notes the Comments of the Planning Commission that the inclusion of NEC
and NLCPR in the States’ Annual Plan is required. In the Union Budget, NEC and NLCPR have been
always a part of Central Assistance to State Plans and there has been omission to mention as such in
the Scheme of Financing of Annual Plans of NE States.  When this omission was pointed out in the
reconciliation process, the Central assistance on this account has been correctly reflected in States’
Annual Plans for 2013-14 fully in line with Union Budget approved by Parliament. This was a
misclassification in the accounts of the State Governments which had been rectified in the 12
th Plan.
2.6.3 The Committee is not satisfied with the explanation given by the Planning Commission as the
funds in the NLCPR are the unspent funds of the 10% allocations earmarked by different Ministries
each year, that too not surrendered at the end of the financial year, but treated as an amaanat for all
practical purposes to finish the incomplete works. The Committee also notes the protest of the Ministry
of DoNER in this regard and is of the considered view that the principle and objective behind NEC
and NLCPR schemes are to fill critical gaps in normal developmental schemes and, consequently, NEC
and NLCPR have been treated as complement to normal Plan programmes, as stated in the NLCPR
guidelines....”Funds available under the Central Pool are not meant to supplement the normal Plan
Programmes either of the State Governments or Union Ministries/Departments/Agencies”. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the funds released under NLCPR and NEC schemes should be
over and above the allocations made to State Governments of the North-Eastern Region in their Annual
Plans and the practice of including allocations for NLCPR and NEC schemes in the Annual Plans of
States should be discontinued henceforth. (Paras 5.19.1, 5.19.2 and 5.19.3)
Action Taken
2.6.4 With regard to Separation of Allocations for NLCPR and NEC Schemes from Annual Plans of
States, it may be mentioned that NEC and NLCPR provisions are part of the Central Assistance to the
States (or State Plan fund) and reflected in the Demand for Grants of DoNER and in Statement 16
on Central Assistance to State Plan of Expenditure Budget), which were not reflected in the Scheme
of Financing (SOF) of States’ Annual Plan till 2012-13. Planning Commission mentioned that when this
omission was pointed out by the Ministry of Finance in the reconciliation process, the Central assistance
on this account was correctly reflected in States’ Annual Plans since 2013-14 in line with Union budget
approved by Parliament.
2.6.5 When NEC and NLCPR provision was included as part States Annual Plan in the (SOF) of
2013-14, the States of NE objected to Planning Commission stating that these amount was coming as
“additionality” to the states. Though in practice, while submitting expenditure statements the State
Governments always included as part of States Plan.  Since 2014-15 the whole process of allocation
of schematic fund undergone a change due to rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS),
which was completed in June, 2013. In 2014-15, CSS numbering 146 was brought down to 66 CSS
and decision was also to provide the fund as ‘Central Assistance to State Plan’. Thus since 2014-15
not only NEC and NLCPR but also 66 CSS became part of SOF for the States’ Annual Plan.

28
Further Observation
2.6.6 The Committee, in its meeting held on 27 th July, 2015, came across the suggestion of
separation of allocation of NLCPR and NEC scheme from the annual plan of States.  The
Committee observes that against allocation of ````` 230 crore for the year 2014-15 under NLCPR
for the Government of Nagaland only ````` 54 crore was released thus leaving shortfall of 76%
of the sanctioned amount thereby instilling a huge deficit causing great concern and loss for
a resource constrained State i.e. Nagaland which ultimately to led to accumulation of in
completed projects and retained projects.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that to
improve the process of selection and implementation of projects, the funds available for
NLCPR and NEC may be sub allocated to NER States upfront i.e. at the beginning of the
financial year so that State Government must be aware of funding pattern well in advance.
This will allow them to make ‘Priority List’ of the projects besides ensuring enhanced active
participation of States besides retaining the power of sanctioning and supervision of projects
under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of DoNER.
Recommendation
2.7 Delay in Land Acquisition and Inclusion of Land Cost in Projects.
2.7.1 The Committee notes that most projects have a precondition that the land should be made
available by the State Governments. However, North Eastern State Governments are reluctant on this
part on the ground that with increasing pressure on land and loss of land due to erosion, it is becoming
increasingly difficult for the States to fulfill this criterion. At times, the land is available at unviable
locations. The State Governments viewed that Ministry of DoNER should incorporate the land cost in
the projects. It should also help NER States to procure land for projects given by other line Ministries.
The Committee came across the issue related to land acquisition, in Arunachal Pradesh, where public
hearing, the first and foremost procedure for land acquisition, had to be postponed twelve times and
finally was held after a lot of persuasions. The Committee agrees with the Cabinet Secretary that only
States ought to address the issue since the major projects are essentially executed through the State
PWDs.
2.7.2 The Committee is in agreement to general principle that for all the Central Sector and the
Centrally Sponsored Schemes, land should be provided by the State Governments as this is essential to
make the State Governments committed. The Committee therefore recommends that the State
Governments should provide land for the projects as the projects are meant for the overall economic
development of the North East Region. (Paras 5.21.1 and 5.21.2)
Action Taken
2.7.3 This has already been made as a pre-condition for sanctioning new projects.
Recommendation
2.8 INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISM
2.8.1 The Committee is surprised to find that although according to the present system, the plenary
session of the North-Eastern Council, is supposed to happen twice in a year, it is being held only once
in a year and there is no time for review, and, only when the Secretary, DoNER or the Secretary, NEC

29
visits the States, they review it.  The Committee feels that institutional mechanism may be created under
NEC for review of projects more frequently and regularly. (Para 5.24.3)
Action Taken
2.8.2 The mandate of North Eastern Council is to function as a regional planning body for North
Eastern Region. North Eastern Council is a statutory body, created through an act of Parliament viz.
NEC Act, 1971,  headed by Hon’ble Minister, DoNER and comprising Governors and Chief Ministers
of the eight NE States as Members and precedes creation of Ministry of DoNER in 2004. The efforts
of NEC and Ministry of DoNER are complementary in nature and perfect synergy exists between the
two organisations.
2.8.3 As already explained above (in the action taken statement on 5.17.1) is  the common interest
for both DoNER and NEC to synergise the efforts for working out a regional planning and focus on
better utilisation of earmarked funds for the NER focusing on the monitoring of utilisation on regular
basis for overall development of the region.
Recommendation
2.9 SYNERGY BETWEEN NEC AND MINISTRY OF DONER
2.9.1 The Committee observes that the NEC has the Governors and the Chief Ministers of the NE
States as its members. The State Governments made a complaint that it should not be reduced to the
level of a Directorate under a Ministry of the Government of India rather it should have an appropriate
status and power to make decisions and provide the required funds for the development of the Region.
The Committee further notes that the NEC has the technical manpower for most of the sectors, however
main constraint with the NEC lies in its limited budgetary outlays and the inflexible sectoral approach
followed by the NEC in allocation to States. A State Government suggested that this can easily be
overcome if synergy is generated between the two bodies and united and integrated approach is adopted.
While the outlays of the NEC can be a part of the overall outlays of the Ministry of DoNER, the
decision making process in respect of allocations and schematic or sectoral priorities could be
democratised through the NEC which  should continue to play its active role as regional Planning Body.
Another suggestion was also made that the NEC may act as the Standing Council or Consultative Body
for the Ministry of DoNER and the Ministry itself could be located in Shillong with its headquarters
in the present NEC. This will help a strong organisational structure grow within a democratic set up
with proper financial outlays, competent technical manpower and delivery mechanisms.  The Committee
desires that the suggestions may be examined thoroughly by the Government and steps may be taken
early to bring synergy. (Para 5.24.4)
Action Taken
2.9.2 The mandate of North Eastern Council is to function as a regional planning body for North
Eastern Region. North Eastern Council is a statutory body, created through an act of Parliament viz.
NEC Act, 1971,  headed by Hon’ble Minister, DoNER and comprising Governors and Chief Ministers
of the eight NE States as Members and precedes creation of Ministry of DoNER in 2004. The efforts
of NEC and Ministry of DoNER are complementary in nature and synergy is continually promoted in
the efforts of the two organisations.

CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE
GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
Recommendation
3.1 FINAL APPROVED COST OF PROJECTS
3.1.1 The Committee notes that in some cases final approved cost of projects based on techno vetting
from Line Ministries differ from the projected estimated cost in the DPR, and the deleted components
are not informed to the State Governments, thus creating  problems in implementation. The State
Governments have strongly objected to this. The Committee, in this connection, recommends that the
State Governments should be kept well informed about the whole process so that they get enough time
to adjust for better implementation of the projects.  The Planning Commission and Ministry of DoNER
should address this issue appropriately. (Para 5.3.5)
Action Taken
3.1.2 Detailed components of the sanctioned projects are reflected in the administrative/financial
sanctions.
Further Recommendation
3.1.3 The Committee reiterates its recommendation that the final approved cost of the projects must
be communicated to the State Government well in advance so that project gets a take off without
financial snags. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of Finance, NITI
Aayog and the line Ministries should take care of grievances of the State Government on this count
and accordingly redress the grievances by apprising the State Government of information about the
whole process of finalization of cost of the projects well in advance so that the State Government get
enough time for suitable amendment in their project plan for better execution of the project.
Recommendation
3.2 ARBITAARY RETENTION AND SANCTIONING OF PROJECTS
3.2.1 Several State Governments brought to the notice of the Committee that there were many cases
where the retention and sanctioning of projects by the Ministry of DoNER were found to be arbitrary.
The Committee is anguished to note an instance, where a road project of 62 kms. was retained in two
phases (31 km. each for 
` 31 crore each), whereas, sanction was approved for only the Phase II of
31 kms. after reduction of almost ` 10 crore from the detailed estimate of the DPR. The Committee
also notes another instance where only a small length out of the proposed road projects was retained,
which was totally illogical. The Committee feels that such arbitrary retention of projects and
unreasonable sanctioning of projects with much lower cost as compared to the proposed amount in the
DPR would be detrimental to the creation of infrastructure. The Committee feels that completion of
30

31
many projects had been stalled due to this reason. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that
the Ministries should avoid adopting such irrational and arbitrary approach and also to be more
realistic in allocating funds considering the topography of the region.
(Para 5.3.6)
Action Taken
3.2.2 Retention and sanction of projects by the Empowered Committee is contingent on a variety of
factors inter alia including availability of funds, ceilings for a particular State Government for retention,
relative backwardness of district, priority given by the State Governments etc. There is no ground for
arbitrariness since the State Government representatives are invariably present in the meetings of the
inter-Ministerial NLCPR Committee. Further, the State Government have been advised to submit Priority
Lists within the overall allocation available to them and covering all the sectors.  This will discourage
skewed selection of projects by the States. To further strengthen and streamline the procedure, Chief
Secretary/Planning Secretary/Departmental Secretary (when concerned) shall alone attend the meeting of
the NLCPR Committee, convened for initial screening of concept papers and later for sanction of
finalised DPRs of the projects included for the State. In case these officers are unable to attend the
meeting, another authorised representative, who is able to take on the spot decisions, may alone attend
the meeting.  In case the authorised representative is unable to satisfactorily answer the queries of the
Committee, the project shall be rejected as unsupported and the funds diverted to next in priority or
to approved projects of other States.
Further Recommendation
3.2.3 The Committee is of the view that the contention of NER State Governments about the
sanctioning of projects with much lower cost as compared to the proposed amount in the DPR
must be examined carefully keeping in account all cost consideration and ensuring that the final
approved cost of the project should not have a bearing on quality of infrastructure creation as
that may pose a great threat/hurdle to development process in NER.
Recommendation
3.3 POWER SECTOR
3.3.1 The Committee takes note of the suggestion of the Ministry of Power that in order to improve
the power situation in the North-Easter Region, there is a need for a comprehensive plan for laying
adequate road network in a time-bound manner to expedite the development of projects in the North-
East as these projects are located in very remote places.  The Committee feels that roads are required
for not only power sector but for overall development of North East.  Various agencies like the Border
Roads Organisation, Ministry of Roads and Highways, State PWDs, etc. need to work in a coordinated
manner for this purpose. (Para 5.8.1)
Action Taken
3.3.2 Ministry of DoNER equally shares the need for a comprehensive plan for laying adequate road
network in a time-bound manner to expedite the development of projects in NER and also the need of
working in coordinated manner by Border Road Organization (BRO), Ministry of Road Transport and
Highways (MoRTH), State Public Works Departments so that power situation in the North Eastern
Region gets improved. Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has already constituted a Committee

32
to review progress of all road projects essential for development of hydro projects in Arunachal Pradesh
in a time-bound manner on 09-12-2013 with the following composition:-
(i) Secretary, RT&H – Chairman
(ii) Director General (Border Roads)

3.6 OBSERV ANCE OF NLCPR GUIDELINES
3.6.1 The Committee has come across the fact that delay in vetting of DPRs by line Ministries

change in Schedule of Rates (SoR).  In fact, the Ministry of DoNER is dependent on line
Ministries for vetting of DPRs under NLCPR Scheme.  The representatives of various State
Governments  also deliberated before the Committee in detail that delay caused in vetting of DPRs
due to repeated observations or otherwise results into further delayed sanctioning of projects which
at time causes time and cost overruns. It has come to the notice of the Committee that retained
NLCPR projects are cleared after 3 or 4 years which creates lots of difficulty as there are no takers
for the projects due to escalation of costs. The Co mmittee also notes the c omplaint of State
Governments regarding the nature of the observations conveyed to the States by the line Ministries
which are at times arbitrary, irrelevant, and not concerned to civil works matters (especially those
from the CPWD). The State Governments observe that DPRs for NLCPR projects are prepared
based on the Guidelines for Administration of NLCPR.  However, DPRs are being revised umpteen
times due to the fact that the reports were subjected to scrutiny against arbitrary standards which
were not specified in the Ministry’ s Guidelines. The State Governments are of the view that the role
of the technical vetting authority for DPRs of NLCPR projects is to examine the broad outline
feasibility and correctness of the DPR instead of raising observations on a particular drawing/
estimate being countersigned or not, or raising arbitrary observations. The Committee views that
undue delay in vetting of DPRs necessitates revision in Administrative and Financial approval
which finally delays completion of projects abnormally. The Committee recommends that the
Ministries should stick to Guidelines for Administration of NLCPR and avoid arbitrariness in their
observations for timely clearances of projects. (Para 5.15.1)
Action Taken

3.7 TECHNICAL WING IN MINISTRY OF DONER
3.7.1 The Committee received the suggestion for establishment of a full fledged Technical Wing
in the Ministry of DoNER for timely vetting of DPRs, which was in fact taken up  by Ministry
of DoNER with Committee of Secretaries (CoS).  The CoS considered the issue and observed that,
“it would not be practical to establish an elaborate technical wing in Ministry of DoNER,
possessing all the skills to examine the various types of projects, as it would invariably lead to
under employment as well as unnecessary duplication of the available manpower resources in the
Government”. The CoS desired that the Ministry of DoNER would initiate measures to have its own
small complement of technical manpower for preliminary checking of the projects and the cost
estimates. Accordingly, Ministry of DoNER established a Technical Wing in the Ministry in January,
2010 headed by Superintending Engineer with an Executive Engineer and 2 Assistant Engineers.
The Committee, however , wonders to find that as per CPWD norms SE is competent to issue
technical sanctions of projects upto 2.5 crore only, whereas, minimum cost of projects to be
considered for funding under NLCPR Scheme is 
` 3.00 crore, therefore, services of Technical Wing
remains underutilized.
3.7.2 The Committee feels that Technical Wing in the Ministry of DoNER needs to be
strengthened to obviate the present circumstances and to ensure expeditious vetting of DPRs under
NLCPR Scheme.  Technical Wing may be vested with full powers for issue of technical sanctions
of projects under NLCPR Scheme along with appropriate number of Executive Engineers and
Assistant Engineers of mixed discipline.  Such arrangements would curb unnecessary delays in

Ministries be assigned time bound targets for techno-economic vetting of DPRs. The issue of doing
away with the current practice of obtaining techno-economic feasibility from the line Ministries at
least for smaller projects may be examined. The Committee is in agreement with the views of the
Ministry of DoNER that routine observations of repetitive nature must be avoided and DPRs may
be corrected at Ministry’ s level to achieve timeline of two months.
(Paras 5.16.1 and 5.16.2)

Action Taken
3.7.3 The services of the Technical Wing will be utilised for preliminary scrutiny of DPRs and
close monitoring of the projects in coordination with North Eastern Council, Shillong. Besides,
the Technical Wing will also scrutinise the Concept Papers, furnished by the State Governments
at initial stage itself so as to provide guidance to the State in proper formulation of project
proposals.
3.7.4 The Ministry has engaged PSUs for expeditious vetting of DPRs submitted by the State
Governments. The following measures have also been taken to optimally reduce the time taken for
vetting of DPRs submitted by the State Governments:-
(a) On receipt of DPRs from the State Governments, the Technical Wing of the Ministry
of DoNER will do the preliminary scrutiny.  The consolidated  query, if any, of the
Technical Wing shall be given within 15 days to the Programme Division, which will
be forwarded online/through e-mail, to the State Planning and Implementing
Department. In case the reply is not received within the period of 15 days from
receipt of query, it shall be presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the
project and the project will be deleted within seven days thereafter without any further
notice.
(b) On receipt of reply to the queries raised by the Technical Wing, the DPRs will be sent
to the vetting agency/line Ministries, with the request to vet the DPRs. The vetting
agency shall raise consolidated queries, if any, which will be forwarded to the State
Government through Ministry, which will be required to furnish replies to the same
within a period of 15 days. If these queries are not settled within 15 days of
communication, the State Government will be given another 15 days for furnishing
replies to the query from the vetting agency, failing which it will presumed that the
State is not interested to pursue the project and the said project will stand rejected.
However, if the State Government finds it difficult to collect data for a reply and gives
cogent and substantial reasons, further time of up to 30 days may be provided and
not beyond.
(c) V etting agency will give techno-economic vetting of the projects within one month
from receipt of replies to the consolidated queries within a period of one month. In
case any further query is raised because of unsatisfactory replies or issues arising,
these should be settled before or on the date the project is placed for sanction before
the Screening Committee.
(d) The line Ministries/NITI Aayog/NEC will be approached in parallel for non-duplication
certificates and for certifying if the project is fit for gap funding. The line Ministries/
NITI Aayog/NEC shall give their comments/observations within one month else it will
be presumed to be clear for non-duplication and gap funding angle. In any event,
these views shall be finally provided at the time of project sanctions.
(e) NLCPR Committee meeting shall be convened periodically to consider sanctioning of
the cleared projects, duly vetted by the vetting agency.

3.9 MERGER OF NEC WITH MINISTRY OF DONER AND SHIFTING ITS
HEADQUARTERS TO SHILLONG
3.9.1 The Committee considered in detail the issue of merger of NEC with the Ministry of DoNER
and shifting of its headquarters to Shillong on the anology of the Space Department and
Department of Atomic energy and designating the Secretary to the Ministry of DoNER as  ex-
officio Secretary of NEC.  The argument put forth was that Ministry of DoNER has to play
coordinating role with the State Governments and oversee/monitor the execution of projects which
can better be done from Shillong rather than Delhi.  The Committee considered the views of the
Cabinet Secretary on the role of the Ministry of DoNER as coordinating Ministry and according
to him the coordination can be best done from Delhi where other Ministries are located and shifting
of the headquarters on the analogy of the Space Department and Atomic Energy, would not really
be an overall great advantage because State Governments are doing a lot of execution. The
Cabinet Secretary felt that the Ministry of DoNER should continue to remain in the national
capital.  The Committee also takes note of the views of  the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER that
only problem in shifting the Ministry of DoNER would be that the Secretary in the Ministry of
DoNER has to attend meetings in the Committee of Secretaries, Cabinet meetings and it would be
difficult for the Secretary to shuffle from Shillong to Delhi. The Committee would also like to
underline the submission of the DoNER Secretary that ‘otherwise there would be better synergy’.
3.9.2 The Committee is of the strong view that if the headquarters of the Ministry of DoNER is
shifted to Shillong, it would be in a better position to monitor the effective implementation of
projects due to on-the-spot supervision. Therefore, the Committee is not in agreement with the views
of Cabinet Secretary. The Committee is of the considered view that on-the-spot supervision and
monitoring would inject better synergy in the overall execution of the projects.  With the
Headquarters at Shillong, the Officers of the Ministry would be more accountable and more
focussed to their duties. Headquarters of the Ministry at Shillong would also provide opportunity
to the Officers of the Ministry to have frequent interaction with the officers of the State
Governments and implementing agencies. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Government may consider shifting the headquarters of the Ministry of DoNER to Shillong and have
a camp office in Delhi to facilitate meeting with other Ministries or organizations in Delhi.
(Paras 5.23.1 and 5.23.2)
Action Taken
3.9.3 The Cabinet Secretary has already put the views of Government in this regard before the
Parliamentary Committee.  During his evidence before the Committee he has already stated that
Ministry of DoNER being a coordinating Ministry, co-ordination could best be done from Delhi
where other Ministries are located and thus shifting of the Ministry on the analogy of Department
of Space and Department of Atomic Energy would not be of much advantage and thus Ministry

39
of DoNER should continue to remain in the national capital. Even the effectiveness of Regional

3.9.4 The Committee observes/finds the dichotomy of opinion amongst two organs of the

only problem in shifting of the Ministry of DoNER from national capital to Shillong would
be that Secretary, Ministry of DoNER had to attend the meeting of the Committee of the
Secretaries (CoS), otherwise there would be better-synergy in working of Ministry of DoNER
as coordinating role with State Government and monitoring the execution of projects due to
better on-the-spot supervision while on the other hand, the Cabinet Secretary had advanced
the view before the Committee that coordination should be best done from Delhi where
other line Ministries are located. The Committee in its 173rd Report made its
recommendation striking a balance amongst the views of Cabinet Secretary and the
Ministry of DoNER that headquarter of the Ministry be shifted to Shillong with a camp
office at Delhi.  In response to the Committee’s recommendation the Ministry of DoNER
is now back tracking from its earlier stand and is advancing the views of the Cabinet
Secretary and thus sculting  the merit of subject and without due scrutiny/examination. The
Committee, in this backdrop, reiterates its recommendation as made in Para 5.23.2 of 173rd
Report.
3.9.5 The Committee further reiterates its recommendation for merger of NEC with the
Ministry of DoNER and designating the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER as the ex-officio

3.10 ROLES OF MINISTRY OF DONER AND NEC AND SYNERGY BETWEEN THEM
3.10.1 It was admitted before the Committee by the Secretary, DoNER that the Ministry of DoNER
and the North-Eastern Council (NEC) combined together contributed less than four per cent of the
total fund flow to the North-Eastern Region in the Eleventh Five Year Plan.  Thus the impact of
NEC and the Ministry of DoNER in financial terms is very marginal. The North Eastern States also
have a feeling that the Ministry of DoNER is still acting as a distant arm of the central line
Ministries. It merely represents them in choosing and implementing projects and it has not been able
to play a proactive role in planning and implementing the Central projects/schemes/policies
implemented in the NE States. The State Governments also feel that the existence of the Ministry
of  DoNER, has, also led the line Ministries to neglect their responsibilities for the development
of the region, leaving it all to the Ministry of DoNER with its meager NLCPR resources. The
Committee also notes that the Cabinet Secretariat has denied this and stated that the percentage
utilization of 10% earmarked allocation has been increasing steadily over the past ten years.
3.10.2 The Committee, however, agrees that the Ministry of DoNER has not been able to play the
role assigned to it very effectively because of various factors discussed in the proceeding

40
paragraphs. However , the Committee is of the view that the Ministry of DoNER can play a bigger
and effective role in shaping the regional developmental priorities and implementing the regional
or State-specific programmes and projects. Active involvement of the Ministry of DoNER is a
precondition in deciding the policies, programmes, schemes, and projects by the Planning
Commission and line Ministries meant for NE region. The Committee, therefore, is of the strong
view that there is urgent need to review and redefine the role of the Ministry of DoNER in
coordinating and liaising with the line Ministries.   There should be a clear cut defined relationship
between the Planning Commission, the Ministry of DoNER, and the NEC for dovetailing and
synergizing of developmental plans, projects, and schemes and a mechanism for such coordination
should be evolved. The Committee is of the considered view that the Secretary, DoNER should be
equipped with more administrative and sanctioning powers to facilitate the smooth implementation
of developmental projects. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should
expand its project portfolio to include projects other than infrastructure sector, including projects
in tourism, agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry etc., besides loan linkages for these sectors.
(Paras 5.24.1 and 5.24.2)

Ministries has undertaken a number of measures from the stage of conceptualization of
scheme, preparation and submission of priority list, expeditious processing/execution of

for preparing and submission and vetting of DPRs, sanctioning, allocation and release of

would like to be apprised of perceptible outcome of the measures so undertaken on the
ground level in the form of period of time reduced in clearance of projects and its
completion in comparison to pre and post reforms phase on removal of all unnecessary
procedural delays.  The kernel spirit of the Committee’s recommendation made in para
5.2.1 of the Committee’s 173 rd Report is to give fillip to developmental process in NER
through procedural facilitation and timely implementation of policies, programmes, schemes
and projects meant for all round balanced development of the region.
(Para 1.1.8)

issue of revisiting the instant specification in guidelines for reserving 25% of new projects

should be considered at the earliest and the same may be laid down in the NLCPR
guidelines. (Para 1.1.10)
The Committee observes that no guidelines have been set up on frequency of
meeting of the NLCPR Committee and timeline for consideration  and sanctioning of

be convened periodically with a set time frame, known to the State Governments so that

SEPARATION OF ALLOCATIONS FOR NLCPR AND NEC SCHEMES FROM ANNUAL PLANS
OF STATES
The Committee, in its meeting held on 27
th July, 2015, came across the suggestion
of separation of allocation of NLCPR and NEC scheme from the annual plan of States.  The
Committee observes that against allocation of ````` 230 crore for the year 2014-15 under
NLCPR for the Government of Nagaland only ````` 54 crore was released thus leaving shortfall
of 76% of the sanctioned amount thereby instilling a huge deficit causing great concern and
loss for a resource constrained State i.e. Nagaland which ultimately to led to accumulation

This will allow them to make ‘Priority List’ of the projects besides ensuring enhanced active
participation of States besides retaining the power of sanctioning and supervision of projects
under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of DoNER. (Para 2.6.6)

44
FINAL APPROVED COST OF PROJECTS
The Committee reiterates its recommendation that the final approved cost of the
projects must be communicated to the State Government well in advance so that project
gets a take off without financial snags.  The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends
that the Ministry of Finance, NITI Ayog and the line Ministries should take care of
grievances of the State Government on this count and accordingly redress the grievances by
apprising the State Government of information about the whole process of finalization of
cost of the projects well in advance so that the State Government get enough time for
suitable amendment in their project plan for better execution of the project. (Para  3.1.3)
ARBITARY RETENTION AND SANCTIONING OF PROJECTS
The Committee is of the view that the contention of NER State Governments about
the sanctioning of projects with much lower cost as compared to the proposed amount in the
DPR must be examined carefully keeping in account all cost consideration and ensuring that
the final approved cost of the project should not have a bearing on quality of infrastructure
creation as that may pose a great threat/hurdle to development process in NER.
(Para  3.2.3)
POWER SECTOR
The Committee understands that there is need to give boost to the transport and
communication infrastructure, thereby requiring Comprehensive Plan for laying road
network in a time bound manner to expedite the development of the projects in far-flung
areas of NER and accordingly it has recommended for striking a coordinated and
collaborative working in this direction. The Committee recommends that operational
efficiency of implementing agencies viz. BRO is required to be enhanced.  The Committee
further recommends that undertaken course of action must entail perceptile changes on the
ground level, thereby requiring also that the Ministry of Power and the Ministry of DoNER
must work in tandem to ensure optimum utilization of power generation potential in a time
bound manner as continued supply of power is itself a basic infrastructure for other
industries and development projects. (Para  3.3.4)
AGGREGATE TECHNICAL AND COMMERCIAL (AT&C) LOSSES
The Committee notes that the progress of major physical activities under
Restructured Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programmes (R-APDRP) by the
NER  States are at various stages of completion.  The Committee impresses that all out
efforts should be taken for expeditious completion of physical activities so that Aggregate
Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses are minimized/eliminated in NER.  The Committee
alos recommends that the Ministry of DoNER must impress upon the State Governments of
Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland submission of DPRs of part B projects for sanctioned to
enable the Ministry of Power to push reform programme in the direction of minimization
of distribution losses without further delay. (Para  3.5.4)
ENHANCING OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY OF BORDER ROAD ORGANISATION
The Committee expresses its anguish to observe the evasive reply of Ministry of
DoNER.  The representatives of Government of Sikkim in Committee’s meeting held on

45
27th July, 2015 stated about operation efficiency of BRO i.e. limitation of 10 kms of road
construction by a single unit of BRO in a year which is in fact, also in the Committee’s
view point not at all impressive but rather disturbing.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates
its recommendation that the Ministry of DoNER take follow up action with MORTH
suggesting BRO for undertaking requisite steps for enhancing its operational efficiency for
meaningful completion of road project within set time frame. (Para  3.6.3)
OBSERVANCE OF NLCPR GUIDELINES
The Committee’s takes notes of merits of simplified procedure with regard to NLCPR
scheme, however, the Committee desires that line Ministry should adhere in relation to
vetting of DPRs of NLCPR projects to examine the broad outline feasibility and correctness
of DPRs, as per the guidelines for administration of NLCPR and avoid arbitrariness and
irrelevant observation for speedy clearance of projects and thereafter completion of projects
without time and cost overruns.  The Committee in its meeting held on 27
th July, 2015
during its interaction with representative of Government of Nagaland came across instances
of procedural delay due to retention of 37 projects of Government of Nagaland from
2010-11 till 2014-15 because vetting process kept on going as there was no time limit set
for vetting up DPRs. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation made in
Para 5.15.1 and recommends further that the Ministry of DoNER should examine the
possibility of outsourcing vetting of DPRs to competent public sector agencies like
W APCOS, NAPCONS, National Institute of Technology, Jorhat (Regional Engineering
College)  for speedy vetting of infrastructure projects. (Para  3.7.3)
TECHNICAL WING IN MINISTRY OF DONER
The Committee takes into account the details of timeline arrangement made for the
speedy implementation of project, however, is of the opinion that the purpose of setting up
the technical wing in the Ministry gets defeated due to lack of administrative power to
Superintendent Engineer to issue technical sanction of projects upto 2.5 crore only whereas
the minimum cost of the project to be considered for funding under NLCPR scheme is
` 3 crore, thereby, nullifying the role of technical wing in the Ministry of DoNER.  The
Committee finds that the Ministry of DoNER is silent in its ATN over the issue of need for
strenghthing of technical wing of the Ministry of DoNER, while the State Government of
NER are in agreement to the Committee’s recommendation made in Para 5.16.2 of 173
rd
Report. Therefore, the Committee reiterates its recommendation and desires that Ministry
of DoNER must reconsider its decision and accordingly apprise the Committee.
(Para  3.8.5)
COMMITTED FUNDING FOR NORTH EASTERN REGION
The Committee notes that the Ministry of DoNER has asked Planning Commission
(NITI Ayog) Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Railways to take the appropriate action
to eliminate the communication gap amongst those Ministries so far the issue of committed
finance for development of NER States is concerned.  However, the Committee feels that
the role of Ministry of DoNER does not end here just acting like a post office. It should
facilitate meetings of these Ministries to sort out the problem of fund to complete the

46
undertaken projects with a designated time frame or enhance executive capabilities as
pointed out by the Secretary, Department of Expenditure that it is not the lack of funds but
the lack of execution capabilities that is hindering the effective implementation of projects
in NER.  The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of DoNER must
proactively act in the matter. (Para  3.9.3)
MERGER OF NEC WITH MINISTRY OF DONER AND SHIFTING ITS HEADQUARTERS TO
SHILLONG
The Committee observes/finds the dichotomy of opinion amongst two organs of the
Government i.e. on the one hand Ministry of DoNER deposed before the Committee that the
only problem in shifting of the Ministry of DoNER from national capital to Shillong would
be that Secretary, Ministry of DoNER had to attend the meeting of the Committee of the
Secretaries (CoS) , otherwise there would be better -synergy in working of Ministry of
DoNER as coordinating role with State Government and monitoring the execution of projects
due to better on the spot supervision while on the other hand, the Cabinet Secretary had
advanced the view before the Committee that coordination should be best done from Delhi
where other line Ministries are located.  The Committee in its 173
rd Report made its
recommendation striking a balance amongst the views of Cabinet Secretary and the
Ministry of DoNER that headquarter of the Ministry be shifted to Shillong with a camp
office at Delhi.  In response to the Committee’s recommendation the Ministry of DoNER
is now back tracking from its earlier stand and is advancing the views of the Cabinet
Secretary and thus sculting  the merit of subject and without due scrutiny/examination. The
Committee, in this backdrop, reiterates its recommendation as made in Para 5.23.2 of 173
rd
Report. (Para  3.10.4)
The Committee further reiterates its recommendation for merger of NEC with the
Ministry of DoNER and designating the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER as the ex-officio
Secretary of NEC.  The Committee is of the view that the measure would enable the
Ministry of DoNER to have holistic planning for balanced economic development of NER.
(Para  3.10.5)
ROLES OF MINISTRY OF DONER AND NEC AND SYNERGY BETWEEN THEM
The Committee finds that the Ministry of DoNER has just indicated that the Ministry
is expanding its project -portfolios in certain fields viz. Animal Husbandary, Organic
Farming, horticulture and Rural livelihood but has not apprised the Committee of action
taken even in brief in these field and the outcome thereof. (Para  3.11.4)
The Committee further observes that the Government has not furnished its action
taken details even the views on the Committee’s recommendation on enhancing
administrative and sanctioning powers to facilitate the speedy and effective implementation
of development plan/projects/scheme/programme. The Committee, in this regard, in
conformity to the view of Government of Sikkim as expressed in Committee’s meeting held
on 27 th July, 2015 reiterates its recommendation that the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER
should have more administrative and sanctioning powers for entailing a booster dose to
development process in NER States. (Para  3.11.5)

47
The Committee is express its concern to observe that Government in its action taken
notes has not furnished any information on steps taken in regard to Committee’s
recommendation for strengthening the role of Ministry and measures undertaken/being
undertaken for striking operational synergy between the Ministry of DoNER and NEC. The
Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation as made in Para 5.24.1 and suggests
that the Ministry of DoNER must play pro-action role. (Para  3.11.6)

5.1 Initiating the discussion, the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER apologized for the unsatisfactory

steps taken in the last one year on strengthening the functioning of Ministry of DoNER like
advancing the timeline for project approval for expeditious implementation of projects, urging the
States and contractors to use software for preparation and vetting of DPRs for higher efficiency.

in preparation and vetting of DPRs, representation of States in NLCPR standing Committee etc. on
which they found the Ministry’s reply unsatisfactory. The Chairman then sought to know the
opinion of the representatives of State Governments on the various issues.

5.3  The Chief Secretaries of Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh expressed their concern regarding
the delay in appraisal and retention of projects at the level of Ministry of DoNER and line Ministries
not giving priority to projects of North Eastern States which leads to inordinate delays. The
representatives of Nagaland, Manipur and Sikkim pointed out the issues like retention of projects
without sanction by the Ministry, the NLCPR and NEC schemes continuing to be the part of the
annual plan of the State in spite of Committee’s recommendation to the contrary, uncertainty of
fund flows, strengthening of technical wing of Ministry of DoNER, representation of State
Governments in NLCPR Committee etc.

on the issues highlighted by the State Governments’ representatives.

CHAPTER I
BACKGROUND ON CYCLONE ‘HUDHUD’
1.1 INTRODUCTION
1.1.1 The Ministry of Home Affairs in its background note apprised the Committee that in the morning
of 6th October 2014, a very severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Hudhud’ developed from a low pressure area which
lay over Tenasserim coast and adjoining north Andaman Sea. It concentrated into a depression in the
morning of 7
th October over North Andaman Sea. Moving west-north-westwards, it intensified into a
Cyclonic Storm (CS) in the morning of 8 th October, 2014 and crossed North Andaman Islands close
to Long Island between 0830 and 0930 hours on the same day. It then, emerged into Southeast Bay
of Bengal and continued to move west-north-westwards. It intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm
(SCS) in the morning of 9
th October, 2014 and further into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm (VSCS) in
the afternoon of 10 th October, 2014. It continued to intensify while moving north-westwards and
reached maximum intensity in the early morning of 12 th October, 2014 with a wind speed of 170 to
180 kmph gusting up to 195 kmph over the west central Bay of Bengal off Andhra Pradesh coast. It
crossed north Andhra Pradesh coast over Visakhapatnam between 1200 and 1300 hours IST with the
same wind speed. After landfall, it continued to move northwestwards for some time and weakened
gradually into SCS in the evening and further into a CS in the same midnight. It then, weakened further
into a Deep Depression in the early morning of 13
th October, 2014 and weakened into a depression in
the evening that day. Thereafter, the cyclone moved nearly northward and weakened into a low pressure
area over east Uttar Pradesh and neighborhood in the evening of 14
th October 2014.
1.1.2 The Ministry of Home Affairs further informed that due to the cyclone, there had not been
much damage except few tree falls, and no loss of life or injury has been reported from any part
of Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

touch with the concerned senior officers of the State Governments of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
for extending the required support and assistance. The MHA control room regularly advised the
concerned stakeholders to take preventive measures for minimising the impact of the cyclone.  An
amount of ` 115.425 crore, central share of State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) was released

17.10.2014 for the management of relief necessitated by notified natural disaster during 2014-15.

memorandum from the Government of Andhra Pradesh for central assistance in the wake of
Cyclone storm ‘Hudhud’ and floods during 2014, an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) was
constituted on 3
rd November 2014.  However, by that time, no memorandum was submitted by the
State Government of Odisha to the Central Government for additional central assistance in the
matter.
1.2.6 The Committee was informed that as a preparedness measure, the Army moved 8 composite
teams from Secunderabad to Visakhapatnam consisting of 285 personnel. 4 teams each were
deployed at Achutapuram and Srikakulam. 2 Medical teams of the Army each were deployed at
Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam. 2 Columns were kept on a standby at Gopalpur. 4 ships of Navy
were deployed at Visakhapatnam along with 6 helicopters, 2 Dorniers, 2 Medical teams and 30
diving teams. The Indian Air Force deployed 4 transport aircrafts and 14 helicopters at different
locations. The Coast Guard also kept 17 ships and 1 aircraft ready at different places.
1.2.7 The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) deployed 26 teams in Andhra Pradesh and
16 teams in Odisha along with boats and other necessary equipment. NDRF assisted the State
Governments to evacuate more than 13,000 persons to safe places. MHA distributed 17 satellite
phones to the State of Andhra Pradesh and 14 satellite phones to Odisha State prior to the hitting
of the cyclone for any emergency telecommunications.
