sought for the purpose of monitoring of the scheme from time to time.  This Ministry is closely co-
ordinating with Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers ’ Welfare not only in respect of scheme of organic 
farming but also in respect of other schemes for wh ich joint workshops have been organized in the 
North East. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION 
 
3.6.3  The Committee is unable to understand the role of t he Ministry of Development of the 
North Eastern Region after the transfer of funds fo r farmers’ welfare.  It appears that the 
Ministry of DoNER has been relegated to the role of an observer.  The Committee would like to be 
apprised whether the Ministry of DoNER is yet to be  divested of the responsibility as per the 
original mandate. The Committee desires to know the  role of the Ministry of DoNER in the 
discharge of its responsibility as the Ministry tha t will steer development in the North Eastern 
Region after the transfer of the schemes to the other Ministries concerned. 
 
3.7 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURECES FOR NER  
 
Recommendation 
 
3.7.1 The Committee has noticed a new trend that ha s started where three Central Ministries namely 
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Minist ry of Road Transport and Ministry of Rural 
Development are running their programmes independen t of Ministry of DoNER. The very purpose of 
creating the Ministry of DoNER was that it will be a nodal Ministry and it will co-ordinate with all t he 
remaining Ministries, except the exempted Ministrie s, for development of the region. This is bound to 
create duplication of work and it has been seen in the road sector. Further the trend also has to be 
arrested otherwise in a very short time many Centra l Ministries may opt for independent functioning in  
the NER, thus relegating the Ministry of DoNER to the background or make it irrelevant. The Committee 
feels that the Ministry of DoNER needs to be restru ctured for better coordination and understanding. 
The Committee is of the considered view that the ro le and duties of the Ministry of DoNER vis-à-vis 
other Ministries have to be defined in clear terms and hence recommend for adequate changes in the 
Allocation of Business Rules, Govt. of India. 
(Para 3.1.21 ibid) 
Action Taken 
3.7.2 The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways i s primarily responsible for the development and 
maintenance of National Highways in the country, in  accordance with the Allocation of Business Rules 
for the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. In  addition to the development of maintenance of 

29 
 
NHs under normal schemes of the Ministry, the Special Accelerated Road Development Programmes for 
North East (SARDP-NE) was initiated by the Ministry  for the development of NHs, State Roads and 
Strategic roads and roads of Interstate Connectivit y and Economic Importance. During the formulation 
stage of the programme detailed discussion were hel d with various ministries of the Govt. of India 
including Ministry of DoNER before approval was obt ained from the Cabinet Committee on Economic 
Affairs (CCEA). Further the status of implementatio n of the programme is being reviewed by Ministry 
of DoNER from time to time. A High Powered Inter-Mi nisterial Committee (HPC), in which Secretary, 
Ministry of DoNER is also a Member, was set up with  the approval of the CCEA for appraisal and 
approval of the various road projects under SARDP-N E. Ministry of Rural Development is 
implementing the scheme of rural connectivity in the entire country including the North Eastern region. 
 
3.7.3 Ministry of DoNER coordinates with the concer ned Ministries that would be responsible for 
implementation of the schemes in their respective s ectors. The coordination aspect is being further 
augmented by setting up sector specific inter-ministerial committees.   
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION 
 
3.7.4 The Committee reiterates its further recommen dation in respect of the action taken note 
with reference to para 2.12.4 and desires to know h ow the Ministry of DoNER proposes to 
discharge its primary responsibility as the Ministr y responsible for steering development in the 
North Eastern Region. 
 
3.8 STATUS OF MAJOR INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS IN NER 
 
Inland Waterways 
 
Recommendation 
 
3.8.1 The Committee is fully aware that the Inland waterways represent the green mode of transport 
and it is extremely important in the NER because of  its unique terrain. The Committee observes that in  
the new RO-RO terminal at Dhubri which is scheduled  to be completed by August 2016, only 65 percent 
of the physical progress has been achieved and it i s unlikely that the project will be completed in ti me. 
In the scenario, the Committee recommends that Mini stry of DoNER in close coordination with the 
Inland Waterways Authority of India should strive to complete the projects in time. 
(Para 3.2.15 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
3.8.2 Construction of IWT-cum-RoRo terminal at Dhub ri (Assam) had been awarded to CPWD in Jan 
2013 and work was scheduled to be completed in Augu st, 2016. However, due to unexpected rise in the 
water level of river Brahmaputra since April, 2016,  the bank protection work got delayed. The work is 
expected to be completed by Jan 2017. The suggestio ns have been noted and the matter is also reviewed 
by Ministry at various levels. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION 
3.8.3 The Committee takes note of the fact that the  construction work of the terminal has been 
delayed and could not be completed by the scheduled  date though the cause of this was beyond 
human control. The Committee hopes that ameliorativ e/corrective measures have been taken and 
recommends that at least now it should be completed by the scheduled date. 
 

30 
 
Power 
 
Recommendation 
 
3.8.4 The Committee takes note of the fact that whi le NER has a huge potential for Hydropower 
generation but the efforts of the implementation ag encies have not translated this in gains for the re gion 
and the nation. The Committee, therefore, recommend s that the Ministry must exhort the implementing 
PSUs and other concerned agencies to accelerate the  pace of hydropower generation in NER. The 
Committee further recommends that efforts must be i ntensified to remove stumbling blocks from 
implementation of Subansiri Lower project in Arunachal Pradesh at the earliest. 
(Para 3.2.17 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
3.8.5 North Eastern Region has enormous hydro-elect ric power potential of 62,604 MW (above 25 
MW) including 4,248 MW in Sikkim. Presently, 14 pow er stations (above 25 MW) of 2,007 MW are in 
operation while 15 projects (above 25 MW) of 5,480 MW are under construction. Further, a total of 134 
Projects (above 25 MW) of 56,458.5 MW were allotted  by State Governments. Out of the above, DPRs 
of 25 projects (above 25 MW) of 21,220 MW were conc urred by CEA which are yet to be taken up for 
construction and DPRs of 5 H.E. Schemes (above 25 MW) of 2,860 MW are under examination in CEA. 
 
3.8.6 The slow pace of development is, inter alia, on account of the following issues: 
• Land Acquisition Issues, Rehabilitation & Resettlement Issues 
• Environment and Forest issues & Cumulative Basin Studies 
• Inadequate Infrastructural facilities 
• Local issues & Inter-state Issues 
 
3.8.7 A large number of hydro-electric projects tha t are presently at various stages of clearances are  in 
the state of Arunachal Pradesh. This Ministry along  with Ministry of Power has jointly taken up these 
issues with the Chief Minister, Arunachal Pradesh and Chief Secretary, Arunachal Pradesh. 
 
3.8.8 The Ministry of Power (MoP) has taken a numbe r of measures for expediting clearance process 
and project implementation including: 
• Consultation Process evolved for expediting Survey & Investigation activities and 
preparation of Quality DPRs wherein appraising agen cies advise Developer in carrying 
out various investigations and firming up the project layout etc. 
• Time bound appraisal norms evolved for examination of DPRs. 
• A number of projects prioritized and being monitore d regularly at highest levels, for their 
expeditious implementation, by CEA and at senior levels in the Ministry. 
• Regular review meetings held with equipment manufac turers, State 
Utilities/CPSUs/Project developers, etc. to sort out the critical issues. 
•   A Power Project Monitoring Panel (PPMP) set up by  MoP to independently follow up and 
monitor the progress of the hydro projects. 
•   Review meetings held by MoP/CEA with BRO, MoRTH e tc. to sort out the infrastructure 
issues. 
 
3.8.9 Subansiri Lower (2000 MW) H.E. Project in Aru nachal Pradesh is stalled since 16.12.11 due to 
agitation launched by various activists against construction of the Project. All out efforts are being made 
to restart construction in the project. 
 

31 
 
3.8.10 Apart from several initiatives in the past, a Project Oversight Committee (POC) was constituted  
on 13.01.2015 to resolve the issue. Twelve meetings  of the POC were held but due to difference in 
opinion on some issues (mainly seismic issues), the  members of POC (Assam) and members of POC 
(GoI) submitted separate reports to MoP in Feb.’16.  Meanwhile, a case related to Subansiri Lower 
Project was filed in the Hon’ble National Green Tri bunal (NGT), Kolkata. As desired by Hon’ble NGT, 
both the reports submitted by POC were submitted to Hon’ble NGT.  
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION  
 
3.8.11 The Committee is of the considered view that  huge hydro-electric power potential of NER 
must be harnessed/utilised to the optimal level for  not only creating new economic developmental 
opportunities in the NER but to meet the electric p ower requirement of the nation as well.  The 
onus lies on the Central Ministries concerned and the State Governments to sort out issues such as 
land acquisition and environmental clearances, law & order or inter-state conflicts at the earliest 
for speedy implementation of the projects on time a nd within the estimated cost and also paving 
the way for projects which are at conception/Detail ed Project Report (DPR) stage.  Moreover, all 
policy initiatives taken in the direction of accele rating hydro-power development must be 
translated into specific course of action with due impetus to their execution without failure so that 
objectives of policy-decisions are achieved within set time-frame.  The Committee also desires that 
all institutional arrangements must be in put place  to enable the completion of projects without 
any hurdles.  The Committee hopes that Subansiri Lo wer project in Arunachal Pradesh would be 
rescued from the legal hurdles/procedural delays an d that all stake-holders will agree for speedy 
implementation and execution of this important project.   

32 
 
CHAPTER - IV 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION IN RESPECT OF WHICH FINAL REPLY OF THE 
GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN RECEIVED 
 
4.1 NORTH EASTERN REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MARKETING C ORPORATION 
(NERAMAC) 
 
Recommendation 
 
4.1.1 The Committee while examining the detailed De mands for Grants 2016 -17 notes that there are 
no budgetary allocations either under Plan or Non-P lan head for NERAMAC. Even trading turnover 
data or earnings from the processing done by the NE RAMAC do not indicate surpluses or profits for the 
NERAMAC. The Committee in its 186 
th  Report on the Demands for Grants of 2015-16 for th e M/o 
DONER had recommended for early establishment of pr oposed e-auction centers throughout the region 
in the North east along with a centralized e-auctio n system with a view to ensure better and timely 
returns for the producers. The Committee had furthe r recommended that NERAMAC should put its acts 
together to revive defunct food processing units in  the region with better equipments, technical know-
how and affordable finance. However, the Committee is disappointed to note that no action has been 
taken on the ground zero and it feels with sadness that it will be an opportunity lost, if an early ac tion is 
not taken. The Committee recommends to the Ministry  to take an appropriate action and provide 
adequate support to NERAMAC in order to achieve the objectives. 
(Para 2.5.3 of 196 th  Report) 
Action Taken 
 
4.1.2 The Ministry has been making all out efforts to enable NERAMAC to perform its prescribed 
mandate.  In the FY 2015-16, an amount of Rs.2 cror e has been released to NERAMAC.  NERAMAC 
has utilised this fund to bolster its business acti vities in terms of procurement of large cardamom, b lack 
pepper, hill grass and some organic vegetables from  farmers of various States at remunerative prices.  
Similarly, in the financial year 2016-17 also, the Ministry has already proposed for release of Rs.2 crore.  
This would enable NERAMAC for taking up more business activities.   
 
4.1.3 The NERAMAC activities have picked up and hav e participated in national and international 
events relating to agri-horti sector.  Recently, it  participated in the international event of Food Ex po, 
SIAL at Paris and the B2B meeting at Mandalay and Y angon during India-Myanmar-Thailand (IMT) 
rally. Survey of markets and mandis was also undert aken to ascertain the export potential from North 
East Region. 
 
4.1.4 It is to be noted that NERAMAC has been posti ng losses for the last three financial years and 
has, therefore, been declared a sick company.  But keeping the larger interests of the farming community 
in the North East Region, it has been decided to re vive it.  For this purpose, the Ministry requested 
NEDFi to undertake a Techno-Economic Viability study of NERAMAC. The NEDFi has since prepared 
a detailed Time Line based Revival Plan for NERAMAC . Issues relating to revival of defunct food 
processing units of NERAMAC and new business model for NERAMAC are being finalised as part of 
revival plan.   
 
4.1.5 On the establishment of e-auction centers wit h a centralized e-auction system, infrastructure of  
the centre at Guwahati has been completed and train ing for operating the software has also been given.  

33 
 
NERAMAC with C-DAC is now moving further to organiz e awareness workshops about the online e-
auction center and registration of dealers & farmers in Sikkim and in other NE states.  
 
FURTHER OBSERVATION 
 
4.1.6 The Committee notes that NERAMAC has been mak ing losses for the last three years and 
hence, declared a sick company, therefore, an early  decision should be taken on the revival 
package of NERAMAC and the Committee may be apprised of the decision taken in this regard.  
 
4.2 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOLOF RESOURECES FOR NER (NLCPR) 
 
Performance Evaluation Study of NLCPR Schemes in XI Plan 
 
Recommendation 
 
4.2.1 The Committee is concerned about the manageme nt of NLCPR fund which by the very 
nature do not lapse, if unused/unspent, but go back  to the Ministry of Finance. As per the Ministry’s 
information an amount of over Rs.15,600 crore is ac cumulated in the ‘Central Pool’ as it could not be 
utilised. The Committee gets a feeling that though it is non-lapsable, the money is not available to t he 
Ministry of DONER or in effect for all practical purposes it is not available to North Eastern States. The 
Committee is of the view that if the unspent money is not available to the MoDONER, the entire purpose 
of creating the Non-lapsable Central Pool of Resour ces by the Parliament will be defeated and hence 
recommend to the Ministry of DONER as well as the M inistry of Finance to work out a mechanism to 
keep the fund at the disposal of the Ministry of DO NER so as to enable it to spend the money as per th e 
need. This will help to create robust transport net work viz. National Highways, Rail network and 
aviation so that the communication becomes faster b etween the mainland and the north east as well as 
inter-state communication. 
 
4.2.2. The Committee questioned the method of budge t allocation under NLCPR. As per the 
information given, the MoDONER has demanded Rs.1500  crore from the NLCPR for 2016-17, but only 
Rs.700 crore is allotted. The reason for slash is t hat MoDONER could spend less than Rs.600 crore 
(Rs.511.88 crore spent till 14.03.2016) in the last  financial year therefore the grant has to be reduc ed. 
Since the fund is non-lapsable, there seems to be no justification in reduction in projected demands. This 
gives rise to the feeling that the ministry of Finance is more interested in accumulating fund in pool than 
spending it for the betterment of the North east, p articularly when the NER is way behind in 
infrastructural development especially in road, rai l and aviation sectors. Therefore, the Committee 
strongly recommends that the Ministry, instead of s aying that ‘the impact of reduction and increase in  
allocation would be assessed during the Financial Y ear 2016-17 and a view would be taken on the need 
to seek higher outlay during the course of the year  through supplementary’, should pursue the Ministry  
of Finance to release funds from the Non- lapsable Central Pool and enhance the grants to at least the  
level of projected demands by the NEC and also their own projected demands. 
  (Para 3.1.18 & 3.1.19 ibid)  
Action Taken  
 
4.2.3 The 56 non-exempted Ministries/Departments ar e required to spend 10% of their plan outlay in 
the North East.  This is reflected in Statement 23 of the Union Budget.  In BE 2016-17 the total 
earmarked outlay of these Ministries amounts to Rs.  33097.02 crores which is 14% higher than the 
previous year.   The overall expenditure of various  Ministries excluding Railways has increased from 
Rs.23170.63 crores (provisional) in 2013-14 to Rs.31291.18 crores (provisional) in 2015-16.    
 

34 
 
4.2.4 The unutilised portion of the funds earmarked  for NER by the non - exempted ministries / 
departments is accrued to Non-lapsable central pool  of resources (NLCPR) being maintained on pro-
forma basis by the Ministry of Finance.  Release ou t of NLCPR pool is made through annual budget of 
Ministry of DoNER for NLCPR state and central schem es.  This Ministry has been pursuing the matter 
with Ministry of Finance for greater allocation bot h under NLCPR and to the NEC.  In addition to the  
requests that were made to enhance the budget at th e BE stage in 2016-17, the Ministry of DoNER has 
also forwarded to Ministry of Finance  a list of 23 6 projects, costing Rs.4729.51 crores, retained und er 
NLCPR and NEC with a request to allocate adequate funds for sanctioning of these projects.  
 
FURTHER OBSERVATION 
 
4.2.5 The Committee strongly recommends that Depart ment of Economic Affairs should not sit 
over the proposal of the Ministry of DoNER on 236 p rojects costing Rs.4729.51 crore retained 
under NLCPR and NEC and take appropriate action without any further delay.  
 
  

35 
 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE- AT A GLANCE 
 
TOTAL REVENUE AND CAPITAL OUTLAY 
 
 Even if allocation to the Ministry of DoNER under Social and Infrastructure Development 
Fund (SIDF) is made by Department of Expenditure, M inistry of Finance and maintained in 
Public Account, and therefore, cannot be re-appropr iated to other schemes, what causes concern 
to the Committee is the fact that against the allocation of Rs.170 crore in 2015-16, the total amount 
released was only to the tune of Rs.49.88 crore.  A gain in the current financial year, the allocation 
in BE was slashed to Rs.100 crore.  This reflects l ow absorption capacity of projects under Social 
and Infrastructural Development Fund meant for NER.  The Committee, therefore, strongly 
recommends that the Ministry of DoNER must pro-acti vely guide the State Governments to 
enhance their absorption capacity for effective imp lementation of projects/schemes under SIDF.  
The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of DoNER, in tandem with State 
Governments, should expedite the process of identif ication of additional infrastructure projects 
for optimum utilisation of allocated funds under SI DF.  Moreover, Ministry of DoNER must 
adhere to strict monitoring /supervision through ti mely procurement of Utilisation Certificate 
(UC) and Quarterly Progress Report (QPR).  
(Para 3.1.6) 
 
INSTITUTIONS UNDER THE MINISTRY OF DoNER: NORTH EASTERN COUNCIL  
 
 The Committee is of the considered view that the c ommitted liability of the NEC to the tune 
of Rs. 2220 crore as on 29 
th  February, 2016 is a huge stumbling block for funct ional efficiency and 
proficiency of NEC. Therefore, the urgent need is t o make concerted efforts to enhance the 
'absorption capacity' of ongoing projects/schemes a nd ensure their timely implementation within 
allocated funds, so that the Ministry of Finance should not point to lower capability of the sectoral 
organisations to absorb the allocated funds as a re ason for not increasing the allocation to NEC 
for starting new projects in the current/next finan cial years.  The Committee, therefore, desires 
that the Ministry of Finance may consider allocatin g funds to NEC as a one-time measure for 
liquidating the committed liability of NEC so that NEC gets an opportunity to start on a clean 
slate.  At the same time, NEC and Ministry of DoNER  must chalk out a plan for enhancing 
absorption capacity of sectoral organisations to im plement the undertaken projects without time 
and cost overruns and establish a pattern of expenditure in accordance with budgeting prudence. 
(Para 3.2.3) 
 
NORTH EAST HANDICRAFTS AND HANDLOOMS DEVELOPMENT 
CORPORATION LTD. (NEHHDC) 
 
 The Committee is constrained to note that the comp letion schedule of the revival plan has 
been extended to 31 
st  March, 2018.  The Committee recommends that NEHHDC  management, 
State Government and Ministry of DoNER must monitor  the progress of the revival project and 
its timely execution in order to ensure revival as per schedule. 
(Para 3.3.5) 
 
AGRI-HORTI POTENTIAL IN NER

ORGANIC FARMING IN NE STATES

 The Committee reiterates its further recommendatio n in respect of the action taken note

CHAPTER-I  
 
OVERVIEW 
1.1 INTRODUCTION 
1.1.1 The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has respon sibilities of internal security, border 
management, Centre-State relations, administration of Union Territories, management of Central 
Armed Police Forces, disaster management, etc.  
 
1.1.2 As per  Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules,  1961 (As Amended up to 15th 
February, 2017) the Ministry of Home Affairs admini sters and implements a number of schemes/ 
programmes and discharges its responsibilities thro ugh its departments which have been detailed 
below with  their respective mandates:- 
 
1.1.3  The Department of Official Language, though has a s eparate Secretary and functions 
independently, comes under the purview of the Home Ministry. It has the nodal responsibility for all 
matters relating to the progressive use of Hindi as  the Official language of the Union, including 
Hindi teaching schemes for Central government employees. It also holds the mandate for Publication 
and distribution of publicity literature for progre ssive use of Hindi as the official language of the 
Union.  
 
           
1.2 Administration Division 
 
1.2.1 The Administration Division is responsible fo r handling all administrative and vigilance 
matters, allocation of work among various Divisions  of the Ministry and matters relating to the 
Warrant of Precedence, Padma Awards, Gallantry Awar ds, Jeevan Raksha Padak, National Flag, 
National Anthem, State Emblem of India and the Secr etariat Security Organisation.  Administration 
is also the Nodal Division for matters relating to Right to Information Act, 2005.   
 
1.3 Border Management Division 
 
1.3.1 This Division deals with matters relating to coordination of the Department of Border 
Management, including matters related to Empowered Committee on Border Infrastructure (ECBI), 
matters pertaining to Border Area Development Programme (BADP), Integrated Check Posts (ICPs), 
Land Ports Authority of India (LPAI), management of  India-Bangladesh Border, India-Pakistan 
Border, India-Nepal Border, India-China Border, Ind ia-Bhutan Border and India-Myanmar Border 
and issues relating to Coastal Security and strengt hening of border policing, guarding, creation of 
infra-structure like roads, fencing and flood light ing of borders, in coordination with the Ministry o f 
Defence and the Ministry of External Affairs. 

2 
 
1.4 Coordination Division 
 
1.4.1 This Division deals with intra-Ministry coord ination work, Parliamentary matters, public 
grievances (PGs), publication of Annual Report of t he Ministry, record retention schedule, custody 
of classified and non-classified records of the Min istry, Internal Work Study and furnishing of 
various reports  relating to employment of  SCs/STs  and Persons with Disabilities to the Department 
of Personnel and Training, etc.  
 
 
1.5 Centre-State Division 
 
1.5.1 This Division deals with Centre–State relatio ns, including working of the Constitutional 
provisions governing such relations, appointment of  Governors, creation of new States, 
administration of the Acts relating to the reorgnis ation of States, nominations to the Rajya 
Sabha/Lok Sabha, Inter-State boundary disputes, ove r-seeing the crime situation in States and 
imposition of President’s Rule. It also has the man date pertaining to the special provisions in Articl e 
371 to Article 371J of the Constitution with respect to certain States.
 
 
1.6 Disaster Management Division 
 
1.6.1 This Division is responsible for legislation,  policy, capacity building, prevention, mitigation,  
long term rehabilitation, response, relief and prep aredness for natural calamities and man-made 
disasters (except drought and epidemics). 
 
1.7 Finance Division 
 
1.7.1 This Division is responsible for formulating,  operating and controlling the budget of the 
Ministry and other matters pertaining to expenditure control, monitoring and financial advice. 
 
1.8 Foreigners Division 
1.8.1  This Division deals with all matters relating to visa, Protected Area Permit (PAP) / Restricted 
Area Permit (RAP) regimes, immigration, citizenship , overseas citizenship of India and acceptance 
of foreign contribution and hospitality. 
 
1.9 Freedom Fighters and Rehabilitation Division 
 
1.9.1 This Division frames and implements the Freed om Fighters’ Pension Scheme and the 
schemes for rehabilitation of migrants from former West Pakistan/East Pakistan and provision of 
relief to Sri Lankan and Tibetan refugees. 
 
 

3 
 
1.10 Internal Security – I Division 
 
1.10.1  Internal Security-I Division deals with matters rel ating to internal security and law & 
order, including anti-national and subversive activ ities of various groups/extremist organisations, 
terrorist financing, policy and operational issues on terrorism, security clearances, monitoring of IS I 
activities and Home Secretary-level talks with Pakistan on counter terrorism.  
 
1.11 Internal Security – II Division 
 
1.11.1  Internal Security-II Division deals with ma tters relating to arms and explosives, 
extradition, narcotics, Narcotics Control Bureau, t he National Security Act and security of VIPs/ 
vital installations.  
 
1.12 Internal Security – III Division 
 
1.12.1  This Division deals with matters relating t o the Protection of Human Rights Act as 
also matters relating to national integration, communal harmony and Ayodhya. 
 
1.13 International Co-operation Division 
 
1.13.1  This Division deals with meetings of the SA ARC interior/Home Ministers, matters 
relating to policy formulation on issues of interna l security, international cooperation on counter-
terrorism, international covenants, bilateral assistance treaties and related items. 
 
1.14 Jammu & Kashmir Division 
 
1.14.1  This Division deals with constitutional matters inc luding Article 370 of the 
Constitution of India and general policy matters in  respect of the State of Jammu & Kashmir and 
terrorism / militancy in that State.  It is also re sponsible for implementation of the Prime Minister’ s 
Package for Jammu and Kashmir. 
 
1.15 Judicial Division 
 
1.15.1  This Division deals with all matters relating to th e legislative aspects of the Indian 
Penal Code (IPC), Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.) and the Commission of Inquiry Act.  It also 
handles matters relating to the State legislations which require the assent of the President of India 
under the Constitution, political pension to erstwh ile rulers before independence and mercy petitions 
under Article 72 of the Constitution of India. 
 
 
 

4 
 
1.16 Left Wing Extremism (LWE) Division 
 
1.16.1  This Division was created on October 19, 20 06 in the Ministry to effectively tackle 
the LWE menace from both security and development a ngles.  It monitors the LWE situation and 
counter-measures being taken by the affected States  with the objective of improving ground-level 
policing and development response as per the locati on specific action plans formulated/to be 
formulated by the affected States. It also reviews proper implementation of various developmental 
schemes of Ministries / Departments concerned in th e LWE affected areas as also optimum 
utilisation of funds released under such schemes. 
 
1.17 North East Division 
 
1.17.1  This Division deals with the internal secur ity and law & order situation in the North-
Eastern States, including matters relating to insurgency and talks with various extremist groups 
operating in that region. 
 
1.18 Police – I Division  
 
1.18.1  Police-I Division functions as the cadre co ntrolling authority in respect of Indian 
Police Service (IPS) and also deals with all matter s relating to training of police personnel, award o f 
President’s Police Medals for Meritorious / Distinguished service and Gallantry. 
 
1.19 Police – II Division  
 
1.19.1  Police-II Division deals with all matters relating to Central Armed Police Forces 
(CAPFs), including their deployment.  
 
1.20 Police Modernisation Division 
 
1.20.1  This Division handles work relating to modernisatio n of State Police Forces, 
provisioning of various items for modernisation of Central Armed Police Forces, police reforms.  
 
1.21 Union Territories Division 
 
1.21.1  This Division deals with legislative and constituti onal matters relating to Union 
Territories, including National Capital Territory o f Delhi.  It also functions as the cadre controllin g 
authority of the Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram and Union Territory (AGMUT) cadre of Indian 
Administrative Service (IAS) / Indian Police Servic e (IPS) as also Delhi-Andaman and Nicobar 
Island Civil Service (DANICS)/ Delhi-Andaman and Ni cobar Island Police Service (DANIPS).  It is 
also responsible for overseeing the crime and law & order situation in the Union Territories.

CHAPTER-II  
OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF DEMANDS FOR GRANTS  
2.1 Overview 
2.1.1 There are ten Demands for Grants which are ad ministered by the Ministry of Home Affairs 
(MHA). The Detailed Demands for Grants of the Minis try of Home Affairs are divided into two 
volumes. The Detailed Demands for Grants (Volume-I)  contains three Grants (Nos. 46-48), namely: 
Ministry of Home Affairs (Grant No. 46); Cabinet (G rant No. 47); and Police (Grant No. 48). 
Volume-II contains seven Grants (49 to 55) meant for the seven Union Territories.  
 
2.1.2 The total allocation for all the ten Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Home Affairs in 
Budget Estimates 2017-18 is Rs. 99279.58 Crore. In BE 2016-17, it was Rs. 89996.83 crore which 
was increased by 4.67% to Rs. 94204.68 crore at RE stage. Thus, allocation in BE 2017-18 shows an 
increase of 10.31% over BE 2016-17 and 5.38% over R E 2016-17. Out of Rs. 99279.58 crore 
allocated in BE 2017-18, Rs. 85852.90 crore is unde r Revenue head whereas Rs. 13426.68 crore is 
earmarked under Capital head. 
 
2.1.3 The Committee was informed that the Twelfth F ive Year Plan period has ended during 2016-
17. From the year 2017-18 onwards, distinction betw een Plan and Non-Plan outlays has been done 
away with. Henceforth, the budgetary allocations will only be categorized as Revenue and Capital.

2.2.4 The Ministry of Home Affairs was also asked t o provide division-wise and scheme-wise 
demands projected by it before the Ministry of Fina nce. The Ministry submitted statement of 
projections of funds along with allocations which is placed at Annexure - I 
2.2.5 The Ministry submitted that some of the schem es like infrastructure of CAPFs, capacity 
building for Disaster Management, countering terrorism in Jammu & Kashmir, North Eastern Areas, 
Left Wing Extremism affected states, Border Infrast ructure viz. Roads, Border Out Posts, Fencing, 
Integrated Check Posts may not be able to function at their full potential due to reduced allocation.  

8 
 
2.2.6 The Committee has noted a nominal increase of  5.24% in allocation under the Demand 
No. 46 (MHA) and 6.43% in allocation under Demand N o. 48 (Police) as compared to the 
allocation made in RE 2016-17.  The Committee feels  that this nominal increase may not be 
even sufficient to offset the impact of higher wage s due to the 7 th  Central Pay Commission's 
recommendations and higher costs due to normal infl ationary pressures. Moreover, the 
allocation under Demand No. 48 (Police) is 23% lowe r than the amount projected by the 
Ministry.  The Committee feels that this shortfall of nearly Rs. 23,526 crore may severely 
hamper the operations of the security forces and im pede the operations of police and border 
infrastructure in the country.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs, 
in view of the imminent necessity of strengthening the border and internal security of the 
country, should pursue the Ministry of Finance for higher allocations at RE stage.     
2.2.7 The Committee also observes that overall allo cation to UTs is much lower in 
comparison to what they have projected.  The Commit tee feels that this may hamper the 
growth and development of the UTs.   The Committee recommends that the Ministry should 
approach the Ministry of Finance for higher allocat ion to these UTs at RE stage. Detailed 
analysis of the respective Grants has been given in Chapter-V of the Report.

2.3.2 Since the Government has discarded the distin ction between Plan and Non-Plan budgetary 
allocation from 2017-18, the Committee wanted to kn ow as to how and in what manner this would 
change the utilization pattern of allocated funds a nd also sought details of the utilization pattern o f 
allocated funds in successive years of the Twelfth Five Year Plan by the Ministry of Home Affairs. 
The Ministry submitted the Division-wise Statement showing the BE/RE/Actual Expenditure in 
respect of various Plan schemes of MHA during the p eriod 2012-13 to 2016-17 (as on 30.12.2016) 
placed at Annexure-II .  
2.3.3 The Committee takes a very serious view of un der utilization of funds in respect of the 
Plan Schemes of Ministry of Home Affairs throughout  the 12 th  Five Year Plan. Almost every 
year, several important Divisions of MHA including Border Management, Disaster 
Management, Police-I, Police-II and Internal Securi ty-I Divisions have surrendered huge 
amounts of funds at RE stage. In some cases the sur rendered funds were to the tune of 50% 
and above which is a clear indication of incoherent  planning, lack of conviction and inefficient 

10 
 
functioning of the Divisions concerned. In most of the Schemes/Heads wherein funds were 
surrendered, the reasons given by the Ministry were  mostly related to non-finalisation of 
proposals, slow progress of construction works and procedural delays. The Committee 
expresses its displeasure in the strongest terms on  this issue and observes that surrendering of 
funds at RE stage may be seen as a clear measure of  inefficiency of and unrealistic budgeting 
by the Divisions concerned as this has direct ramif ications on the country’s security and law 
and order situation.  
 
2.3.4 The Committee also notes that some Divisions were unable to completely utilise the 
funds even after the substantial cuts at RE stages imposed by the Ministry of Finance. The 
Committee feels that this is quite inexcusable as f ailure to absorb the funds even after 
surrendering nearly 40-60% of the budgetary allocat ions at RE stage is an indicator of 
underperformance. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs 
must explore innovative solutions, prepare flexible  and workable action plans, consistently 
meet all deadlines, and develop strategic alternati ves wherever the current strategy may not

avail of the benefit of the package in terms of cre ation and upgradation of infrastructure such as

tubewell, primary school, high school, health sub c entre, Angan Wari Centre, household electricity

Ministry apprised the Committee as follows: 

17

underway. Further, authorization has been issued to  the executing agency (JKPCC) for

sites was in progress. The State Govt. identified a bout 90 Acres (723 Kanals) of land in 7 
districts of Kashmir valley for construction of 344 0 transit accommodations. The State 
Govt. will issue notification for land acquisition soon and begin construction work. 
(iii) In 2015, Government of India sanctioned Rs. 40 cror e for providing grant-in-aid to 
Central Tibetan Relief Committee (CTRC), a register ed Society headed by His Holiness, 
Dalai Lama to meet administrative and social welfar e expenses over a period of 5 years 
from 2015-16 to 2019-20. 
(iv) About 1622 Bru families (8573 Nos.) have been repat riated and resettled in Mizoram so 
far. To review the repatriation process, a Joint Mo nitoring Group (JMG) under the 
chairmanship of JS (NE), MHA was constituted on 10. 8.2016 with members from State 
Governments of Tripura and Mizoram, Bru representat ives from Tripura and Civil

10.10.2016, 24.11.2016 and 12.2.2017 to discuss and  decide issues related to repatriation

occupied Kashmir and Chhamb Niabat Areas under Prim e Minister Development Package for 
Jammu and Kashmir.  However, no expenditure was inc urred upto December, 2016 on this 
account.  The Committee, therefore, strongly recomm ends that the Ministry should earnestly 
implement this package by making prudent and timely  utilization of allocated funds.  The 
Committee also desires to be apprised about the sta tus of the implementation of this 
rehabilitation package.  
3.4.8 The Committee is displeased with the fact tha t against an allocation of Rs. 340 crore in 
BE 2016-17  for  Rehabilitation Package and up-gradation of infrastr ucture of the Bangladeshi 
Enclaves and Cooch Behar District, Rs. 200 crore were surrendered at RE stage and even after 
that no expenditure was incurred by the Ministry up to December, 2016. The Committee is 
particularly anguished at the reports of these pers ons living in abject poverty and left to fend 

18 
 
for themselves even for most basic necessities. The  Committee would like to strongly 
emphasize the importance of expeditiously implement ing this rehabilitation package for the 
persons who have expressed their faith in India and  opted for Indian citizenship with a hope 
that Government of India will provide them essentia l facilities and decent means of livelihood 
and infrastructure.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs 
should not let the returnees from Bangladeshi encla ves suffer anymore and should implement 
the rehabilitation package with utmost sincerity an d urgency and, until the package is fully 
implemented, adequate relief may be sanctioned and provided to them on a continuous basis.  
The Committee also recommends that the senior offic ers of the Division concerned may visit 
the enclave dwellers periodically and review the st atus of implementation of the package on a 
regular basis. The Committee may also be kept appri sed of this on a quarterly basis till the 
implementation is completed.

amount of cash relief to be paid on a monthly basis  to all the families who opted for Indian 
citizenship subsequent to the exchange of enclaves between India and Bangladesh. An urgent 
decision may be taken to provide this assistance im mediately and arrangements may be made 
for directly transferring this assistance into the Aadhaar-linked bank accounts of the 
beneficiaries under the Direct Benefit Transfer Scheme.

provides that Grant in aid to State Governments may  be sanctioned to meet the expenditure incurred

under the rules, the bills for the year 2013-14 are  to be reimbursed first before processing the bills  
for the financial years 2014-15 and 2015-16. In vie w of this the funds requirement was reviewed by 
MHA according to the pendency of previous years. 
3.10.2  The Committee sought to know the rates of d uty allowance and quantum of cash 
award given by various States to Home Guards.  The Ministry replied that Home Guard is a State 
Subject and duty allowance is paid to the Home Guar ds by the respective State Governments and it 
varies from State to State and daily allowance paid by the States is in the range of Rs. 60 to Rs. 425.  
3.10.3  The Committee is constrained to note the po or state of the Home Guards 
throughout the country.  The Committee is deeply an guished to note that some of the States 
are paying duty allowance as low as Rs. 60 per day to the Home Guards.  This is despite the 
Supreme Court’s order on  increasing the duty allow ance of Home Guards to minimum of the 
pay to which the police personnel are entitled.  Th e Committee is not satisfied with the reply of 
the Ministry that it does not have details of imple mentation of the Supreme Court’s order by 
the States.  The neglect of this issue by the Ministry is reflective of corresponding neglect of the 
Home Guards by the States.  The Committee, therefor e, recommends that the Centre should 
compile and maintain State-wise data of duty allowa nce being paid to the Home Guards and 
strive towards bringing uniformity in the rates of duty allowance paid by the States.  The 
Committee also recommends that the Ministry should direct the States to implement the 
Supreme Court’s order in letter and spirit.

of fencing in India-Bangladesh Border which was a f lat land unlike the tough terrains of India-
Pakistan Border. The representative of the Ministry  replied that the issues of land acquisition and 
public protests were the main reasons for this slow progress.   
4.6.19     The Committee is concerned at the state of affairs of construction/upgradation of 
infrastructure along India-Nepal Border (INB).  In Bihar part of INB, only 19.1 km of roads 
were constructed throughout the year, while only 21 .3 km of roads were completed in Uttar 
Pradesh.  The Ministry took the plea of pending lan d acquisition as the reason for this 

39 
 
extremely slow pace of construction.  The Committee  feels that if pace of road construction 
does not improve then it would take a decade more to complete the construction of roads along 
INB.  The proposal was approved long back in 2010.  The Committee is surprised to note that 
even such important border infrastructure projects are delayed due to the problem of land 
acquisition and yet the Ministry failed to find a s olution to this persistent problem that plagues 
almost all the border infrastructure projects throu ghout the country.  The Committee feels 
that the Ministry needs to find a permanent solutio n to the problem of land acquisition in 
border areas in the national interest. The Ministry  may hold meetings with all the 
Governments of Border States where land acquisition  has delayed implementation of projects 
and make all out efforts to find a permanent solution to this problem. 
4.6.20  The Committee is anguished to note that out  of the plan allocation of Rs. 1418.97 
crore for border fencing and roads construction alo ng India-Bangladesh border, during 12 th  
Five Year Plan, only Rs. 887.79 crore (62.56%) of t he plan allocation could be spent. The 
Committee was also dismayed to observe the extremel y tardy progress of border 
infrastructure projects with completion of only aro und 15 km of fencing, 26 km of roads, 46 
km of flood lights and just 11 border outposts duri ng 2016.  The Committee is aware of the 
issues that affect construction projects along India – Bangladesh border; however, the inability 
of the Ministry to resolve these issues for so long  seems unjustifiable. Even the Supreme Court 
expressed its strong displeasure at the manner in w hich border fencing projects languish along 
IBB and lack of any specific plan of the Ministry t o complete it.  The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should chalk out a strict and specific plan, while adhering to the 
timeline stipulated by the Supreme Court, for compl etion of all the infrastructure projects 
along IBB and devote its sincere efforts to plug al l the gaps on the border that were still being 
exploited for illegal cross border influx and smuggling.

Delhi Police. The Committee wonders how the task of  developing an efficient traffic

management and communication network in Delhi inclu ding modernisation and technology.

4.9.8 The Committee is disappointed to observe the poor achievement of financial targets by 
the Delhi Police. Under all the Schemes, including Scheme for Safety of Women, substantial 
part of funds allocated in BE 2016-17 were surrende red at RE stage presumably due to poor 
expenditure in the first half of 2016-17. Even then , the utilization of funds remained poor and 
a mere 42% of RE allocation was utilised by the end  of December, 2016. Delhi Police needs to 
realize the importance of these Schemes which are e ssential for developing Delhi as a safe and 
convenient place to live. The Committee feels that Delhi Police’s failure to utilize even such low 
amounts of funds points to a serious lack of capaci ty for fund utilization. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the division concerned i n MHA should periodically review the 
financial performance of Delhi Police based on whic h the Ministry should make efforts 
towards improving the fund utilization capacity of Delhi Police.

5.3.1 The Committee, while discussing the functioni ng of the Delhi Police, raised several queries 
on different software applications used by them for  fighting crime and to improve the law and order 
situation in the National Capital. The representati ve of Delhi Police during the evidence explained 
that with the help of “e-beat book” application whi ch is about to be launched Beat Officer of a 
particular area will be in touch with residents in a digital mode, sharing information with them and 
providing any further services  which he/she can ot herwise render by visiting them physically. The 
Senior Citizens’ App that has been launched since l ast October would be extended to other citizens. 
The Committee during its evidence held on 28 th  February 2017 also expressed its anguish over the 
deplorable situation regarding the safety of women in Delhi. 
5.3.2 The Committee expresses apprehension that suc h software should not actually reduce 
the physical movement and active patrolling of the police on ground level and recommends 
that proper assessment with regard to its impact ma y be done before launching. The 
Committee also strongly recommends that Delhi Polic e has to be more responsive towards 
women’s safety in the NCT of Delhi.   
 
Traffic Congestion in Delhi 
5.3.3 The Committee, in its meeting held on Demands  for Grants of the Ministry of Home Affairs, 
deliberated on the problem of traffic congestion in  Delhi which has reached unsustainable 
proportions. Members of the Committee raised many c ritical questions with regard to the limited 
carrying capacity of the roads, choking of roads du e to ever increasing traffic, insufficient parking,  
need for construction of more arterial roads to eas e the traffic congestion and emergency evacuation 
plan of the protected persons.  
5.3.4 The representatives of Delhi Police while agr eeing that traffic management was indeed a 
worrisome issue in Delhi stated that the issue had been taken up with the concerned authorities. 
 5.3.5   The Committee feels that the Delhi traffic congestion has become quite alarming and 
the Delhi Police has failed to implement any signif icant measures to improve the situation. The 
Committee takes note of the choked roads in Delhi w hich makes evacuation of Protected 
Persons very difficult during traffic congestion.  The Committee also observes that a huge 
number of vehicles are getting registered every day in the Capital and presence of roundabouts 
on various cross-roads instead of traffic signals w hich cause congestion.   The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Delhi Police needs to prepare a meticulous traffic management 
plan for Delhi and allocate adequate funds for addressing the issue of traffic management. The 
Committee also recommends that urgent measures shou ld be taken for managing the city 
traffic in a better way with construction of more a rterial roads and parking bays, declaring 
some roads as one-way, devising effective emergency  evacuation measures for the protected 
persons and stringent measures against traffic violators.

6.6.2 The Committee notes the submission of Delhi P olice regarding the status and number of 
users of Himmat App and feels that this App has fai led to serve the purpose for which it was 
introduced with a lot of fanfare. The Committee fin ds that complex registration process and 
non-availability of App in Hindi have restricted th e number of users of this App. The fact that 
the App had only 30821 registered users in a city w ith a population of almost 19 million 
reflects upon the comprehensive failure of this App  to function as an SOS helpline for the 
women. The Committee also feels that without adequate publicity among the target group, this 
App will not be able to see any increase in number of users. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that Delhi Police should redesign this App by simplifying it and either remove the 
registration process or simplify it as much as poss ible by seeking only the minimum details 
required. The Committee also recommends that Himmat App must be made available in Hindi 
as well to enable a large number of women to use this App.  
6.6.3 The Committee also feels that due publicity w as not given to this App and better 
publicity in more unconventional ways and through s ocial media platforms can help increase 
the number of users.  The Committee, therefore, rec ommends that Delhi Police must hire the 
services of a private digital marketing agency to publicize this App among the target users, and 
give a specific target to the agency of achieving at least a million downloads by the end of 2017.  
 
6.7 Long Term Visa (LTV) to Minority Communities fr om Pakistan, Bangladesh and 
Afghanistan 
6.7.1 The Ministry in its list of achievements duri ng 2016-17 submitted to the Committee stated 
that Government had issued instructions on 19.8.201 6 for granting various facilities to persons 
belonging to minority communities in Afghanistan, B angladesh and Pakistan who were staying in 
India on Long Term Visa (LTV) or who have applied f or LTV. These facilities include permission 
for opening of bank accounts, permission for purcha se of dwelling unit for self occupation and 
suitable accommodation for carrying out self-employ ment, issue of PAN card, Aadhaar number and 
driving license, permission to take up self-employm ent or business, allowing free movement within 
the State/UT, permission to transfer LTV papers fro m one State/UT to another, reduction in penalty 
on non-extension of short term visa/LTV on time and  permission to apply for LTV at the present 
place of residence. 
6.7.2 The Ministry also informed, during its presen tation before the Committee, that the 
Citizenship (Amendment) Bill, 2016 was introduced i n Lok Sabha on 19.07.2016 to facilitate grant 
of Citizenship to minority communities from Pakista n, Bangladesh and Afghanistan who have 

71 
 
entered into India on or before 31.12.2014. The Com mittee was further apprised that this Bill was 
under consideration of a Joint Parliamentary Commit tee. The Ministry also stated that powers were 
delegated on 23.12.2016 to District Collectors of 1 6 Districts of 7 States and State Governments of 
remaining Districts for processing grant of Citizen ship for a period of 2 years. The amount of 
application/processing fees was also reduced to benefit minority community migrants from Pakistan, 
Bangladesh and Afghanistan. 
6.7.3 Some of the Members of the Committee took exc eption to the submission of the Ministry and 
queried as to how the Ministry can proceed with red uction of application fee for LTV while the bill 
was still being examined by the Joint Parliamentary  Committee concerned.  The Home Secretary 
replied that this was done as the fee is fixed unde r the rules and not under the Act which was being 
amended.  Moreover, as of now only the notification  for reduction of fee was issued and any 
application will be taken and processed only after the amendment Bill was passed.   
6.7.4 The Committee is surprised by the notificatio n notifying the reduction of application fee 
specifically for minority community only for LTV. T he Committee feels that the Ministry 
should have waited for the passage of the Bill by t he Parliament before going ahead with the 
notification. While the Committee appreciates the m easures taken by the Ministry as 
mentioned in Para 6.7.1, the Committee recommends t hat, notifications should be issued after 
The Citizenship (Amendment) Bill, 2016 is passed by the Parliament.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs,
having been authorized by the Committee to submit the report on its behalf, do hereby present this Two
Hundred Second Report on Demands for Grants (2017-18) relating to the Ministry of Development of
North Eastern Region (DoNER).

Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs is mandated to consider the
Demands for Grants of the related Ministries, and make report thereon. In pursuance thereof, the
Committee in its sitting held on 1st March, 2017 heard the presentation of the Secretary, and other
officials of the Ministry of DoNER as well as officers of the Implementing Ministries/Departments/
Agencies and considered the Demands for Grants (2017-18) of that Ministry.

papers received from the Ministry of DoNER:-
(i) Detailed Demands for Grants of the Ministry for the year 2017-18;
(ii) Background Notes on the Demands for Grants (2017-18);
(iii) Outcome Budget (2017-18) of the Ministry;
(iv) Annual Report (2016-17) of the Ministry;
(v) Written replies furnished by the Ministry to the Questionnaires sent to it by the Committee;
(vi) Presentation made by the Secretary of the Ministry and oral evidence; and
(vii) Oral and written clarifications given by the Ministry to the points/issues raised by the

CHAPTER-I
OVERVIEW
1.1 INTRODUCTION
1.1.1 The North Eastern Region (NER) collectively represents eight states of the North East viz.
Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura. The region
possesses enormous potential and opportunities and also inherent challenges. The Department of
Development of North Eastern Region was set up in September, 2001 under the Ministry of Home Affairs
and subsequently upgraded to a full-fledged Ministry in May 2004 underscoring its complete commitment
to ensure development with equity for the NER to unleash the potential of its human and natural
resources. The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region implements schemes and programmes
through State Governments and some Central Ministries for which Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources
(NLCPR) and funds for Special Packages are allocated. The Ministry aims to give focused attention to
address the special needs of the region. It mainly coordinates with various Ministries/Departments
primarily concerned with development activities in the NER whereas, the respective Ministries/Departments
remain responsible in implementation of programmes in their respective fields. North Eastern Council
(NEC) is a statutory Regional Planning Body which provides financial assistance for a variety of projects
including infrastructure projects like construction of roads, improving air connectivity etc. through State
Governments.
1.2 MANDATE AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE MINISTRY
1.2.1 As per the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961, the Second Schedule (Rule
3), subjects allotted to the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (Uttar Poorvi Kshetra Vikas
Mantralaya) are as follows:
(a) Matters relating to the planning, execution and monitoring of developmental schemes and
projects of North Eastern Region including those in the sectors of Power, Irrigation, Roads
and Communications;
(b) Hill Area Development Programme in North Eastern Region;
(c) Non-lapsable Fund for the North Eastern Region;
(d) North Eastern Council;
(e) North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Ltd. (NEDFi);
(f) North Eastern Regional Agricultural Marketing Corporation Limited (NERAMAC);
(g) The Sikkim Mining Corporation Limited;

2
(h) North Eastern Handloom and Handicrafts Development Corporation (NEHHDC), Shillong;
(i) Road works financed in whole or in part by the Central Government in the North Eastern
Region; and
(j) Planning of Road and Inland Waterways Transport in the North Eastern Region.
1.2.2 While the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) would coordinate with
various Ministries/Departments concerned with development and welfare activities in the North Eastern
Region, respective Ministries/Departments would be responsible in respect of subjects earmarked for
them. The projects under different schemes of the Ministry are planned and executed through the State
Governments. According to the Annual Report (2016-17) of the Ministry, its main mandate is to coordinate
with various Ministries/ Departments primarily concerned with development and welfare activities in the
region. It also monitors their expenditure under 10% GBS, as surrendered amounts are transferred to the
NLCPR (pool) which is notionally maintained by Ministry of Finance. However, it is a subject matter of
M/DoNER as per Allocation of Business rules. This exercise is being undertaken on annual basis and the
allocation and actual expenditure figures given by the respective Ministries/Departments are collected,
compiled and forwarded annually to Ministry of Finance for vetting.
1.3 TRANSFER OF SCHEMES TO LINE MINISTRIES
1.3.1 The Committee, taking note of the transferring of the scheme of organic farming from the
Ministry of DoNER to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Capacity Building & Technical
Assistance scheme to the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), desired to know
the reasons for such transfer of jurisdiction and whether such arrangement has encroached upon the
original mandate of the Ministry of DoNER and the residual role of the Ministry of DoNER in respect
of these schemes. In response to that, the Ministry of DoNER replied that in compliance with the
decision taken in the Committee of Secretaries meeting held on 16th September, 2016 on convergence
of Central Skill Development Schemes/Programmes/Institutes under the Umbrella of M/o Skill Development
and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and on proposal by the MSDE, Capacity Building component of Capacity
Building and Technical Assistance (CB&TA) scheme of Ministry of DoNER has been transferred to
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) so as to avoid increase in administrative
expenses, duplication of effort, non-uniformity of standardization, etc. It was also stated that the Ministry
of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare implements the organic farming scheme because of its domain
expertise.
1.3.2 It was further added by the Ministry of DoNER that it is closely coordinating with the Ministry
of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare through various committees constituted for the scheme not only in
respect of the scheme of organic farming but also in respect of other schemes for which joint workshops
have been organized in the North Eas?t. The Ministry of DoNER is a part of the Committee of MSDE
that reviews and approves the proposals made under the scheme. It has been mentioned in the Allocation
of Business Rules that "While the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region would coordinate
with various Ministries/Departments primarily concerned with development and welfare activities in

3
North Eastern Region, respective Ministries/Departments would be responsible in respect of subjects
allocated to them". As such, transfer of the schemes has not encroached upon the original mandate of
the Ministry of DoNER.
1.3.3 The Annual Report of the Ministry stipulates further that the coordinating role of the Ministry
emanated from monitoring development projects for socio-economic development of the region. The
Ministry coordinates with various Central Ministries/Departments in respect of the development and
welfare schemes/programmes implemented by them in the North Eastern Region. Besides, calling the
progress of expenditure out of the earmarked outlay for NER, a set of Ministries/Departments has been
assigned to each senior officer of the Ministry for regular and continuous interactions with respective
Ministries/Departments. In addition to the routine interactions, the Ministry also convenes sectoral review
meetings with key Ministries such as Railways, Road Transport & Highways, Civil Aviation, Power,
Environment, Forest & Climate Change, Tourism etc. for effective implementation of the schemes and
time-bound completion of major infrastructure projects. The Ministry of DoNER is represented in Inter-
Ministerial Groups of major Ministries such as MoRTH, Railways, MSME, Home, etc. and is also
consulted at policy formulation and project implementation stage through EFC, Cabinet note circulation.
To ensure co-ordination among the Central Ministries, Ministry of DoNER has constituted several Inter-
Ministerial Committees (IMC). Currently there are four IMCs functioning in Road sector, Civil Aviation
sector, Livelihood Programmes and Tourism sector. Meetings of the IMCs are held regularly.
1.3.4 The Committee understands that the Ministry of DoNER has the primary responsibility for
accelerating the overall economic development in NER and, in order to boost fast track
development, a greater synergy is required amongst the Ministry of DoNER and implementing
agencies of schemes. In this regard, the Committee reiterates its view expressed in its 173rd
report on strengthening of the working of the Ministry of DoNER for effective implementation
of Policies, Programmes, schemes and projects meant for NER that the Ministry of DoNER can
play a larger and effective role in shaping the regional developmental priorities and implementing
the regional or State-specific programmes and projects. Active involvement of the Ministry of
DoNER is a precondition for successful implementation of the policies, programmes, schemes,
and projects meant for the NE region. The Committee strongly reiterates its recommendation
that there is urgent need to review and redefine the role of the Ministry of DONER in coordinating
and liaising with the line Ministries. There should be a clear cut defined relationship between the
NITI Aayog, the Ministry of DoNER, and the NEC for dovetailing and synergizing developmental
plans, projects, and schemes and a mechanism for such coordination should be evolved.
1.3.5 The allocation of funds for the North Eastern Region is being done annually on lump sum basis
by the non-exempted Central Ministries/Departments at the BE/RE stage under Major Heads 2552 (for
revenue expenditure), 4552 (for capital expenditure) and 6552 (for loan expenditure) expended under
their respective functional schemes. In the Budget 2017-18 several changes were introduced, for example
the distinction between Plan and Non-Plan has been done away with, revenue/capital classification has
been adopted and Railway Budget merged with Union Budget. Besides, earmarking for North Eastern

4
Region has been reflected through Statement 11 of the Union Budget, Expenditure V olume. As per the
Statement 11, a total of ` 32,180.08 crore was allocated by 55 Central Ministries/Departments for NE
Region during 2016-17 (RE), including the Ministry of DoNER, but excluding the allocation by the
Ministry of Railways of ` 5050 crore for the region under the Rail Budget 2016-17. Similarly, for the
current Financial Year 2017-18, the total budgetary allocation for the NE Region by non-exempted
Ministries/Departments is ` 43,244.64 crore.
1.3.6 The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) has one Demand i.e. Demand
No. 23 which is in the List of Demands for Grants for the Financial Year 2017-18 and the Budget of
the Ministry includes the following Schemes (Major Head-wise):
(i) Major Head 2052 (Sectt. General Services): Secretariat General Services, covering the
Salaries and other administrative expenses of the Ministry;
(ii) Major Head 2070 (Other Administrative Services), North Eastern Council, Shillong:
Other Administrative Services, relating to Salaries and other administrative expenses of the
North Eastern Council, Shillong;
(iii) Major Head 2250: (Other Social Services): Capacity Building & Publicity: The provision
is for providing technical assistance for training of State Government Functionaries of
North Eastern States in the interest of good governance. The provision under Advocacy &
Publicity Scheme is for providing financial assistance to NGOs and Government agencies
for organizing business summit, trade expos, seminars, Media campaign etc. which are
meant for promotional activities involving the North Eastern Region.
(iv) Major Head 2552 (North Eastern Areas):
(a) Schemes of North Eastern Council (NEC): The NEC as a Regional Planning Body
aims to ensure integrated development of the eight States of North Eastern Region.
NEC provides funds for projects in sectors like agriculture, education, tourism,
health, community development and air connectivity.
(b) NE Region Livelihood Project (Externally-aided Project): The North East Region
Livelihood Project (NERLP) is a major initiative for addressing the needs of employment,
income and natural resource sustainability of the rural population of the NE Region.
The project is funded through the World Bank. The provision is for facilitating the
implementation of the project.
(c) NE States Road Project Management Unit; and
(d) Support for Consultancy, Monitoring, Third Party Evaluation, Impact Assessment
studies etc, under the Non Lapsable Central Pool of Resources Scheme.
(v) Major Head 3601(Grants- in- aid to State Governments)
(i) Central Pool of Resources for North Eastern Region. [NLCPR - State Scheme]: The
broad objective of the Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR - State) is

5
to ensure speedy development of infrastructure in the North Eastern Region and
Sikkim by increasing the flow of budgetary financing for specific viable infrastructure
projects/schemes to the State Governments in the region. Projects for infrastructure
development under NLCPR - State Scheme are identified/prioritized by State
Governments and submitted to the Ministry of DoNER for approval and providing
funds.
(ii) North Eastern Council - Special Development Project: The NEC gives Grants-in-aid
to the State Governments of North Eastern Region for Development of Sectors like
Agriculture & Allied, Power, Water Development, Banking Industries & Tourism,
Transport & Communication, Medical & Health, etc.
(iii) North East Road Sector Development Scheme- (Externally-aided Project) (Earlier
NESRIP-EAP): The provision is for North Eastern State Roads Investment Program
(NESRIP), an ADB assisted project for construction/upgradation of Roads in NE
Region.
(iv) Special Package for Bodoland Territorial Council: This is a Special Development
Package to give grant for funding identified infrastructure and development projects
of the area.
(v) Special Package for Karbi Anglong Territorial Council: This is a Special Development
Package to give grant for funding identified infrastructure and development projects
of the area.
(vi) Special Package for Dima Hasao Territorial Council: This is a Special Development
Package to give grant for funding identified infrastructure and development projects
of the area.
(vi) Major Head 4552(Capital Outlay on North Eastern Areas)
(i) Schemes of North Eastern Council [Capital outlay]: NEC supports improvement of
airports in NER and also provides for housing for NEC Staff.
(ii) Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources for North Eastern Region (NLCPR) Central:
The broad objective of the Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR) -
Central is to enable the Central Ministries/Departments to fund projects/schemes in
the North Eastern Region (NER) and implement schemes/projects of regional and/ or
national priorities in NER in addition to projects taken up by them through the 10%
mandatory earmarking.
(iii) North East Road Sector Development Scheme- Programme Component: The North
Eastern Road Sector Development Scheme (NERSDS) has been introduced for
rehabilitation/construction/up-gradation of Inter-State neglected roads in NER.

6
(iv) Schemes under the Social and Infrastructure Development Fund (SIDF): This is a
special fund for creation and up-gradation of infrastructure facilities in Arunachal
Pradesh and the border areas in North Eastern Region the provision for which is met
out of the Public account. Though the Budget of DoNER reflects an indicative
provision for this purpose, the amount does not have any additionality in the GBS of
the Ministry.
(vii) Major Head 6851 - (Loans for Village and Small Industries)
(a) Working Capital Loan to North Eastern Regional Agricultural Marketing Corporation
Ltd (NERAMAC): North Eastern Regional Agricultural Marketing Corporation Limited
(NERAMAC), a Central PSU, operates to promote food processing and trading of
Agricultural and Horticultural produce in the North Eastern Region. The provision is
to be used as working capital by the Corporation for carrying out its business
activities.
(b) Working Capital Loan to North Eastern Handicrafts & Handlooms Development
Corporation Ltd (NEHHDC): North Eastern Handicrafts and Handlooms Development
Corporation (NEHHDC) was set up in March 1977 to provide the developmental and
promotional inputs for products and design development, training and up-gradation of
technologies and for marketing the finished products of the region Ministry provides
loan to NEHHDC to cover its cash losses.
(viii) Major Head 6885 (Other loans to Industries & Minerals)
Loan to North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Limited (NEDFi): NEDFi was
incorporated as a public financial institution incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 on August 9,
1995 with its registered office at Guwahati. NEDFi aims to catalyse economic development of the North
Eastern Region. NEDFi is a financial institution which provides credit and other facilities to industrial
enterprises, infrastructure projects, agro-horticulture units in NE region for promotion, expansion and
modernization and also provides microfinance in all eight states of NER. The Long term loan is provided
to NEDFi for encouraging entrepreneurship in NER.

2.2 ADV ANCE/PERSPECTIVE PLANNING IN THE POST FIVE YEAR PLAN PHASE
2.2.1 When the 12th Five Year Plan ends in 2016-17 it will mark the end of traditional Five Year
development planning. This Ministry has identified key focus areas in medium and long term horizon.
A 3-year Action document for 2017-18 to 2019-20 aligned to the predictability of financial resources
during the 14th Finance Commission Award period has been prepared. The elements of an Inter-
Ministerial Coordinated Strategy for the period 2017-18 to 2023-24 have been identified. Connectivity
being the key focus area, the Ministry is in its coordinating role-tracking initiatives in road, rail and
telecom sector in close coordination with the implementing Ministries/Departments and also identifying
and bridging gaps in social and physical infrastructure through the DoNER/NEC schemes. It was
informed by the Ministry that efforts would be made to accelerate sustainable growth of the region
particularly keeping in view its comparative advantage in organic farming and potential of processed
products; handlooms and handicrafts, tourism, bamboo, medicinal plants as well as imparting newer
employable skill for promoting livelihood creation & entrepreneurship and scope for economic linkages
offered by the Act East Policy initiatives.
2.2.2 The Committee understands that the Five Year development planning approach is coming
to an end with the conclusion of the last financial year of the 12th Five Year Plan i.e. 2016-17.
The Committee takes note of the key focus areas identified by the Ministry to give impetus
during the medium and the long term period. The Committee desires that the Ministry of DoNER
should expedite the process of identification of the projects meant for being implemented in the
key focus areas so that the development process in those areas will be accelerated. The Committee
further desires that specific monitoring mechanism must be put in place to ensure timely
implementation of economic infrastructure projects to be undertaken during medium and long
term period. The Committee is of the considered view that when strict adherence to the timeline
and the stipulated cost are ensured, while implementing projects/schemes by the executing
agencies under the three year action plan, perceptible change can be achieved.
2.2.3 The Committee also takes note of the Inter Ministerial Coordinated Strategy chalked out
for the period 2017-18 to 2023-24. The Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry of
DoNER must be assigned the pivotal position in the whole arrangement so as to steer economic
development in NER. As indicated in the mandate of the Ministry, coordinating role of the
Ministry in tracking initiatives in the key focus areas like connectivity (i.e. rail, road, air) and,
telecom sector and the monitoring mechanism of implementing projects/schemes of the Ministry
as well as NEC, must be given top priority. The Ministry should also take maximum advantage
of the scope for economic linkages offered by the Act East Policy Initiative.

2.10.3 The Ministry apprised the Committee of major achievements of the NERLP as on December 2016
which are:-
(a) About 2.80 lakh rural households (House Holds) have been covered, against the target of
3 lakh rural HHs. Technical supports are being provided to further improve the livelihoods
of the beneficiaries.
(b) Project has formed 24,139 Self Help Groups as against the target of 28,000 as on December,
2016.
(c) Out of 24,139 SHGs, already formed, 19,787 SHGs have received either revolving fund or
Livelihood fund (community investment fund-CIF) from the Project. About 80% of the
SHG members have availed at least one cycle of loan out of the funds provided by the
project and of their own savings as against the minimum target of 60%.
(d) The increase in income for SHG HHs in real term who have availed loan for various
livelihood activities are in the range of 20%-25% (as against the target of at least 30%). The
income will go higher than 30% by the end of the Project.
(e) The implementation of Community Development Plan (CDP) and Skill Training & Placement
programs is progressing as per target and will achieve its target.
(f) Various initiatives are being taken up to improve the farm technology in different production
clusters of Livestock, Vegetables, Handloom & Handicrafts and Spices.
2.10.4  The progress of financial linkage/bank credit to the SHGs has been slow as only 300 SHGs have
received bank credit as against the target of 8400 SHGs due to poor network of bank branches especially
in Nagaland, shortage of manpower in banks and lack of confidence of bankers on SHGs.
2.10.5  Against the projected demand of `280.00 crore for 2017-18, only an amount of `150.00 crore
has been earmarked in BE 2017-18. Given the closing date and annual expenditure target of the project,
under- allocation of fund would affect the project activities. As such, additional fund would be sought
at the RE stage to achieve the target.
2.10.6  Pertaining to the Committee's query on the projects undertaken under NERLP and whether the
same have proved effective in exploring employment opportunities, improving rural livelihoods, in select
11 districts of Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura, the Ministry informed that out of the savings
mobilised by SHG members and community investment funds provided by the Project, more than 2 lakh
SHG members have availed loan for various livelihood activities. The Project is also set to take up 22

27
livelihood clusters, out of which 7 are at advance stage which will benefit more than 10,000 farmers
directly. As in December, 2016 the Community Development Plans (CDPs) are being executed in 206
villages which would impact more than 15,000 HHs. A total of 1600 CDPs would benefit a lakh HHs
by the end of 2017. Under the skill training, 5000 youths have been trained and 2114 youths have been
given placement.
2.10.7  The Committee is constrained to express its displeasure that against the estimated
expenditure of ````` 220.00 crore only ````` 150.00 crore was earmarked in BE 2016-17, thus leaving
a fund gap of ````` 70.00 crore. Against this, fund to tune of ````` 24.00 crore only was allocated at RE
stage. The resultant is reflected in the outcome of the scheme. As against the target of three

2.11.1 North East Road Sector Development Scheme (NERSDS) was formulated by the Ministry of
DoNER to take up such interstate roads as identified by NEC in consultation with the State Governments
of the Region that were critical for connectivity but were not maintained by the State Governments. The
objective of the scheme is to develop road transport Sector in the NER by extending financial support
for construction/up-gradation of strategic roads and corridors (ODR, MDR, Single lane and double lane
roads etc.). NEC as a Regional Planning body has supported the Infrastructure Development of the
Region since its inception. As a part of its initiative towards the development of the Region during FY
2013-14, NEC identified 47 strategically important interstate roads (1666 Km), in consultation with the
State Governments of the Region, which are orphan in nature, as these roads are not maintained by either
of the states. Initially, the scheme was administered by M/DoNER through an empowered Inter-Ministerial
Committee which would be responsible for screening, appraisal, approval and monitoring of project
proposals. Sanctioned projects would be implemented/executed by Central Ministry/Agency or State Govt
wherever feasible.

December, 2015 under the chairmanship of Secretary, DoNER, wherein after deliberations it was decided
that 4- roads from amongst the list identified by NEC were selected for consideration for funding under
the scheme. It was agreed that NHIDCL will be the implementing agency for all the approved projects
and they would finalize the DPR, incorporating therein a 4-years maintenance clause with cost involved
and would receive the fund from M/DoNER as lump-sum transfer for executing the works.
