2.1 ADV ANCE/PERSPECTIVE PLANNING IN THE POST FIVE YEAR PLAN PHASE
Recommendation
2.1.1 The Committee also takes note of the Inter-Ministerial Coordinated Strategy chalked out for the
period 2017-18 to 2023-24. The Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry of DoNER must
be assigned the pivotal position in the whole arrangement so as to steer economic development in NER.
As indicated in the mandate of the Ministry, coordinating role of the Ministry in tracking initiatives in
the key focus areas like connectivity (i.e. rail, road, air) and, telecom sector and the monitoring
mechanism of implementing projects/schemes of the Ministry as well as NEC, must be given top priority.
The Ministry should also take maximum advantage of the scope for economic linkages offered by the
Act East Policy Initiative. (Para 2.2.3 of 202nd Report)
Action Taken
2.1.2 Coordinating role of the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region emanates from monitoring
developmental projects for socio-economic development of the region. The Ministry coordinates with
various Central Ministries/Departments in respect of the development and welfare schemes/programmes
implemented by them in the North Eastern Region. However, respective Ministries/Departments are
responsible in respect of subjects allocated to them. As a part of Inter-Ministerial co-ordination, Ministry
of DoNER monitors and keeps track of expenditure under 10% GBS by non-exempted Ministries/
Departments. This exercise is being undertaken on annual basis and the allocation and actual expenditure
figures by respective Ministries/Departments are collected, compiled and forwarded annually to Ministry
of Finance for vetting. To further strengthen this monitoring mechanism, a digital monitoring framework
called "Track 10" is also being developed by the Ministry to track the annual allocation and expenditure
in North East. Moreover, mechanism for quarterly review of expenditure has already put in place recently
and Ministry of DoNER is now authorized to recommend re-appropriation from non-spending Ministries
to those Ministries who have exhausted their allocation and are in need of additional funds. To achieve
the best level of synergy and review issues involved in the implementation of Schemes/Programs in cross
cutting areas, Ministry of DoNER has also constituted several Inter-Ministerial Committees (IMC). Based
on Inter-Ministerial discussions, following 3 areas have been identified for close Inter- Ministerial focus,
i.e., STINER, Bamboo & Piggery.
2.1.3 Under Science and Technology Intervention in North Eastern Region (STINER) major thrust is
given towards the dissemination of clean technology and rural technology in farm & non-farm sectors,
available with the various scientific and technical institutes of India. Major partners in the STINER are
Office of Principal Scientific Adviser to Government of India, Ministry of DoNER, Bhabha Atomic
Research Centre (BARC), RUTAG (Rural Technology Action Group) of IITs, Council for Scientific &
11

12
Industrial Research (CSIR) and Indian Council for Agricultural Research (ICAR). They are contributing
and disseminating the appropriate technologies to the NER which will help in reducing the drudgery of
rural people. For reducing the solid waste in NE States, BARC is providing Clean Technology for
conversion of solid waste into energy. For dissemination of technology, MoUs have also been signed with
the Ministry under Science & Technology Interventions in the North East Region (STINER) aiming at
enabling STINER and promoting NISARGRUNA technology of BARC in bio-energy technology in
association with Tripura State.
2.1.4 An Inter-Ministerial Bamboo Sector Coordination Group (IBSCG) has been constituted in the
Ministry of DoNER to promote bamboo development in North Eastern Region. The Ministry is also
taking up Advocacy of Appropriate Technologies related to Bamboo and its usage via the Council for
Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR) and the O/o the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government
of India. The Ministry of DoNER in collaboration with the German Development Agency, GIZ and
International Network for Bamboo and Rattan (INBAR) is advocating optimal usage of bamboo resources
in NER and a pilot project is being taken up in Mizoram.
2.1.5 Recognizing the immense scope offered by Piggery for livelihoods in the NER Ministry of DoNER
will steer Inter Ministerial process to optimize the potential of the Piggery Sector in the NER.

DoNER during the consideration of Demands for Grants (2017-18) pertaining to the Ministry. The

3.7 NORTH EAST REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MARKETING CORPORATION (NERAMAC)
Recommendation
3.7.1 The Committee takes note of the submission of the Ministry that allocation of 
` 2.00 crore in RE
2016-17 and BE 2017-18 to NERAMAC is not sufficient to meet the requirement of working capital
required for its business activities and an amount of ` 7.11 crore would be required as working capital
as a part of ` 20.86 crore one time fund requirement. The Committee observes that it is ironical that

22
on the one hand NERAMAC has been declared as a sick company due to its negative net worth and on
the other hand NERAMAC is expected to create a world class infrastructure for processing, value
addition and marketing of agricultural allied goods in NER. The sorry state of affairs is that no
concerted efforts have been made during last two years because of scarcity of funds with the organization.
Under the said circumstances, the Committee feels that the first and foremost course of action is to
improve the financial strength of NERAMAC itself. The Committee takes note of the revival plan under
consideration of the Ministry. The Committee recommends that Government should take an early decision
on the revival package without further procrastination. (Para 2.17.4 ibid)
Action Taken
3.7.2 The Government has taken a conscious decision to explore the possibility of reviving the NERAMAC.
Currently, the Ministry entrusted the task of preparing the Techno Economic Viability Report to North
Eastern Development Finance Corporation Limited (NEDFi). NEDFi is in the process of updating and
finalising the report through extensive consultation with all the stakeholders in all the states of NER. After
getting it vetted by a third party organization, the Ministry will take a view on how to go about revival
of NERAMAC. In the meanwhile, a number of steps have been taken to make NERAMAC a vibrant
organization. Many professionals in the field of finance and accounts have been appointed to ensure
proper financial management. The manpower strength of NERAMAC at different locations in the region
has been reworked and redeployed to suit the functional needs. Necessary action has also been taken
to comply with the essential regulatory requirements of various kinds. Besides the steps having been
taken to strengthen the organization from within, care has also been taken to implement its core mandate
like enhancing the income of the farmers of the region by means of market intervention. Some of the
recent initiatives of NERAMAC are as under:
(i) Sikkim is the largest producer of large Cardamom. But the farmers of Sikkim have not been
getting proper price for their produce. Price ranged from ` 420 to ` 480 per Kg which was
even lower than the cost of production due to which farmers started avoiding its production.
NERAMAC then intervened and conducted auction of the large Cardamom. In the recent
auction, farmers got almost double the rate of the prevailing price as stated above. NERAMAC
is also planning to conduct such auction in collaboration with Spices Board in other NER
states like Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland so that the farmers' income can be enhanced.
(ii) Recently, NERAMAC in collaboration with MSTC (Metal Scrap Trading Corporation- a PSU
under the Ministry of Steel) and; CRWC (Central Railways Warehousing Corporation- a PSU
under Ministry of Food and Consumer Affairs) marketed 700 MT of fresh Ginger from
Tuinsang (a remote district of Nagaland) through e-auction. In this process, the farmers got
better price for their produce.
(iii) It is well known that majority of agriculture and horticulture produce of North Eastern
Region are organic by default. NERAMAC has taken steps to market them so as to ensure
premium price for the farmers of North Eastern Region. Recently, NERAMAC has launched
much awaited common brand for entire North East, namely ONE (Organic North East). By

23
doing so, all organic produce of the North Eastern Region would get an umbrella brand
which will enhance their visibility in a big way in larger market including export market.
(iv) Recently, NERAMAC has opened its organic showroom cum restaurant under the brand
name "ONE" (Organic North East) at Dilli Haat, INA, which is one of the happening places
in New Delhi. NERAMAC is also planning to open similar stalls at other NDMC locations
so that the benefit of North East natural produce can be extended to people of Delhi and
in return farmers of NER may get remunerative prices.
(v) NERAMAC is also exploring the opening of stalls at some of the Metro stations in different
parts of Delhi for selling/promoting the North East Agro-horti products for ultimate benefit
of the farmers of the region.
Further Recommendation
3.7.3 The marketing intervention of NERAMAC to improve the financial position of farmers of
NER is well taken by the Committee. However, poor financial conditions and inadequate inter-
mediary steps undertaken by the Government to improve the financial viability of the Corporation
is a matter of concern for the Committee. The Committee wonders as to how a financially
dwindling Company is expected to implement its core mandate/activities efficiently and effectively
like creation of a world class infrastructure for processing, value addition and marketing of
agricultural allied goods in NER. The Committee takes exception to the fact that the NERAMAC
did not get allocation of amount of ````` 7.11 crore working capital to carry out its business
activities, as a part of ````` 20.86 crore one time fund requirement. The Committee apprehends that
by the time the revival plan of NERAMAC is finalized due to managerial reluctance and procedural
delay, the financial viability of the corporation may dwindle further. The Committee, therefore,
strongly recommends that the sooner the revival plan of NERAMAC is finalized and implemented
better it would be not only for the corporation but also for the entire agricultural and allied
sector in NER.
3.8 MANAGEMENT OF DEVELOPMENTAL PROJECTS UNDERTAKEN BY NEC AND UNDER
NLCPR
Recommendation
3.8.1 The Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry must focus on bigger projects where the
average envelope size must be 
` 30 crore to `40 crore because fewer projects of reasonable size can be
Monitored better and completed quickly in one or two years without time and cost overruns.
(Para 3.1.3 ibid)
Action Taken
3.8.2 North Eastern Region (NEC) is funding projects in far flung and remote villages and backward
areas of NER with a number of bottlenecks such as inaccessibility etc. Increasing the project ticket size
to ` 30 to 40 crore in a strict manner may not be feasible. It is to mention that the projects taken up
under Transport and Communication Sector are mostly above ` 100 crore. Ongoing projects are monitored

24
and inspection carried out on a regular basis both by NEC and States. However, efforts can be made
to keep the average size of the projects at 15-20 crore.
Further Recommendation
3.8.3 The Committee is unable to understand as to how the projects funded by NEC in far flung
and remote villages and backward areas of NER with bottleneck of inaccessibility, as pleaded by
the Ministry of DoNER, would act as a deterrent factor in increasing the average envelope size
to ````` 30 crore– ````` 40 crore. At the same time, the Ministry cites the fund size of ````` 100 crore in
the Transport and Communication Sector. On the other hand, the Ministry appears indifferent
to the recommendation of the Committee to enhance the fund size from ````` 15 crore to ````` 20 crore.
The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation as made in para 3.1.3 of 202nd Report.
Recommendation
3.8.4 The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the projects should be smaller in number,
bigger in envelope size and there should be tighter time-frame for implementation and the guillotine must
be applied at the end of three years. The committee notes the assurance of the Secretary of the Ministry
of DoNER to take up the matter in the Plenary Council to push that the minimum project size should
be 
` 30 crore and the first instalment would be ` 15 crore in order to overcome the legacy of procrastination.
(Para 3.1.5 ibid)
Action Taken
3.8.5 As brought out in reply to Para 3.1.3 above, it may be reiterated that the North Eastern Region
(NEC) is funding projects in far flung and remote villages and backward areas of NER with a number
of bottlenecks such as inaccessibility etc. Increasing the project ticket size to ` 30 to 40 crore in a strict
manner may not be feasible. However, efforts can be made to keep the average size of the projects at
15-20 crore. During the NEC Plenary held in May, 2017 (Agenda Item No. 4), this aspect along with
the Conversion of NEC Schemes to Central Sector Schemes was discussed. It was generally accepted
that the emphasis should be on large infrastructure projects having interstate ramifications and necessary
convergence with other Central Sector Schemes implemented by other Ministries.
Further Recommendation
3.8.6 The Committee is well aware of the limited working season in NER, therefore, it should
not be advocated as ground for time overrun in completion of the projects undertaken by the
Ministry. So far as non-submission of Utilisation Certificates (UCs) by the State Governments
and implementing agencies are concerned, the Ministry of DoNER may keep them on alert mode
through effective monitoring mechanism of online submission of UCs at the earliest.
3.8.7 The Committee is aware of the challenges faced at the project formulation and selection
stage and understands that in exceptional circumstances it may not be feasible to keep the size
of the project uniform due to multifarious bottlenecks of the North Eastern Region. However,
the Committee desires to insist that emphasis on large infrastructure projects, as generally
accepted in the NEC Plenary session, should be the guiding principle and exceptions should be

25
few and rare. Furthermore, the Committee is not satisfied with the fact that the Ministry has
not furnished any reply on the time-frame aspect of the projects. In this regard, the Committee
reiterates its recommendation that the Ministry should ensure that the timeline of the project
is strictly adhered to. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should ensure that
any bottlenecks are anticipated and accounted for at the project formulation stage itself so that
the project implementation agency may not use this as an excuse for the delay in the
implementation of the project.

3.10 INFRASTRUCTURE CIVIL  AVIATION
Recommendation
3.10.1 The Committee understands that long-term measures like operationalization of non-operational
airports, construction of more green-field airports, enhancement of overall capacities of terminals and
aprons and hangars require time for fructification especially in view of infrastructural bottlenecks
peculiar to NER. The Committee, however, desires that all the long term strategies should be given
momentum and there should be no scope for time and cost overruns. The Committee also recommends
that the Ministry should intensify its efforts and expedite the implementation of short-term measures like
extension of runways, upgradation of safety and security infrastructure and installation of Instrument
Landing Systems wherever required. The Ministry of DoNER may take up with Ministry of Civil Aviation
for early completion of short term measures. (Para 3.3.10 ibid)
Action Taken
3.10.2 There are 11 operational airports and 12 non-operational airports in the North-East Region. Out
of the 11 operational airports, Guwahati and Imphal are international airports. The upgradation of the

26
operational airports is a continuous process depending on the traffic demand and other operational
requirements.
3.10.3 Increasing the capacity of Terminal Building and operational area at the existing operational airports
is depending on the traffic. Works like extension of runway, upgradation of safety and security
infrastructure, construction of boundary walls, installation of ILS, A TC Tower-cum-File station, construction
of terminal buildings, modification of terminal buildings etc., are already taken up.
3.10.4 Operationalisation of the existing non-operational airports is a long term strategy and it is proposed
to operationalise Tezu at Arunachal Pradesh for which the development works are in progress. Further,
there is proposal to establish the airports at Along, Ziro, Passighat in Arunachal Pradesh and Rupsi in
Assam as Joint Use airports with IAF wherein AAI will construct Civil Enclaves. The State Governments
to provide land for Civil Enclaves in Arunachal Pradesh/de-notifying the forest land at Rupsi.
3.10.5 The construction of Greenfield Airport is also a long term strategy. At present, there is no airport
in Sikkim and the 1st airport is coming up at Pakyong near to the capital. The work is in advance stage
and is expected to be completed by Sept., 2017. Further, there is proposal to construct an airport in the
capital city of Arunachal Pradesh i.e. Itanagar. After detailed comparative analysis, the high level Committee
recommended Hollongi site is preferable for construction of Greenfield Airport. For this, revised DPR
along with details shall be submitted to the Standing Committee for consideration and approval in due
course.
3.10.6 Considering the topography of the region, it will be better to have Instrument Landing facilities
at all the operational airports. At present, the Instrument Landing facility is available at all the airports
except Shillong and Lilabari. The Civil Enclaves at Jorhat and Tezpur have DVOR facility so that these
airports also coming under instrument operations. There is plan to provide ILS at Shillong and Lilabari
depending upon the provision of land, site conditions and removal of obstacles by the State Government.
3.10.7 Considering Night landing facilities at all the operational airports is another long term strategy. At
present, Night Landing Facility available and permission from DGCA is also available for the airports at
Guwahati, Imphal, Agartala, Dibrugarh, Dimapur and Lilabari.
Further Recommendation
3.10.8 The Ministry of DoNER may apprise the Committee about the details of projects pending
under the Ministry of Civil Aviation with estimated/enhanced cost and time-frame to be completed
along with physical and financial achievement against set targets. The Ministry of DoNER may
also inform the Committee about the steps taken to overcome the bottlenecks in the direction
of completion of projects undertaken and also about the projects under consideration for their
early take off in Civil Aviation Sector in NER.

3.12 TOURISM SECTOR IN NER
Recommendation
3.12.1 The Committee takes note of the measures undertaken by the Ministry of Tourism to promote
tourism in the North East Region and the challenges being faced in tapping the full potential of NER
as a preferred tourist destination. The Committee desires that the challenges and bottlenecks being faced
in the promotion of tourism should be addressed appropriately to make tourism attractive. Since NER
has abundant potential to attract tourists from all around the globe and also because tourism is the main
stay of the people of NER, it is imperative that the policy makers and the implementing agencies of
projects/schemes pertaining to the promotion of tourism in NER must pay attention in the augmentation
of tourism infrastructure like connectivity by rail, roads, air or waterways so that NER becomes the most
favoured tourism destination in the country. In order to enhance the sense of hospitality, there is need
to improve capacity building for service providers in the tourism sector. There is ample scope to promote
specific attractive features at various centres of tourism like eco tourism, medicinal and naturopathy
tourism and historical, mythological, religious and wildlife aspects of tourism. (Para 3.15.4 ibid)
Action Taken
3.12.2 The primary responsibility for tourism infrastructure is of Ministry of Tourism. However, their
efforts are supplemented by the NEC through its own resources as well. Efforts of providing a general
connectivity through roads/air etc. to the remote areas of the region, as stated below, do contribute
towards upgradation of the tourism infrastructure also.

28
3.12.3 North Eastern Council (NEC), Ministry of DoNER under its schemes has been supporting the
State Governments in improving the road connectivity in the region. Of NEC's total budget of ` 925
crore, the allocation for road sector is around 20%. A special road development scheme titled "North
Eastern Road Sector Development Scheme (NERSDS)" (though not tourism specific) has been introduced
to address the issues of inter-state road connectivity. NEC's efforts in improving the road and air
connectivity have contributed positively to the promotion of tourism in the NE region.
3.12.4 For improving air connectivity in the region, NEC has supported Airports Authority of India (AAI)
in improving airports at Guwahati, Shillong, Dibrugarh, Imphal and Jorhat. NEC has also supported the
construction of the new airport at Tezu in Arunachal Pradesh. NEC has been providing viability gap
funding to Alliance Air for providing air connectivity between Kolkata to Guwahati, Shillong, Tezpur and
Lakhimpur.
3.12.5 NEC's efforts in improving the road and air connectivity have contributed positively to the promotion
of tourism in the NE region.
3.12.6 NEC has been supporting the State Governments for capacity building for service providers in
tourism. NEC also supports institutes such as Institute of Hotel Management, Food Craft Institute etc.
for conducting capacity building training courses in tourism. Ministry of Tourism and NEC has been
supporting the State Governments for promoting theme-based tourist circuits.
3.12.7 NEC, Ministry of DoNER has also facilitated the setting up of the North East Tourism Development
Council (NETDC) which has been set up as a Section 8 Company with the participation of the private
sector. The NETDC will be dedicatedly promoting theme-based intra-regional and international tourist
circuits, promoting the North East of India-Paradise Unexplored, as a single tourist destination and brand,
coordinating tourism promotion among the states and tour operators and also associate/partner with
Foreign Tourism Promotion Bodies especially from East and South and South Asian Countries. NETDC
will also promote Inter-Country Tourism Trader Forum combining North East States with BIMSTEC and
ASEAN countries under a single East South Asia brand for joint promotion of common theme based
tourism products.
Further Recommendation
3.12.8 The Committee appreciates the role of NEC, Ministry of DoNER in supporting the line
Ministries in improving the road, air and waterways connectivity in the direction of augmentation
of tourism infrastructure in NER. However, the Committee desires that NERSDS be also re-
oriented to tourist spot connectivity i.e. tourism-specific. NETDC must be directed to promote
theme-based intra-regional and international tourist circuits besides co-ordinating tourism
promotion. The Committee further reiterates its recommendation that the Ministry of DoNER
in tandem with the Ministry of Tourism must promote eco-tourism, medicinal & naturopathy
tourism and historical, mythological, religious and wildlife spectrum of tourism to improve the
present basket of tourism products.
Recommendation
3.12.9 The Committee notes the number of efforts being undertaken by the Government for promoting
tourism in North Eastern Region. However, the Committee feels that only promotional activities and

29
publicity will not make up for the infrastructural and connectivity bottlenecks that have limited the
tourism potential of NER. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should chalk out a
long-term strategy in consultation with the State Governments of NER and Ministry of Tourism to address
the infrastructural bottlenecks particularly accommodation facilities, intra-regional connectivity and
accessibility of exotic tourist destinations in NER. (Para 3.15.7 ibid)
Action Taken
3.12.10 NEC through Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) had prepared the Integrated Tourism Master Plan
for North Eastern Region. A total of 31 Regional Circuits were identified to be developed of which 9
have been taken up in the 1st Phase. States have been prioritising their projects, both infrastructure as
well as soft interventions, aligned with the recommendations of the Master Plan.
3.12.11 Ministry of Tourism under its Swadesh Darshan and PRASAD schemes and NEC under its own
schemes has been supporting the State Governments of NER in creating tourist infrastructure as well
as taking up skill building programs for the local youth.
3.12.12 NEC has funded several infrastructure development projects in all the States which include
tourist lodges, Yatri Niwas, development of tourist spots and historical sites, wayside amenities, etc.
3.12.13 NEC, Min. of DoNER is actively considering funding for completion of the incomplete projects
under the erstwhile PIDDC scheme of the Ministry of Tourism so that tourist infrastructure can be built
up rapidly in the region.
Further Recommendation
3.12.14 The Committee takes note that only 9 out of a total of 31 Regional Circuits identified
for developments have been taken up for development in the 1st phase. The Committee
recommends that remaining 22 may also be taken up for developing to ensure a network of
tourist infrastructure as per Integrated Tourism Master Plan for North Eastern Region. The
Committee further recommends that NEC must take an early decision for funding the incomplete
projects under the erstwhile Product Infrastructure Development at Destinations and Circuits
(PIDDC) Scheme of the Ministry of Tourism so that the money already spent on those does not
go waste and the tourist infrastructure can be built in NER to attract the tourists from within
the country and abroad as well.

CHAPTER-IV
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION IN RESPECT OF WHICH FINAL REPLY OF THE
GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN RECEIVED
4.1 TRANSFER OF SCHEMES TO LINE MINISTRIES
Recommendation
4.1.1 The Committee understands that the Ministry of DoNER has the primary responsibility for accelerating
the overall economic development in NER and, in order to boost fast track development, a greater
synergy is required amongst the Ministry of DoNER and implementing agencies of schemes. In this
regard, the Committee reiterates its view expressed in its 173rd report on strengthening of the working
of the Ministry of DoNER for effective implementation of Policies, Programmes, schemes and projects
meant for NER that the Ministry of DoNER can play a larger and effective role in shaping the regional
developmental priorities and implementing the regional or State-specific programmes and projects. Active
involvement of the Ministry of DoNER is a precondition for successful implementation of the policies,
programmes, schemes, and projects meant for the NE region. The Committee strongly reiterates its
recommendation that there is urgent need to review and redefine the role of the Ministry of DONER in
coordinating and liaising with the line Ministries. There should be a clear cut defined relationship
between the NITI Aayog, the Ministry of DoNER, and the NEC for dovetailing and synergizing
developmental plans, projects, and schemes and a mechanism for such coordination should be evolved.
(Para 1.3.4 of 202nd Report)
Action Taken
4.1.2 Inputs have been sought from NITI Aayog in the matter. For a better functional integration
between the two organisations, Secretary, DoNER has been appointed as ex officio  Member, North
Eastern Council and Secretary, North Eastern Council as ex officio Additional Secretary in the Ministry
of DoNER.
Further Recommendation
4.1.3 The Committee hopes that the Ministry of DoNER would apprise the Committee of the
inputs received from NITI Aayog as soon as the same is received. The Committee recommends
that the Ministry of DoNER must chalk out suitable strategy for accelerating the overall economic
development in NER. The Committee strongly recommends for evolution of better co-ordination
amongst NITI Aayog, the Ministry of DoNER and NEC, in prioritising and formulating regional
or state-specific developmental plans/projects and schemes. The Committee would further like
to be informed of the co-ordination & controlling/monitoring mechanism established amongst the
Ministry of DoNER, line Ministries and other concerned implementing agencies for efficient and
effective implementation of various projects/schemes/programmes for overall distribution of
benefits of development amongst people living in NER.
31

32
4.2 ADV ANCE/PERSPECTIVE PLANNING IN THE POST FIVE YEAR PLAN PHASE
Recommendation
4.2.1 The Committee understands that the Five Year development planning approach is coming to an
end with the conclusion of the last financial year of the 12th Five Year Plan i.e. 2016-17. The
Committee takes note of the key focus areas identified by the Ministry to give impetus during the medium
and the long term period. The Committee desires that the Ministry of DoNER should expedite the process
of identification of the projects meant for being implemented in the key focus areas so that the development
process in those areas will be accelerated. The Committee further desires that specific monitoring mechanism
must be put in place to ensure timely implementation of economic infrastructure projects to be undertaken
during medium and long term period. The Committee is of the considered view that when strict adherence
to the timeline and the stipulated cost are ensured, while implementing projects/schemes by the executing
agencies under the three year action plan, perceptible change can be achieved. (Para 2.2.2)
Action Taken
4.2.2 In pursuance of Ministry of Finance OM No. 24(35)/PF-II/2012 dated 05th August, 2016, laying
down guidelines for outcome review of the ongoing schemes of Central Ministries/Departments for
continuance beyond 12th FYP, evaluation of ongoing schemes of Ministry of DoNER has been conducted.
Based on this, EFC/SFC notes with proposed modifications of different ongoing schemes of Ministry of
DoNER viz. NLCPR, NEC, SIDF etc. were prepared and circulated. The proposed changes on substantive
nature of schemes funding pattern and implementing agencies was thoroughly discussed with the State
Governments in the meeting held for the purpose and also NEC Plenary. From FY 2017-18, the schemes
of North Eastern Council (NEC), NLCPR and NERSDS have been categorized as Central Sector Schemes
and are no longer categorised as block grants to States. It may also be noted that Ministry of DoNER
schemes have got special dispensation from Ministry of Finance to use Major Head 3601 as one-time
measure to release funds to State treasuries instead of Implementing Agencies directly till March, 2020
provided funds are routed through PFMS. This will ensure that the schemes are implemented without
any glitch as the implementing agencies in NER have limited capacity/expertise in running Central Sector
Schemes and funds are released following the 'just-in-time' principle. Further, unlike the usual practice
of seeking appraisal/approval of schemes for three years (2017-18 to 2019-20) i.e. co-terminus with
Fourteenth Finance Commission period, Ministry of DoNER has sought appraisal/approval of its schemes
for 2 years to ensure their timely completion. With necessary approvals at various levels, the modified
schemes will commence from this Financial Year itself.
4.2.3 The North Eastern Council in its 66th Plenary held in May, 2017 approved a Regional Plan to be
implemented in 3 year period between 2017-18 to 2019-20. Based on the core elements of the Regional
Plan, an EFC Memo on the Schemes of NEC has been prepared and circulated for comments of line
Ministries. Another, EFC Memo on the North East Road Sector Development Schemes has also been
formulated for upgradation of neglected Inter-State Roads. On approval of the two Schemes implemented
by the Competent Authority, the implementation of the projects under these schemes shall be taken up.
It has been envisaged that no new project shall be taken during the 3rd year (2019-20) and the projects
already undertaken shall be accomplished. Robust inbuilt monitoring mechanism in the revised schemes
will ensure adherence to timelines.

33
4.3 CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES FOR NORTH EAST AND SIKKIM
Recommendation
4.3.1 The Committee feels that when the projects are underway, there is no reason why the Ministry of
Finance should reduce the allocation at RE. Already several projects in NER are suffering cost and time
and overruns. Reduction in allocation will further affect the projects. A pragmatic view should be taken
for allocations to NER. (Para 2.7.4 ibid)
Action Taken
4.3.2 The recommendations of the Committee have been noted. The recommendations of the Parliamentary
Standing Committee have been forwarded to Ministry of Finance for appropriate action.
Further Recommendation
4.3.3 The Committee desires that it may be apprised of the action taken by Ministry of Finance
in this regard.
Recommendation
4.3.4 The Committee notes that allocation for 2017-18 has been kept at the same level of BE 2016-
17. At least this year, the allocation should not be reduced at RE stage. The Ministry should also ensure
that the projects are implemented without time and cost overruns. The Committee further notes that
against the projected demand of 
` 770.00 crore, an amount only to the tune of ` 695.00 crore has been
earmarked in 2017-18 which is not sufficient to meet the requirements of funds towards first installment
of 58 projects costing to ` 941.23 crore retained during the current financial year and committed
liabilities of subsequent instalments towards various ongoing projects. Subject to the status of implementation
of the projects, allocation may be enhanced to meet the requirement of funds of ongoing projects.
(Para 2.7.6 ibid)
Action Taken
4.3.5 The recommendations of the Committee have been noted. Ministry of Finance will be requested
to grant additional allocations, if necessary, at RE Stage of 2017-18. The recommendations of the
Parliamentary Standing Committee have been forwarded to Ministry of Finance for appropriate action.
Further Recommendation
4.3.6 The Committee reiterates its recommendation and would like to be apprised the action
taken by the Ministry of Finance in this regard.
4.4 SOCIAL AND INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT FUND (SIDF)
Recommendation
4.4.1 The Committee was given to understand that reduction in allocation of capital outlay under Social
and Infrastructure Development Fund (SIDF) from 
` 170.00 crore in BE 2016-17 to `100 crore in RE
2016-17 and to ` 110.00 crore in BE 2017-18 was done commensurate with the progress of the projects

34
and utilisation of funds by the State Governments. The Committee takes a serious view of the underutilization
of funds even after reduction at RE stage in 2016-17. The Committee notes that the delay in release of
funds to the implementing agencies of various projects and non-receipt of utilization certificate and
relevant documents from the State Government are the factors affecting speedy implementation of
projects under SIDF and leading to underutilization of funds. Although the fund earmarked under SIDF
is an indicative provision and is debitable from the Public Accounts and does not have any additionality
in the GBS of the Ministry of DoNER, the objective of the scheme is of paramount importance as the
fund is meant for border areas facing special problems which could not be tackled through normal
schemes. The Committee strongly feels that unless and until the mechanism for implementation of projects
is strengthened, the future of the projects identified at the estimated cost of 
` 586.02 crore would be
jeopardized. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of DoNER must perform a pro-
active role in co-ordination with the stakeholders concerned and ensure optimum utilization of earmarked
funds within the same financial year. (Para 2.15.6 ibid)
Action Taken
4.4.2 The Ministry has taken following measures to accelerate utilization of funds under SIDF:
(i) Continuously pursuing the matter with State Governments. Regular Video Conference with
the State Governments to review the projects and discuss other issues with object to
accelerate utilization of funds under SIDF.
(ii) Camping of officers of Ministry of DoNER.
Further Recommendation
4.4.3 The Committee hopes that the measures undertaken by the Ministry of DoNER to accelerate
utilization of funds under Social and Infrastructure Development Fund (SIDF) would result in
speedier execution of undertaken projects and would obviate time and cost overruns. The Committee
further desires that all projects under the scheme identified at the estimated cost of ````` 586.02
crore must be completed within stipulated timeframe.
4.5 TOURISM SECTOR IN NER
Recommendation
4.5.1 Though the number of foreign tourists and domestic tourists visiting North Eastern Region is
increasing year after year, however, the Committee desires that there must be a better method for counting
the number of visitors, in order to be absolutely sure that the count of the number of tourists counted
is reasonably correct. For tourists visiting the North East, the best record appears to be hotel registration
which is mandatory. The Committee feels that hotel registration is a reasonably foolproof method because
the passport numbers are collected there. (Para 3.15.6 ibid)
Action Taken
4.5.2 The recommendation for counting the number of tourists visiting the North East of India through
hotel registrations has been taken up with the NE State Governments.

35
Further Recommendation
4.5.3 The Committee would like to be apprised of the response of the State Governments on the
suggestion of the Ministry of DoNER for counting the number of tourists visiting NER through
registration of tourists in the hotels.
4.6 MAJULI ISLANDS
Recommendation
4.6.1 The Committee takes notes of the allocation of 
` 207.00 crores for Majuli Islands to be spent in
three years for protection of river banks from erosion due to Brahmaputra river. The Committee hopes
that the project will be completed within the stipulated period and the work will be of good quality so
that there is no further erosion of the river bank. (Para 3.17.2 ibid)

4.6.2 The matter is being regularly reviewed with Ministry of Water Resources, River Development &
Ganga Rejuvenation. The project was sanctioned in the month of December, 2016. Brahmaputra Board

4.6.3 After scrutiny, five bidders were found qualified for this work. Now issuance of Request for

4.6.4 The Committee desires to be apprised of step taken with regard to progress made on the
issue of Majuli Islands after Request for Proposal (RFP) proposal for which allocation to the tune
of ````` 207.00 crore has been earmarked to protect the river banks from erosion caused by
Brahmaputra River.

DIMA HASAO TERRITORIAL COUNCIL
The Committee observes that under Dima Hasao Territorial Council (DHTC) Package of
`````200.00 crore, 10 projects costing `````121.64 crore has already been taken up for funding by the

NORTH EAST REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MARKETING CORPORATION (NERAMAC)
The marketing intervention of NERAMAC to improve the financial position of farmers of
NER is well taken by the Committee. However, poor financial conditions and inadequate inter-
mediary steps undertaken by the Government to improve the financial viability of the Corporation
is a matter of concern for the Committee. The Committee wonders as to how a financially
dwindling Company is expected to implement its core mandate/activities efficiently and effectively
like creation of a world class infrastructure for processing, value addition and marketing of
agricultural allied goods in NER. The Committee takes exception to the fact that the NERAMAC
did not get allocation of amount of ````` 7.11 crore working capital to carry out its business
activities, as a part of ````` 20.86 crore one time fund requirement. The Committee apprehends that
by the time the revival plan of NERAMAC is finalized due to managerial reluctance and procedural
delay, the financial viability of the corporation may dwindle further. The Committee, therefore,
strongly recommends that the sooner the revival plan of NERAMAC is finalized and implemented
better it would be not only for the corporation but also for the entire agricultural and allied
sector in NER. (Para 3.7.3)

the Transport & Communication Sector. On the other hand, the Ministry appears indifferent to
the recommendation of the Committee to enhance the fund size from ````` 15 crore to ````` 20 crore.
The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation as made in para 3.1.3 of 202nd Report.
(Para 3.8.3)
The Committee is well aware of the limited working season in NER, therefore, it should
not be advocated as ground for time overrun in completion of the projects undertaken by the
Ministry. So far as non-submission of Utilisation Certificates (UCs) by the State Governments
and implementing agencies are concerned, the Ministry of DoNER may keep them on alert mode
through effective monitoring mechanism of online submission of UCs at the earliest.
(Para 3.8.6)
The Committee is aware of the challenges faced at the project formulation and selection
stage and understands that in exceptional circumstances it may not be feasible to keep the size
of the project uniform due to multifarious bottlenecks of the North Eastern Region. However,
the Committee desires to insist that emphasis on large infrastructure projects, as generally
accepted in the NEC Plenary session, should be the guiding principle and exceptions should be

CHAPTER - I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED
BY THE GOVERNMENT
1.1 REASONS BEHIND THE FLOOD
Carrying Capacity of the Water Bodies
Recommendation
1.1.1 The Committee takes note of the submission of the Ministry of Water Resources that the encroachment
of lakes and river beds played a major role in causing massive flood in Chennai. The Committee feels
that the State Government should check mafia involved in illegal construction for business and usurping
water bodies for their real estate business. The flood channels and riverbed should be cleared as soon
as possible by removing illegal/ unauthorized constructions. (Para 7.1.3 of 198th Report)
Action Taken
1.1.2 The Government of Tamil Nadu informed the Committee that they fully accept the recommendations
that the flood channels, river beds as well as other water bodies should be cleared by removing the
encroachments. Further, it is informed that most of these encroachments are by landless migrant labours
that come in search of employment to urban local bodies. Those encroachments made by real estate
business operators and other institutional land grabbers in the water bodies are not significant and
evictions are carried out without much difficulty as and when it is identified. (For instance, the illegal
constructions in the major riverbeds i.e. Kosasthalayar, Coovam and Adayar River by some of the
educational institutions were evicted during the year 2005-06).
1.1.3 The State Government also informed that the unprecedented floods during the year 2015 was due
to multiple factors, the major reason being the extremely heavy rains in the catchment areas and in the
urban areas. The actual rainfall in Chennai district during 01st December, 2015 to 5th December, 2015
was 399 mm as against normal rainfall of 40.6 mm during the same days which is excess of 883
percentage. During the same period the Kancheepuram district received rainfall of 467.2 mm as against
the normal rain fall of 34.5 mm which is excess of 1254 percentage. The problem was accentuated due
to breach of systems tanks and choking of river canals due to siltation, shoal formation and encroachments.
1.1.4 The Government of Tamil Nadu stated that they had launched a major drive during 2015 and 2016
for desiltation and removal of shoals and encroachments to ensure that the water courses are clear.
During the flood period itself 7170 number of encroachments were evicted in Adayar River and 4239
families have been accommodated in 4239 tenements of Tamil Nadu Slum Clearance Board (TNSCB) and
each rehabilitated encroacher was given a flat costing ` 8 lakh free of cost.
1.1.5 In addition, a large number of encroachments (by people living in below poverty line) have been
identified for removal and the families are being convinced to shift to tenements constructed by Government
of Tamil Nadu through Tamil Nadu Slum Clearance Board. In spite of the best efforts of the State
2

3
Government, the time consuming process of rehabilitation of evicted families is resulting in delays in
removal of encroachments. However, it was also mentioned that the Hon'ble high court of Madras is
directly monitoring the progress of encroachment removal and rehabilitation of the evicted families.
1.1.6 The Government of Tamil Nadu always emphasizes the need for removal of encroachments and
protection of water bodies and it may not be out of place to place on record that Government of Tamil
Nadu has enacted Tanks Protection Act, 2007 and Tamil Nadu Land Encroachment Act, 1905 is being
followed for removal of encroachments from rivers and channels.
1.1.7 During the year 2016, a major drive was launched for desilting 22,899 tanks, 11,446 km. length
of river courses and canals, 14,112 encroachments were removed from water bodies. 6,960 recharge
pits were created and 8,657 defunct bore wells were converted as recharge wells. A special drive was
launched to clear the blockages under and on either side of the culverts and bridges and total blockages
under 15,870 bridges and 1,41,633 culverts were removed. 500 meters upstream & downstream bridges/
culverts were also desilted in several areas.
Recommendation
1.1.8 The Committee is given to understand that unplanned urbanisation and growth of cities are also
the main contributing factors for floods in and around Chennai. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Centre should come out with a proper long-term master plan for metro cities to prevent such
disasters in future. The committee is also of the opinion that it is an eye opener and other metro cities
must also learn from it. (Para 7.2.5 ibid)
Action Taken
1.1.9 The concern of the Committee has been communicated to the Ministry of Urban Development and
Ministry of Housing & Urban Poverty Alleviation in the matter. Accordingly, they have initiated aforesaid
(Sl. No. 7.2.4) actions in the matter.
1.2 ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF DIFFERENT CONCERNED AGENCIES
Recommendation
1.2.1 The Committee also observes that the NDMA plays a very crucial role in mitigating problems of
disaster victims. Therefore, its vacant posts should be filled up on priority. The Committee also recommends
that after any disaster in future, the NDMA should meet urgently. (Para 8.7 ibid)
Action Taken
1.2.2 As per Disaster Management Act, 2005, the National Authority shall consist of the Chairperson and
such number of other Members, not exceeding nine as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
Presently, four Members are working in NDMA. One Member has been vested with administrative/
financial powers, necessary to run the Authority. The Members have been meeting very frequently.
However, observation/ concern of the Committee have been noted.

4
Recommendation
1.2.3 The Committee is of the considered view that there should be an emphasis on pre-disaster preparedness
in disaster management set up of the State as the same would minimize the loss of lives and property
in the situation of any unforeseen eventuality. Had this mechanism of prevention and mitigation been
in place in the State to the required extent, the loss of lives and property could have been minimized.
(Para 8.11 ibid)
Action Taken
1.2.4 There is well established institutional mechanism at National, State and District level in the country
to develop appropriate prevention, preparedness and mitigation measures in disaster situation.
1.2.5 Disaster Management is multi-disciplinary subject, which require coordinated and holistic approach
from all Ministries/ Departments of Central and State level. The DM Act envisage that every Ministry/
Department of Central and State Governments shall make provisions, in its annual budget and take all
necessary measures for prevention, mitigation, response and capacity building for disaster management
and allocate sufficient funds for carrying out the such long/ medium term works activities.
1.2.6 However, Government of India has accepted the 14th Finance Commission recommendation to
devolve 42% of the divisible pool to States during 2015-16 to 2019-20. Earlier it was 32%. Accordingly,
all the Centrally Sponsored Schemes have now been subsumed into State Funds. Accordingly, State
Governments are required to undertake all necessary measures for prevention, mitigation of long/ medium
term works activities and allocate sufficient funds for carrying out such activities as per their State
specific requirement and magnitude of ground situation.
1.2.7 The Government of Tamil Nadu informed that they are taking elaborate preparative measures to
face North East Monsoon every year and because of the extensive preparedness arrangements made by
the State during September-October 2015 large scale evacuation was possible during flood of December,
2015 and large number of relief centers were arranged for the evacuated people from the affected area
which resulted in minimizing the loss of lives.
1.2.8 In all, lakhs of people were rescued, evacuated or moved to safer places throughout state and
accommodated in 7069 relief camps. Not only food and drinking water, but also basic amenities were
ensured to the people accommodated in relief centers.
1.2.9 In order to preserve public health and prevent outbreak of epidemic diseases, State Government
had spread bleaching powder and other disinfectants in the streets and half a kilo bleaching powder were
provided to each household. Double the usual dosage of chlorination has been done. Diseases surveillance
has been done by the dedicated teams, round the clock during calamity period.
1.2.10 Accordingly, State Government has stated that they had taken aforesaid major initiatives through
Public health department and awareness generation among the general public in the aftermath of December,
2015 floods, the outbreak of epidemics in the flood affected area were completely prevented.

5
High Priority for preparedness during NEM 2016
1.2.11 The Government of Tamil Nadu has also informed that they always accord high priority to
preparedness in disaster management and taking into account the lessons learned from the floods of
2015, a massive exercise was initiated from the month of September, 2016 to face the North East
Monsoon which is associated with floods on the one hand due to cyclonic storms, excessive downpour,
cloudburst and drought on the other in case of failure of monsoon. The key measures adopted for
disaster preparedness to face North East Monsoon 2016 are detailed below:
1. Identification of vulnerable areas, mapping and analysis of vulnerability.  The identified
areas were classified into
(i) Areas of Very High vulnerability 7- 572 (Above 5 feet)
(ii) Areas of High vulnerability- 804 (3 to 5 feet)
(iii) Areas of Moderate vulnerability- 1145 (2 to 3 feet)
(iv) Areas of Low vulnerab ility- 1671 (below 2 feet)
Vulnerability maps were prepared at the rate of 3 vulnerable areas in each map at Firk (Rural
areas)/ Ward (Urban areas) level incorporating vulnerability analysis, details of escape routes
and relief centers in the map itself.
2. Unification of efforts of multi sectoral items at field level: Constitution of 498 Inter
Departmental Zonal Teams led by Revenue Authority. The team members are drawn from
Policy, Fire Services, Rural Development and Agriculture Departments etc. Each team is to
closely monitor 5 to 7 vulnerable areas.
3. Community participation: Community participation at grass root level through enrolment
of 11,479 able bodied volunteers, with skills of swimming and climbing, as First Responders
(10 per vulnerable area) 1499 First Responder Teams were formed in very highly and highly
vulnerable areas. The first responders were trained by Fire services/SDRF and Red Cross
Society. Mobile teams of first responders and Snake catchers were also formed at Block/
Taluk/Sub-Divisional and District levels for deployment based on need.
4. Prepositioning: Prepositioning of rescue teams and relief materials in the vulnerable areas
to ensure rescue and relief operations.
5. Strengthening of SDRF and coordination between Central and State agencies: State
Disaster Response Force was strengthened by training 1275 police personnel from Special
Forces (70 to 80 in each coastal district) increasing the SDRF strength from about 100
during the previous years. Coordination between Central and State Agencies as well as
unified action by multiple agencies of Government of Tamil Nadu was given top priority.

6
Arrangements were made for establishing green corridors to facilitate quick movement of
rescue teams and relief materials.
6. Involvement of multiple stakeholders: To sensitize the Private Institutions, series of
meetings were held at District/ State level with Hospital/ Educational organizations/
Communication Service providers and Oil Companies to develop institutional level strategies
and to ensure round the clock functioning of emergency services.
7. Communication through multiple channels: Usage of multiple channels such as print/
electronic/social media/wireless systems to spread awareness among the community on the
Do's and Don'ts during disasters. Multiple mock exercises were organized on different days
including on International Disaster Reduction day.
8. Preparedness to manage flood through de-siltation & eviction of encroachments and
removal of blockages under bridges and culverts was accorded high priority: A major
drive was launched for de-silting 22,899 tanks, 11,446 Km. of river courses and canals.
14,112 encroachments were removed from water bodies. 6960 recharge pits were created
and 8657 defunct bore wells were converted as recharge wells. A special drive was launched
to clear the blockages on either side of the culverts and bridges and total blockages under
15,870 bridges and 1,41,633 culverts were removed. 500 meters upstream and downstream
of bridges/ culverts were also desilted in several areas.
1.2.12 In view of the aforesaid measures taken/initiated by the State Government it is expected to improve
the existing disaster management practices including the preparedness and minimizing the loss of lives
and property in the situation of any unforeseen eventuality in the State. The efforts of the State
Government in facing North East Monsoon 2016 based on the lessons learnt in the previous year resulted
in deft handling of the very severe Cyclone Vardah. However, the strengthening of the disaster management
including pre-disaster preparedness is a continuing process of the governance.
1.3 RELIEF & REHABILITATION EFFORTS AND MEASURES
Recommendation
1.3.1 The Committee emphasizes that disaster management requires coordinated and holistic approach
from all Ministries, Departments of Central as well as State level. The Committee notes that the Central
Government extended support to the Government of Tamil Nadu by providing timely support to supplement
the efforts of the State Government for tackling the situation effectively in the wake of flood situation
in Chennai during 2015. But at the same time, the Committee observes that the NDMA meetings should
take place immediately to monitor the situation depending upon the gravity of the disaster, since they
only play the most crucial role in coordinating multiple agencies belonging to the Centre and the State
who are involved in mitigating the disaster. The Committee however, appreciates the work done by the
state Government as well as Chennai Corporation, in terms of relief and rehabilitation works.
(Para 10.2.3 ibid)

7
Action Taken
1.3.2 Obs ervation of the Committee is noted by NDMA. However, it is informed that Members of
National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) meet regularly for coordinating multiple agencies of
Central and State those are involved in mitigating the disaster situation in the country.
1.4 FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE
Recommendation
1.4.1 The Committee notes that there is significant gap between the demand for financial assistance
made by the State and the actual help extended to them by the Centre. In this context, the Committee
takes note of the statement of the representative of the Ministry of Finance while deposing before the
Committee which is as follow:
"The State Government normally gives the Memorandum that includes damages, infrastructure and
long-term mitigation also. The assistance normally from the Government under the NDRF is for
the short-term repair and relief only. We only supplement the short-term measures because it is a
supplementary approach. Normally, there is a gap between the demand of the State Government
and the actual assistance. There is an Inter-Ministerial Committee which gives its comments on
the report and then this Executive Committee and the high level Committee see to it that it is as
per the set norms. The norms have been set by the Government as to which are the items that are
admissible for relief from the NDRF. So, normally, this difference takes place. But, in this case,
for Tamil Nadu, still that document has not been examined." (Para 11.7 ibid)
Action Taken
1.4.2 In this case, it is stated that the High Level Committee (HLC), in its meetings held on 15th
February, 2016 approved the assistance of `1737.65 crore from NDRF, subject to adjustment of 50%
of balance available in the SDRF account of the State for the instant disaster.
1.4.3 It is stated that the Government of India had released the 1st installments of Central Share of State
Disaster Response Fund amounting to ` 254.625 crore for the year 2015-16, to the State on 27th May,
2015. Further, in order to support the affected people of the State, the Government of India had released
assistance of `388.42 crore ( ` 133.795 cr. + ` 254.625 crore) from SDRF and ` 552.00 crore from
Special Assistance of central plan schemes to Tamil Nadu on 23rd November, 2015. Besides, an amount
of `1000 crore ( ` 866.31 cr. + ` 133.69 cr.) released, 'on account' basis from NDRF to the State
Government on 3rd December, 2015 and 16th December, 2015 respectively. As such, Government of
India has released ` 2195.045 crore from SDRF/ NDRF and Special Assistance to Tamil Nadu for
management of relief necessitated by natural disasters during 2015-16.
Recommendation
1.4.5 However, the Committee recommends that in view of the extraordinary circumstances and the huge
damage caused to the State, particularly to the Chennai city, necessary assistance may be provided

8
without further delay. The Committee feels that huge damage has occurred to the road infrastructure and
restoration thereof is a gigantic task. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that adequate grant should
be given to the State for this purpose. (Para 11.8 ibid)
Action Taken
1.4.6 Observation is noted and communicated to Ministry of Urban Development and Ministry of Road
Transport. In this context, it is mentioned that Section 49 and Section 39 of DM Act, 2005, envisage
to every Ministries or Department of the Government of India and State Governments that it shall make
provision, in its annual budget, for funds for the purpose of carrying out the activities and programs set

coordinated and holistic approach from all Ministries/ Departments of Central as well as State level.
However, the Government of India will continue to extend all possible support to the State Government

CHAPTER - II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS ON WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE
TO PURSUE THE MATTER IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT'S REPLY
2.1 ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF DIFFERENT CONCERNED AGENCIES
Recommendation
2.1.1 In the opinion of the Committee, any natural disaster of bigger intensity has the propensity to
cause extensive damage. Thus, instead of putting the blame on the forces of nature, we should use
advanced technology to fight it out. Moreover, the administration of both Centre and State should work
together and remain vigilant to tackle the situation. The Committee also observes that natural disaster
of high magnitude will always adversely affect people in large number and the administration has to
respond in a fastest possible manner. Accordingly, the NDMA and all concerned bodies of Central and
State Governments should have established procedures so that vital time is not lost in wriggling out
procedural delays. (Para 8.6 of 198th Report)
Action Taken
2.1.2 There are institutional mechanisms at the National and State level for effective management of
natural disasters. There have been significant improvements in the overall system and procedures in Tamil
Nadu. In order to strengthen the existing disaster management system, the Disaster Management Act,
2005 was enacted and notified on December 26, 2005. The Act provides for institutional mechanisms
for drawing up and monitoring the implementation of the disaster management plans, which includes
holistic, coordinated, and prompt response to any calamity situation in the country and ensures measures
by various wings of government for prevention, mitigation and for minimizing the effects of calamities.
Further, the strengthening of the disaster management is a continuing process of the governance.
2.1.3 NDMA has issued guidelines for management of floods in 2008 and for management of Urban
Flooding in 2010. Implementation of the same is required to be done by the State Government. NDMA
has also issued detailed advisories to all the State Governments for taking necessary timely measures
during the monsoon season. 10-point advisory has been issued for immediate attention on urban flood
preparedness and mitigation. Formulation of roadmap strategies for medium term and long term mitigation
measures is under process.
2.1.4 The Government of Tamil Nadu has informed that they have well established procedures for
effective co-ordination and preparedness to face the events during North East Monsoon. TNSDMA have
close co-ordination with NDMA in the event of disasters. However, events of December, 2015 should
be analyzed taking into account the unprecedented down pour of gigantic proportion which was unheard
in the history of Chennai city.
2.1.5 In spite of the mammoth task that was faced, Government of Tamil Nadu had acted with great
alacrity in implementing restoration measures and it was possible due to the established procedures
9

10
followed by the Government of Tamil Nadu in close co-ordination with Central agencies and Government
of India.
2.1.6 However, the State Government has stated that the 2015 experience did impart certain lessons for
being imbibed to face unprecedented disasters. Government of Tamil Nadu have identified the gaps and
strengthened its preparedness measures and co-ordination mechanism which resulted in deft handling of
the very severe cyclone Vardha during December, 2016.
Recommendation
2.1.7 The Committee impresses on the fact that scientists all over the world are now highlighting on
global warming and its consequences like, unusually high rain fall and sea cyclones. These would be
rather more common phenomena and happen frequently in coastal states then a rare instance. Therefore,
the Committee recommends the Ministry of Home Affairs and NDMA to keep their preparedness at
optimum level. (Para 8.9 ibid)
Action Taken
2.1.8 The concern of the Committee has been noted in the matter. In this context it is pertinent to state
that the primary responsibility for disaster management including preparedness rests with the States.
Appropriate institutional mechanisms in the form of National Disaster Management Authority, State
Disaster Management Authority and District Disaster Management Authority have been setup in the
country to develop appropriate preparedness and response mechanism in disaster situation. These setups
have also been networked with the early warning system and also with the National Emergency Operation
Centre for receiving and dissemination of alerts/ advisories/ information relating to the natural calamities.
As a part of institutional mechanism, this Ministry and NDMA coordinate with the State Government and
other stakeholders.
Recommendation
2.1.9 The Committee observes that there are multiple agencies involved in the disaster management
process and feels that despite the best efforts all these take lot of time and consequently the administration
fails to reach out to the victims. The Committee recommends that there should not be so many layers and
NDMA has to revamp the process in co-ordination with the Centre and the State. (Para 8.10 ibid)
Action Taken
2.1.10 Observation is noted. Since, Disaster management is multi-discipline subject, it requires coordinated
and holistic approach from all Ministries/ Departments of Central as well as State level. However, NDMA
is responsible for laying down guidelines for management of various types of disasters, natural as well
as manmade. Guidelines for management of Floods and Urban Flooding have been issued by NDMA in
the past. Efficient implementation of the same by coordinating the actions of all the agencies under them
is the responsibility of the State Government.
2.1.11 Further, the strengthening of the disaster management including revamping the process in coordination
with Center and the State is a continuing process of the governance.

2.2 EXTENT OF DAMAGE DUE TO FLOODING
Recommendation
2.2.1 The Committee understands that damage to social and physical infrastructure and financial loss
to individuals and micro and small industries due to unprecedented torrential downpour in Chennai and
other parts of Tamil Nadu if calculated properly, may run into thousands of crores. The Committee,
therefore, urges upon the Central Government to look sympathetically into the needs of the State
Government in terms of reconstruction and rehabilitation and immediately announce a special relief and
rehabilitation package which is in consonance with the demands of the State. (Para 9.3 ibid)
Action Taken
2.2.2 The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises has informed that the relief package was
drafted in accordance with RBI master circular on natural calamities with reference to Micro, Small &
Medium Enterprises (MSME) Sector. The following relief package was endorsed in the 144th SLBC
meeting held on 18th December, 2015 at Chennai.
(i) Extending Moratorium period of two years.
(ii) Converting existing term loan and interest as converted term loan.
(iii) Rescheduling of term loan.
(iv) Extending fresh loan facilities.
